News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
Whatever his returns, there has been an extra focus to Brook’s approach this summer, possibly because he has learnt from a grievous indiscretion in Wellington last winter. While others chase the Indian Premier League, he is totally committed to England, taking his break while that tournament is on and playing every match in all formats for his country.

Brook had come to the crease at the fall of the first wicket and, while it is early days, England appear to have added another arrow to their quiver. They handed a debut to opener Aneurin Donald, with his cap presented in the pre-match huddle by Pietersen, the new “specialist mentor”.

Donald has been selected as an “intent merchant”, charged with going extremely hard from the first over, aping Phil Salt, who is missing with a quad injury. He did what he was asked to do, smearing his first ball for two, then pulling six to leg and hammering four through the offside before the first over was out. Another big shot, off Wellalage, in the second saw him well caught in the deep, but 12 off five had kickstarted the innings.

News.title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
News.content:
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

News.title: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Sports.title: Former England star James Milner returns to ex-club after calling time on career
Sports.content:
Next

JAMES MILNER has made a surprise return to Liverpool just months after calling time on his record-breaking Premier League career.

The former England star, 40, is back at Anfield on a temporary basis to help coach the club’s academy youngsters.



Milner finally hung up his boots this summer following an incredible 24 YEARS playing in the Premier League.

But the serial winner has wasted little time plotting the next chapter of his career.



Milner is currently working towards his Uefa Pro Licence as he looks to move into coaching.

And Liverpool academy director Alex Inglethorpe has invited the Reds legend back to Kirkby to gain valuable experience working with the club’s youngsters.

The arrangement is understood to be casual, with Milner assisting Liverpool’s existing coaches rather than taking charge of a particular age group.

He worked with the club’s Under-11s last weekend and is expected to spend time with different squads during his spell.

It marks a return to familiar surroundings for a player who enjoyed eight trophy-laden years on Merseyside.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Milner made 332 appearances in all competitions for Liverpool after joining from Manchester City on a free transfer in 2015.



He became one of Jurgen Klopp‘s most trusted lieutenants and served as vice-captain during one of the most successful periods in the club’s recent history.

Milner helped Liverpool win the Champions League in 2019 before finally ending the club’s 30-year wait for a league title the following season.

He also lifted the FA Cup, League Cup, Community Shield, Uefa Super Cup and Fifa Club World Cup during his time with the Reds.

Milner left Liverpool for Brighton in 2023 and spent the final three seasons of his playing career on the South Coast.

His extraordinary career also included spells with Leeds, Newcastle, Aston Villa and Manchester City.



And Milner bowed out having rewritten the Premier League record books.

He made his 658th top-flight appearance in February to become the competition’s all-time appearance holder.

His final Premier League outing fittingly came against Manchester United in May.



Milner’s move into coaching will come as little surprise to those who worked with him during his playing days.

He previously spent time helping out at Liverpool’s academy while still playing for the first team.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler also gave the veteran opportunities to gain coaching experience during his spell with the Seagulls.

Liverpool have regularly opened the doors of their academy to former players looking to earn their coaching qualifications.

Ex-Reds defender Conor Coady has also been working with the U21s alongside head coach Rob Page.

Former Liverpool academy defender Tom Clayton, meanwhile, was recently appointed assistant manager of the U16s.

And now Milner is back at Kirkby as he takes his first steps towards a potential career in the dugout.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr drawn into Real Madrid political storm after refusing to wear pre-match T-shirt
Sports.content:
Next

KYLIAN MBAPPE, Vinicius Jr and former Liverpool defender Ibrahima Konate have been drawn into a political storm after a pre-match T-shirt snub.

All the players in Real Madrid’s LaLiga game at Elche on Tuesday night were asked to wear T-shirts supporting the people of Ceuta.



The Spanish enclave on the North African coast has been the centre of violence after some 80,000 migrants crossed the border from Morocco in July.

Under a LaLiga initiative, the majority of clubs had worn the T-shirts bearing the slogan “Todos somos caballas” – “we are all mackerels”, the nickname for inhabitants of the city – although Barcelona had not taken part.



But while all the Elche players and eight of the Madrid starters wore the clothing before the kick-off – Real won 3-2 with a stoppage-time goal from Carlos Espi – the trio staged their own protest when they were handed the tops in the tunnel.

Vini Jr, Mbappe and Konate all wore their shirts rolled down to only half-way, obscuring the message.

That saw a backlash with some politicians accusing the Madrid players of showing contempt for Spain.

Jose Maria Figaredo, spokesperson for the populist Vox party, said: “These three players are perfectly free to do and defend whatever causes they want.

“But the Spanish people are also perfectly free to feel outraged by three millionaires who live in Spain and then don’t support the Spanish people.”

Ester Munoz of the opposition People’s Party – currently leading election polls – said she believed the trio had failed to “defend Spain”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

She added: “I believe it’s a humanitarian issue and they will have to explain why. To be honest, I felt quite embarrassed for them.”

The issues saw members of the socialist government talking of “personal decisions” and that “sport is sport and the values of sport must never be lost” and accusing opposition voices of “twisting” the situation.



While the left-wing Sumar party said: “Helping Ceuta cannot be used to divide based on national identity sensitivities or even to incite racism.”

Real backed the players despite the furore, with sources insisting that while Madrid agreed to Elche’s request for them to wear the shirts in solidarity, the club “respects individual opinions” and gave players the freedom to decide if they would participate.

Sports.title: Ex-Everton boss Ronald Koeman announces death of wife Bartina, 65, after cancer battle
Sports.content:
Ex-Everton boss Ronald Koeman announces death of wife Bartina, 65, after cancer battle

Ronald Koeman has opened up on the passing of his wife, who died earlier this week at the age of 65 having battled cancer with players past and present offering their condolences

View 2 Images Ronald Koeman's wife has died at the age of 65 (Image: Jam Press/@bartinakoeman)

Ronald Koeman has announced the death of his wife, Bartina Koeman-Boddeveld, who has died at the age of 65 after a lengthy battle with cancer.

‌



The Netherlands legend has received multiple messages of condolence after revealing the news on his Instagram. The couple had been married for 41 years and have three children together. Koeman shared a photo of him and his wife and confirmed she died on Tuesday.

‌



Koeman's social media post said: "With intense sadness, but also with great pride and love, we say goodbye to my beautiful wife, our dearest mom and grandma. Bartina Koeman-Boddeveld. January 30 - September 15 2026. Familie Koeman"

‌



Koeman had his wife alongside him throughout his legendary football career. The defender was one of the best players of his generation and scored the winning goal in the 1992 European Cup final, which saw Barcelona beat Sampdoria.

‌



After hanging up his boots the Dutchman went into management and recently had been in charge of his national side, but stepped down this summer after their World Cup exit, making it clear that his wife's circumstances had given him a new perspective.

He said: "The past years have made me realise again that there are more important things than football. Football has been my life, but health is priceless.

"When someone you love is fighting a tough battle, your perspective changes. My wife Bartina has supported and encouraged me every day to finish my work as a national coach, despite her own illness process. That is a testimony to incredible strength. I appreciate her more than I’ll ever be able to put into words."

‌



View 2 Images When Ronald Koeman stepped down from his latest job he cited his wife's health as changing his outlook on life (Image: Jam Press/@bartinakoeman)

A host of compatriots have sent well wishes to Koeman as he deals with the personal tragedy. Dutch internationals Wesley Sneijder and Luuk de Jong among those to send messages, as has Ryan Gravenberch's partner, Cindy Peroti.

Koeman never played in England but his managerial career took him to the likes of Spain, Portugal and England. His two jobs in England saw him lead Southampton and Everton. Whilst at St Mary's he led the Saints to seventh and sixth place finishes, securing Europa League football.

Sports.title: Premier League panel unanimously agree on Arsenal red card controversy in final verdict
Sports.content:
Premier League panel unanimously agree on Arsenal red card controversy in final verdict

The Premier League Key Match Incidents panel have unanimously agreed on what the outcome of Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes' kick on Emi Martinez should have been

View 2 Images Gabriel Magalhaes kicked Emi Martinez (Image: Sky Sports)

The Premier League Key Match Incidents panel have unanimously backed Chris Kavanagh and his Video Assistant Referee team's decision not to dismiss Gabriel Magalhaes during Arsenal's encounter with Chelsea. The north London side came away 2-1 victors against the Blues earlier this month, but the match was not without its share of controversy.

‌



Arsenal saw Riccardo Calafiori's strike chalked off for offside, while Kai Havertz's leveller was permitted to stand despite a marginal offside call. Both rulings also received unanimous 5:0 backing from the panel.

‌



But Gabriel's challenge on Emi Martinez may have been the most divisive moment of the match. With Chelsea still leading through Morgan Rogers' strike, Martinez attempted to gather a low free kick from Martin Odegaard. Scrambling for the ball, Gabriel caught the Chelsea goalkeeper in the face when he aimed a kick at the ball.

‌



The ball subsequently slipped from the Argentine's grasp, but no punishment was forthcoming despite protests from Reece James and Joao Pedro. Martinez clutched his head and received treatment but was able to continue.

VAR chose not to send Kavanagh to the monitor to review the situation, and ultimately the KMI panel have decided that was the right call. The panel is made up of three former players or coaches, one representative from the Premier League, and one from Pro Ref (Professional Game Referees).

‌



They also released the following statement: "The panel unanimously supported the referee's call of no red card. Multiple players were on the ground competing and challenging for the loose ball, and the action of Gabriel was not deemed to be an act of violent conduct or serious foul play."

While that group was unanimous in their backing of Kavanagh, the outcome may come as a surprise to Wayne Rooney. Speaking on Match of the Day, Rooney claimed Gabriel was 'extremely lucky' not to receive his marching orders.

View 2 Images The panel did not believe that Gabriel deserved a red card (Image: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

Ashley Young, also on the show, concurred. "I'm exactly the same way," Young said.

Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho already in Aston Villa desperation with 'easy' £43m transfer conditions

Alejandro Garnacho is looking to kickstart his Aston Villa career after joining on loan from Chelsea and the former Man Utd winger already faces a potentially vital moment

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first Aston Villa start (Image: Jon Super/Shutterstock)

Alejandro Garnacho will be desperate for a start in the Carabao Cup when Aston Villa face Coventry City at the CBS Arena on Wednesday night (8pm). The winger arrived from Chelsea on loan with a conditional obligation to buy, believed to be tied to his appearance tally.

‌



So far, though, Garnacho has managed just 31 minutes across three Premier League outings, with teenager George Hemmings keeping him out of the XI. Unai Emery has nonetheless stressed that he has been encouraged by the Argentine's development since joining the club.

‌



"Every training session we are doing, he is showing he can play matches," Emery said. "He played a few minutes, but it was not enough, firstly due to the minutes he played and the things he showed.

‌



"Progressively, I am seeing him better. The most important thing is being consistent and demanding through the attitude he has. Then, I believe and I trust that he will achieve his best performance progressively."

Sports.title: Inside Max Dowman's rise as Arsenal prodigy gives Mikel Arteta taste of the future
Sports.content:
Max Dowman is intent on breaking records with every appearance.

This time, Dowman became only the second 16-year-old to score a brace for a Premier League side since Wayne Rooney in 2002. His double for Arsenal in the Carabao Cup tie at Ipswich showcased his prodigious talent which has got the potential to take him to the very top for club and country.

Dowman is already the youngest scorer and title winner in Premier League history. The youngest player to appear in a Champions League knock-out match.

But, actually, this is nothing new for the Arsenal wonderkid who has been exceeding expectations since he was first spotted at the tender age of just four. Dowman, whose family live in Essex, was running round six year olds at a village pitch in Kelvedon Hatch and, even then, it was obvious that his super power was running with the ball.

‌



He stood out a mile because of his dribbling ability, his lovely left foot and the way that, even at the young age, he struck the ball. It was exquisite.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Premier League clubs cannot bring kids in until they are five and they do so with the ultimate aim of then signing them at the first opportunity when they turn nine years old. And even when he started going in to Arsenal on a regular basis, he was dazzling academy coaches who could not believe he was just five. He shone even against older kids who - don’t forget - were pretty good themselves if they were at Arsenal.

‌



The likes of West Ham, Chelsea and Tottenham all wanted Dowman but Arsenal had the trump card. His family are all Arsenal fans. When Chelsea were sniffing round him a while back, his dad Rob took to social media to say: “Arsenal are our club.”

Arsenal’s academy is producing a rich vein of kids - Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Marli Salmon - and it is regarded as world class when it comes to developing and nurturing young talent.

Other clubs may be better at the business side of academy - producing kids and selling them on - but Arsenal’s recent success rate speaks for itself when it comes to outstanding youngsters.

View 3 Images Dowman scored twice in Arsenal's win over Ipswich Town (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Every kid needs a huge degree of luck to make it. One injury can completely derail them. They also need a strong support network behind them. You only have to look at Jude and Jobe Bellingham to understand the value of family. Not just one kid to make it a top European club. But two. That is a tribute to their upbringing and their values.

It is the same with Dowman. People at Arsenal talk glowingly about his dad Rob - who is a hugely successful businessman in his own right - and mum Caroline plus his whole family. They are right behind him - but in the right, supportive way.

When Dowman signed professional terns for Arsenal, his dad posted a picture of the scout who discovered him and said: “Proud day for us. Nothing would have been possible without this guy. Thank you Johnny Knight.”

Knight is a hugely respected scout, a top guy who knows youth football inside out and never seeks the limelight. But some families get carried away and forget how it started. The Dowmans didn’t.

‌



The Dowmans keep Max grounded. He is good-looking, smart (he was still at school while training and playing for Arsenal), clearly a brilliant footballer and Adidas flew him out to New York during the World Cup. He has starred in an advert already.

View 3 Images Dowman helped Arsenal win the Premier League last term (Image: Getty Images)

But even amid the post-match scramble outside grounds, he makes sure he signs autographs and his family are known for being friendly, generous and down-to-earth among the hardcore of Arsenal fans who travel home and away. No wonder Arsenal fans love Max already.

His double at Ipswich - particularly his first - showed his talent. Running with the ball, dribble, switch of feet and a stunning finish. His wonder goal against Everton, breaking from his own half to score, was one of the best moments of last season.

‌



That was also the moment he announced himself to the wider football world. A few days later, Thomas Tuchel - announcing his next England squad last March - was being asked about whether he had a chance of going to the World Cup.

It was too soon. But you can bet he will not have to wait much longer. Now the question for Mikel Arteta is how does he get him in the Arsenal team? You cannot hold him back much longer - even with so much talent in the Arsenal squad.

His best position really is in the middle as a No10. That is Arsenal’s future. But he can play deeper, wide right coming in on his left foot and on the other flank. Even the best start wide and come inside.

Dowman is destined for the very top. And he is being guided there in the best possible way.

‌

Sports.title: Referee backed over Man Utd VAR decision as Premier League release official verdict
Sports.content:
Referee backed over Man Utd VAR decision as Premier League release official verdict

Manchester United were at the centre of VAR controversy on Sunday after Erling Haaland's controversial goal for Man City and now the Premier League have had their say on another incident

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha was at the heart of the decision at Everton (Image: Getty Images)

The Premier League have confirmed that referee John Brooks and VAR officials were correct not to award Manchester United a penalty at Everton on September 6th. Brazilian forward Matheus Cunha looked to have been brought down in the Toffees box during the 2-2 draw.

‌



Cameroon international Bryan Mbeumo broke the deadlock for Michael Carrick's men shortly after the interval, curling a precise low effort from the edge of the area. United then believed they had an opportunity to double their advantage from the spot, when Cunha appeared to be felled from behind by defender James Tarkowski.

‌



Having collected the ball in Everton's half, England winger Marcus Rashford surged forward into Jordan Pickford's area, leaving both Tarkowski and centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite in his wake with some slick footwork before rolling it back to Cunha on the edge of the six-yard box.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

As the forward shaped to find the net, a last-gasp challenge from Tarkowski dispossessed him, sparking furious appeals for a penalty from United's players on the pitch and their travelling supporters in the stands.

Although VAR briefly reviewed the incident, replays demonstrated that Tarkowski had won the ball cleanly before Branthwaite cleared the danger.

‌



The Premier League have since confirmed that their panel of refereeing experts unanimously upheld the decision to wave away the penalty appeals.

They said: "The referee's call of no penalty was supported as Tarkowski clearly and fairly won the ball through Cunha's legs."

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha was tackled by James Tarkowski against Everton (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



The incident occurred just a week before the contentious decision to allow Erling Haaland's goal to stand in United's 1-0 Manchester derby defeat the following Sunday.

The on-field ruling initially flagged him offside, though it was subsequently argued that the Norwegian was actually in an onside position, with Patrick Dorgu's outstretched leg playing him on.

Despite this, officials overlooked the fact that Enzo Fernandez — who was positioned offside — had interfered with play, meaning the goal should never have been given.

Article continues below

Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref has since conceded an "error of judgment" on the part of the VAR officials, with United receiving a formal apology.

Sports.title: Swansea ball boy Eden Hazard kicked, now 31, makes £300m after huge US sale
Sports.content:
Swansea ball boy Eden Hazard kicked, now 31, makes £300m after huge US sale

The ball boy, who was then 17, shot to fame after his infamous clash with Eden Hazard during Swansea's League Cup tie against Chelsea in 2013

View 2 Images Chris Morgan made the headlines after Eden Hazard lashed out at him

A Swansea ball boy once kicked by Eden Hazard has gone on to make an astonishing fortune, with reports suggesting he has earned around £300million from selling his vodka empire. Charlie Morgan was just 17 when he became the centre of global attention during Chelsea's 2013 League Cup clash with Swansea City, after Hazard lashed out while trying to retrieve the ball Morgan was shielding.

‌



The Belgian was sent off, the clip went viral, and Morgan's name suddenly travelled far beyond South Wales. Hazard later said he apologised to Morgan, explaining: "The ball boy came in the changing room and we had a quick chat. I apologised and the boy apologised as well, and it is over. Sorry."

‌



Now 31, Morgan has built one of the world's most recognisable premium vodka brands. He co‑founded Au Vodka with business partner Jackson Quinn in Swansea in 2015, and the company has since exploded in popularity - known for its gold bottles, celebrity endorsements from the likes of Floyd Mayweather and Ronaldinho, and rapid expansion following investment from DJ Charlie Sloth.

‌

The brand has now been acquired by US drinks giant Sazerac, with Reuters reporting the deal is worth approximately £300m, though the exact financial terms remain undisclosed. Au Vodka had previously been valued at around £150m, and Morgan and Quinn were estimated to have personal net worths of roughly £75m each.

More than 80 people are now employed in South Wales as Au Vodka continues to scale, and Sazerac chief executive Jake Wenz has been full of praise for the brand, calling it one the company has long admired.

‌



"Au Vodka is a brand we've long admired," he said. "What Charlie, Jackson, and Charlie have achieved in just over a decade is spectacular and rare, and we have big plans for Au as we welcome the brand into the Sazerac family."

He said the takeover would bolster Sazerac's presence in the UK while giving Au Vodka 'a path for continued global growth.'

Morgan and Quinn have often reflected on their early days, saying they launched the business with 'nothing but an idea and a belief that vodka didn’t have to be boring.'

"We are proud to have built it into one of the most disruptive brands of this generation," he said. "With Sazerac, Au can be offered to more people, in more markets, faster than we ever could alone."

Au Vodka now sits alongside more than 500 drinks in Sazerac's portfolio, which includes brands such as BuzzBallz and Southern Comfort.

Sports.title: WTA reveals new Finals host from 2027 with aim of 'Super Bowl for women's sports'
Sports.content:
The WTA Finals will be staged in Charlotte, North Carolina in the United States from 2027.

As part of the WTA's desire "to build the preeminent championship experience in women's sport", the tour's showpiece season-ending event for the top eight singles players and doubles teams will be staged at Spectrum Center, the home of the NBA's Charlotte Hornets, in 2027-2029.

This year's WTA Finals are taking place in Indian Wells, California in November after the controversial deal to stage the event in Saudi Arabia ended a year early.

"Our ambition is for the WTA Finals to be not only the premier championship in women's tennis, but one of the defining global events in women's sports," said WTA chair Valerie Camillo said.

"We want to create the Super Bowl for women's sports. And not just the competition, but an event that is the annual gathering for women's tennis, women's sports, and women's sport business.

"Audiences are growing, investment is growing, female athletes are increasingly at the center of sports and culture around the world.

"And women's tennis has helped lead and define that progress for more than 50 years. And we believe our biggest championship should reflect the scale of this moment."

Since being held for five consecutive years in Singapore in 2014-2018, the WTA Finals have been staged at six different venues including this year's at Indian Wells.

"The WTA has always owned the WTA finals, but now going forward, we're going to operate it too," Camillo added.

"We're taking control of the creation of the revenues and the controlling of the expenses and the delivery of the entire thing. And that allows us to control our own destiny."

The WTA is also relocating its global headquarters to Charlotte.

"This is a transformational moment for Charlotte and for our organization," said Will Pitts, CEO of the Charlotte Sports Foundation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the 2025 WTA Finals between Elena Rybakina and top seed Aryna Sabalenka

"Bringing the WTA Finals to our city is a testament to what Charlotte has become as a world-class sports destination, and we are incredibly grateful to the WTA for their trust and partnership in making this vision a reality.

"None of this happens without the support of our partners at the state, city, and county levels, and we are deeply thankful for their commitment to growing Charlotte's sports footprint."

Sports.title: Why Monaco's hosting a Sprint - F1's 2027 calendar changes explained
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s 2027 calendar is out with next season again scheduled to run to a record-equalling 24 race weekends.

But the schedule features a number of points of intrigue including an increase in Sprints, headlined by the addition of Monaco, the continued presence of the sport's usual Middle Eastern rounds, and the return of two popular tracks...

Four more Sprints

As reported in July, Formula 1 is increasing the number of Sprint weekends on the calendar for 2027.

The final number of Sprints has been confirmed as 10, four more than the six which have featured in each of the past four seasons.

The alternative format, which was first introduced in 2021 and features an additional qualifying session to set the grid for a short-form 100km race, has led to increase in global television audiences, which F1 says are 12 per cent higher than on non-Sprint weekends which feature three practice sessions.

The Sprint weekend schedule Friday

Practice

Sprint Qualifying



Saturday

Sprint

Grand Prix Qualifying



Sunday

Grand Prix

The 10 venues for 2027 are split evenly between tracks that have staged Sprints previously - Montreal, Silverstone, Monza, Interlagos and Qatar's Lusail - and newcomers to the format in Sakhir, Albert Park, Suzuka, Monaco and Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina Circuit.

The current Sprint format, which features points for the top-eight finishers, is thought set to remain the same for 2027.

2027 Formula 1 - Race Calendar 1 Bahrain* March 12-14 13 Hungary July 30-Aug 1 2 Saudi Arabia March 19-21 14 Italy* September 3-5 3 Australia* April 2-4 15 Spain September 10-12 4 Japan* April 9-11 16 Azerbaijan September 24-26 5 China April 16-18 17 Turkey October 1-3 6 Miami Apr 30-May 2 18 Singapore October 8-10 7 Canada* May 21-23 19 USA October 22-24 8 Monaco* June 4-6 20 Mexico October 29-31 9 Portugal June 18-20 21 Brazil* November 5-7 10 Great Britain* July 2-4 22 Las Vegas November 19-21 11 Austria July 9-11 23 Qatar* December 3-5 12 Belgium July 23-25 24 Abu Dhabi* December 10-12

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater takes a look at the big talking points from the 2027 F1 season calendar, including a Sprint taking place in Monaco for the first time

Why Monaco is staging a first-ever Sprint

Certainly, many of the early headlines and debate around the 2027 calendar has centred on the fact Monaco has unexpectedly been included as one the 10 Sprint venues.

Not only has the Principality never hosted a Sprint before, its main 78-lap Grand Prix is already not known for overtaking around its narrow, twisty wall-lined circuit with the race often proving processional in dry conditions.

It is regularly Qualifying - and the flat-out challenge of threading an F1 car between the barriers - that proves the most jaw-dropping aspect of the Monaco weekend. F1 has pointed out that the addition of the Sprint means there will now be two such grid-setting sessions in 2027

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix

It can also be argued that having only one practice session, rather than the usual three, offers the chance for more unpredictability in the pecking order given drivers will only have one practice session to build rhythm and confidence, a crucial element of a successful Monaco weekend.

"Traditionally Sprints have been held at tracks where it is easy to overtake. Clearly that's not the case at Monaco," said Sky Sports' Craig Slater.

"But the big bonus here we'll have two red-hot qualifying sessions. That's what that track is all about and the drivers will have the ultimate test on two occasions that weekend."

Season start and ending Sprint weekends

For the first time next year, the season will both start and finish with a Sprint event.

Bahrain opens the season with the format on March 12-14 while Abu Dhabi will close it on December 10-12.

The season-opening Sprint will certainly present a different challenge for teams and drivers given they will have just one practice session that weekend to prepare for the campaign's first competitive session, Sprint Qualifying, on the Friday evening.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 British Grand Prix Sprint race

However, pre-season testing at the same Sakhir circuit (February 24-27) will run to four rather than three days - one more day than is usually the case outside of years featuring big rule changes - meaning they will at least be familiar with the track with the new 2027 cars.

Still, the season-opening Sprint represents a new challenge and could offer some early-season surprises in the pecking order for one, or both, grids if teams are not on top of their cars and set-ups.

The fact that the season will finish with back-to-back Sprint events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi inevitably raises the possibility of the world title being decided in a Saturday race should the fight go down to the final rounds.

There is already precedent for this from Qatar 2023 when Max Verstappen clinched his third world title in the Sprint.

Middle East races scheduled as F1 waits on final 2026 decisions

The sport's four Middle Eastern races all feature on the 2027 season, bookending the 24-race campaign.

That also remains the case for 2026's final two scheduled races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi with just over two months to go until the sport is due to head there.

Image: Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina circuit is due to close the current season on December 6

The conflict in the Middle East has already seen this year's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix cancelled and the Bahrain Grand Prix moved to Malaysia on October 4, having originally been scheduled for April at its own Sakhir track a week before Jeddah.

F1's intention and planning remains for 2026's concluding two rounds to go ahead as scheduled. Although Stefano Domenicali had previously indicated that there was a mid-September timeframe on making a final decision on whether the events could take place, there is thought to be no hard deadline as such with officials able to wait for longer before making a final call.

Italy's Imola circuit is understood to be the contingency to close the current season in December should the Middle Eastern rounds not be able to take place.

The early-season 2027 dates in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia are not scheduled for another five months, giving F1 and the FIA plenty of time to continue monitoring the latest situation.

Portugal and Turkey return

Formula 1's calendar first increased to a record 24 grands prix in 2024 and that number is again scheduled for next year.

Next year's calendar features no absolutely-new venues, but the sport will return to Portugal and Turkey for the first time since the popular European venues were called up to help out during the Covid-affected 2020 and 2021 seasons.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Turkish Grand Prix is back! Watch drivers go flat out on Istanbul Park's iconic turn 8

They replace the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, which starts a rotation with the Belgian GP and next returns in 2028, and Dutch Grand Prix, whose deal has ended.

Portugal's Portimao circuit takes over Barcelona's June slot, while Turkey returns at the start of October as part of a slightly rejigged run of races after F1's summer break, which will stretch to five weeks in 2027.

The season will finish on December 12, one week later than this year and the joint-latest since 2020.

Sports.title: World Grand Prix schedule confirmed as Littler looks to defend title
Sports.content:
The World Grand Prix takes place at Leicester's Mattioli Arena, beginning on September 28, live on Sky Sports.

The event uniquely requires players to begin and finish every leg on a double or the bullseye.

The 32-player field features the top 16 players on the PDC Werner Rankings Ladder and the top 16 players from the ProTour Rankings yet to have qualified, as they bid to claim double-start glory.

Defending champion Luke Littler will headline the competition in Leicester, which will see the sport's top players battle for a newly-boosted £150,000 top prize and the coveted title.

2023 champion Luke Humphries will also be hunting a second World Grand Prix title, while Dutch number one Gian van Veen returns to the arena where he broke the record average last year in defeat to Littler.

Sports.title: F1 announce 2027 calendar and increase in Sprint rounds
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has announced its 2027 calendar and an increase in the number of Sprint weekends from six to 10, with the season starting in Bahrain.

For a fourth consecutive year, there are 24 rounds scheduled with Portugal's Portimao and Turkey's Istanbul Park returning to the calendar.

As expected, the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort falls off the schedule while the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya moves into a rotational deal with Spa-Francorchamps that will see the Spanish event held in even numbered years from 2028 and the Belgian Grand Prix held in odd numbered years from 2027.

2027 Formula 1 - Race Calendar 1 Bahrain* March 12-14 13 Hungary July 30-Aug 1 2 Saudi Arabia March 19-21 14 Italy* September 3-5 3 Australia* April 2-4 15 Spain September 10-12 4 Japan* April 9-11 16 Azerbaijan September 24-26 5 China April 16-18 17 Turkey October 1-3 6 Miami Apr 30-May 2 18 Singapore October 8-10 7 Canada* May 21-23 19 USA October 22-24 8 Monaco* June 4-6 20 Mexico October 29-31 9 Portugal June 18-20 21 Brazil* November 5-7 10 Great Britain* July 2-4 22 Las Vegas November 19-21 11 Austria July 9-11 23 Qatar* December 3-5 12 Belgium July 23-25 24 Abu Dhabi* December 10-12

*denotes Sprint weekend

F1 had delayed its calendar announcement for next year due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has created uncertainty over the end of the current season with Qatar and Abu Dhabi still currently scheduled to take place later this year.

Bahrain will host a four-day pre-season test on February 24-27 before holding the 2027 season-opener on March 12-14 and it will be a Sprint weekend, with the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix a week later.

Australia reverts to the third round of the season in early April and will also host a Sprint, as will the next race in Japan before China rounds off a triple-header.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and George Russell tussle for the lead of the 2026 Chinese GP Sprint

Miami retains its slot in the first weekend of May before Sprint rounds in Canada and, for the first time, Monaco, with F1 highlighting fans are "set to enjoy two thrilling qualifying sessions" around the streets of Monte Carlo.

The returning Portuguese Grand Prix slots into mid-June and is followed by a Sprint weekend at the British Grand Prix on July 2-4, with Austria moving to after Silverstone.

Back-to-back weekends in Belgium and Hungary will take the F1 circus to the summer break.

F1 2027 Calendar and Sprint announcement - key points Portuguese and Turkish Grands Prix return to calendar for first time since 2021

Season-opener returns to Bahrain for first time since 2024 and it will be a Sprint weekend

Number of Sprint weekends increased from six to 10

British Grand Prix is on July 2-4

Summer break is five weeks long, rather than four

Season to conclude in Abu Dhabi on December 10-12

A sprint round at Monza in early September will be the first event back after five weeks off, a week longer than usual, with the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid a week later.

Azerbaijan, Turkey and Singapore form part of a triple-header before the usual Americas triple-header in Austin, Mexico and Brazil, which is a Sprint weekend.

Las Vegas will host the only Saturday race of 2027, although it will be Sunday morning in the UK, then two Sprint weekends in Qatar and Abu Dhabi on December 10-12 conclude the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Look back at some of the most dramatic moments to have taken place at the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix

"The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," said F1 president Stefano Domenicali.

"We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Turkey to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to 10 events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special.

"Formula 1 continues to go from strength-to-strength, attracting new audiences around the globe. Week after week, the world's greatest drivers will battle on some of the most challenging tracks in motorsport, supported by F1's outstanding teams, world-class manufacturers, and global partners. Together, they create a spectacle unlike anything else in sport. As we continue this remarkable journey of growth, I want to thank our fans around the world as their passion drives everything we do."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch back to the 2020 Turkish Grand Prix where Lewis Hamilton claimed his seventh world title in a chaotic rain-hit race

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem added: "The 2027 FIA Formula One World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport.

"With 24 Grands Prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Turkey, and the opportunity for an expanded Sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation, and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

Sports.title: Football Daily | Madrid endure an awkward night after T-shirt trouble and Elche scare
Sports.content:
REAL UNEASE

Anxious to sample some traditional Spanish culture while taking in a La Liga match years ago, Football Daily and some friends decamped to Gran Alicant. As we prepared to leave a quaint bodega (the Dick Turpin), where we’d been sampling the local hooch (Guinness), to travel to the nearby stadium, an elderly local resident with an unmistakable mackem accent informed us that the Elche home game to which we were heading was not being played until the following evening. It had fallen victim to Spanish TV’s infuriating habit of rescheduling random top-flight matches with little or no notice or consideration for Johnny-come-latelys who might have travelled from afar to watch them. We never did get to see Elche play in the flesh but did get to watch the current La Liga basement-dwellers give José Mourinho an almighty fright on TV on Tuesday night, as they went this close to snatching a point from Real Madrid.

Allowed to spend 14 times more on players and coaching staff than their hosts at the Estadio Martínez Valero under La Liga rules, it was no surprise to see Real Madrid go 2-0 up as they appeared to be cruising towards a routine rout of their lowly opposition. However, a succession of missed chances (hello, Vinícius Júnior) followed by second-half sucker punches from Abiel Osorio and Fer Niño meant Mourinho was sweating as Elche approached the final seven minutes on the front foot, looking for an unlikely winner. Sadly, there was no fairytale and Carlos Espí popped up with a late, late winner to break Elche hearts and dig his side out of one of several holes they have already found themselves in this season. While a balmy Tuesday night in Elche may not be the most glamorous of environments, not for the first, second, third, fourth or even 534th time in their history, Madrid found a way.

“Three points and nothing more,” harrumphed Mourinho in his post-match interview. “The problem seems obvious to me. It’s harder to know why but it’s easier to understand that there are matches that seem over but in the end, aren’t. Matches where we have three, four, five chances to finish them but don’t. After failing to do so, it feels like we go from ease to losing control. With the changes I made in the end, I took all the risks. We won but I could have lost.” Modest to a T, as ever, Mourinho will be hoping for a better performance from his team when they make the short trip to the Wanda Metropolitano to face their city rivals Atlético on Sunday (or Saturday, depending on the whims of broadcasters) before the international break.

While the out-of-sorts Vinícius Jr did little on Tuesday night beyond convince Arsenal fans they may have dodged a very expensive summer bullet, he was one of three Madrid stars who refused to show off T-shirts showing solidarity with the people of Ceuta that were handed to both sets of players as they made their way out on to the pitch before kick-off. Along with Kylian Mbappé and Ibrahima Konaté, Vinícius Jr chose not to show the slogan “Todos somos caballas” (“We are all mackerels”), in support of the Spanish exclave which was overwhelmed by the arrival of 80,000 migrants, mostly from Morocco, in recent months. Subsequently lambasted in some quarters for being too supportive of the migrants and not supportive enough of the citizens of Ceuta, it was an awkward situation where the Madrid players were put on the spot and simply couldn’t do right for doing wrong.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Niall McVeigh at 8pm (BST) for a red-hot Bigger Vase clockwatch, while Will Unwin will be on deck at the same time for Rumblews Cup goal updates.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, ‘I regret that I didn’t eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever’. That was the feeling. That was the moment” – as part of the FA’s forthcoming feature ‘Reflections: England’s World Cup Journey’, Thomas Tuchel was recently interviewed by Daniel Sturridge about the aftermath of England’s famous 3-2 win over Mexico at the Azteca, and made a bizarre admission about his eating habits while showing an alarming misunderstanding of the body’s digestive system.

View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel failed to mention what he was chewing during that second half with Argentina. Photograph: Ricardo Mazalán/AP

double quotation mark I almost wish I was a West Ham fan. As an eternally suffering Spurs supporter, I find myself looking enviously towards the London Stadium these days. The Hammers are top of the table, banging in goal after goal (already 20 more than Spurs’ tally in the league). They score even when they lose and seem to have bought a proper No 9. My Spurs, meanwhile, continue the tradition of the last two years in style, sitting comfortably in 17th with 1,047 wingers on contract, and getting knocked out of one of the competitions they could ‘conceivably’ have won, the only competition they seem to be able to score goals in as well. In hindsight, West Ham made the right choice to go down. Hammers fans, you are welcome!” – Yannick Woudstra (and no others).

double quotation mark Hugh Fordham’s idea [Tuesday’s Football Daily letters] has some merit. But it reminded me of a pithy comment by Bill Nicholson. ‘Do you think he was interfering with play?’, he was asked. Nicholson responded: “If he’s not interfering with play, what’s he doing on the pitch?!’” – Harry McDonald.

double quotation mark In support of Hugh Fordham’s suggestion, I remember discussing the idea of interfering with play while on a training course for referees back in the 1960s. We were told that unless someone was ‘lying injured near the corner flag’ any player should be treated as being involved in play. Not a lot of room for subjectivity in those days. And obviously no thought of stopping play for the hypothetical injured player!” – Trevor Field.

Sports.title: Maresca says Manchester City still waiting for apology after incorrect 2023 derby goal
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has said Manchester United cannot complain about the controversial derby winner on Sunday because Manchester City are still awaiting an apology from the referees’ chief, Howard Webb, for a match-defining decision in the same fixture three years ago. City lost at Old Trafford in 2023 after Bruno Fernandes equalised despite an offside Marcus Rashford running close to the through ball from which his teammate scored.

Maresca was Pep Guardiola’s assistant at the time and had to witness Rashford’s winner a few minutes later. “The goal was not a regular goal, if you remember,” Maresca said. “And to be honest, no one apologised. We are still waiting for the apology for that goal. Sometimes it happens for you, sometimes it happens against you. It’s football.”

City host Norwich on Thursday in the Carabao Cup, a competition which provides Maresca with the first opportunity to win a trophy at the club. Guardiola won it on a record five occasions.

Phil Foden will not be involved after being sent off against United for kicking out at Fernandes, earning a three-match ban. “At half-time, he was very sad, very upset because he knew there was something wrong,” Maresca said. “Then after the game he was a little bit more relieved, he was a little bit more happy. And then yesterday he was very good. He knows the reaction was not a good one, but again, it’s finished and we move on.”

Maresca, who worked as head coach of City’s under-21s and had five graduates to the first team, could offer opportunities to youngsters as well as fringe players. The teenagers Ryan McAidoo, Kaden Braithwaite and Floyd Samba, son of the former Blackburn defender Chris, will be in the squad, having spent the season with the first-team group.

“When we started pre-season we had many young players and then at the end we decided to keep just these three players,” Maresca said. “They can work with us every day, they can improve, and at some point they can also get a chance to get some minutes.”
