Sports.title: Wrexham announce landmark milestone in £70m Racecourse Ground redevelopment
Sports.content:
Wrexham have completed the latest phase of their Racecourse Ground redevelopment project.

The Red Dragons are in the process of building a new 7,750-capacity Kop Stand.



3 Wrexham have completed the latest phase of their Racecourse Ground redevelopment Credit: Getty

Construction on the stand began in December, with the club hoping it will be completed ahead of the start of next season.

Their plans remain on course after the steelwork for the stand was completed.

Wrexham stadium milestone

Wrexham have announced the 125-tonne inverted ribbon truss has been successfully installed as part of the new stand's construction.



It has been described as 'one of the most technically complex’ engineering operations of the project.

Speaking to the club's media channels, Wrexham CEO Michael Williamson explained: "The successful lift and installation of the steel truss is a landmark moment for the club, not only in the construction of the new Kop Stand itself but also for the wider Gateway Project.



"We are now looking forward to seeing the Kop Stand continue to evolve and take shape over the coming months."

The construction of the new Kop Stand will restore the Racecourse Ground to a four-sided stadium.



It will also take the venue's total capacity over 18,000 and comply with UEFA category four requirements.

Reaching category four status would allow Wales to play home European Championship qualifiers and Nations League matches at the Racecourse Ground.

Wrexham at the Racecourse Ground

The venue was first built in 1807, but has been used for football since Wrexham began playing matches there in 1864.

3 Wrexham hope to complete the construction of the new Kop Stand ahead of next season Credit: Getty



At present, the Racecourse Ground has a capacity of 10,771 supporters.

However, that figure is set to reach over 18,500 once the new Kop Stand is completed.

The old stand was closed in 2008 due to concerns over fan safety.

It was subsequently demolished in 2023, leaving the ground with just three stands.

As a result, the stadium is the smallest by capacity in the Championship this season.



Wrexham are currently in their second successive season in the second tier.

3 Wrexham's ground will hold over 18,500 fans once the new stand is completed Credit: Shutterstock

Following three promotions in a row from the National League to the Championship, the club finished seventh last season.

Phil Parkinson's side currently sit 19th after seven matches this term following a 6-0 defeat to West Ham United last weekend.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon warned teammate ready to take his place as Barcelona tipped to win LaLiga ‘by a mile’
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon warned teammate ready to take his place as Barcelona tipped to win LaLiga ‘by a mile’

Andy Brassell believes Anthony Gordon cannot afford to rest on his laurels, even if Barcelona 'really needed him'.

Gordon joined from Newcastle before the World Cup and has quickly taken to life at Barcelona, registering five assists from his first six appearances.

3 Gordon has essentially replaced Marcus Rashford as Barcelona's left-winger Credit: Getty

But it's not just Gordon's attacking contributions that have made him so vital to Barca's early season success.

Anthony Gordon has been what Barca needed

"It's just the work he gets through off the ball," European football expert Brassell said on Monday's Hawksbee and Jacobs.

"He's ideal for them. They've really needed him because they weren't able to get Julian Alvarez, so they've been playing Raphinha as a centre-forward.

"Who knew, he's (Raphinha) absolutely brilliant at it."

Raphinha, who moved to Barcelona from Leeds in July 2022, has netted eight times in all competitions this season.

Previously a left-winger, the Brazilian's shift to centre-forward has proved transformative.

However, talkSPORT understands Raphinha is not seen as a long-term solution up front, with Harry Kane and Erling Haaland viewed as alternative targets should Barcelona fail to land Alvarez.

Which Barcelona teammate should Anthony Gordon be concerned about?

That could spell trouble for Gordon, who could be nudged down the pecking order if Raphinha is moved back to the left-wing.

But Raphinha isn't the only teammate Gordon has to worry about being usurped by.

"He's got good competition to keep him honest," Brassell said.

3 Raphinha has now scored over 80 goals for Barca since he moved from Leeds Credit: Getty

"Karim Adeyemi came on for him and scored the clinching goal near the end."

Like Gordon, Adeyemi moved to Barcelona in the summer.

However, Adeyemi, who joined from Borussia Dortmund, has started just twice for the Catalan outfit this term.

The 24-year-old started Barcelona's LaLiga opener where he got on the scoresheet in a 5-0 rout of Elche.

But since then, Adeyemi has been reduced to cameos ranging from 28 minutes to 10.

Even if Adeyemi is reduced to being Gordon's back-up on the left, at least for now, it still leaves Barcelona with a strong attacking option to call on when needed.

3 Adeyemi's goal against Levante was Barcelona's 21st from five LaLiga fixtures Credit: Getty

Brassell: Barcelona may be scoring for fun, but they won't win Champions League

And Brassell believes that spells bad news for the rest of the competition, as he claimed Barcelona will 'end up winning LaLiga by an absolute mile.'

Brassell's belief is backed up by Barcelona's blistering goalscoring rate, with Hansi Flick's side netting 26 goals in just six games across all competitions this term.

Should Barcelona maintain that rate and play 57 games, which was how many they played last season, they are on track to score an absurd 247 goals.

However, he's not-so-certain about their Champions League aspirations and pointed to their defence that has shown a worrying tendency to be too casual as the potential reason why.

"Defending like they are defending at the moment, they will not win the Champions League, I don't think," Brassell said.

"They're competitive, they can play anyone off the park, there's no doubt about that. They can score goals galore.

"Can they keep it out against top level opposition? That's the question."

Sports.title: England fans to be allowed in for behind closed doors clash with Croatia in UEFA climbdown
Sports.content:
England fans to be allowed in for behind closed doors clash with Croatia in UEFA climbdown

England have confirmed 100 fans will be permitted to watch their Nations League clash against Croatia in Rijeka.

The contest was originally set to be played behind closed doors, with UEFA handing down the punishment due to crowd issues during Croatia's Nations League quarter-final against France in March 2025.



3 A small portion of England fans will have to try and provide the noise against Croatia Credit: Getty

Along with the two-match crowd ban, UEFA fined Croatia a total of €93,000 (£79,000) and ordered them to cover the cost of repairs after their visiting fans caused damage to the Stade de France during the return leg.

England release statement confirming limited attendance for Croatia clash

However, following lobbying from FA chiefs, UEFA have softened their stance.

"We’re pleased to confirm that, following discussions with UEFA, a small delegation of England Supporters Travel Club members will be permitted to attend England’s UEFA Nations League fixture against Croatia on Saturday 3 October," an England statement read.



"It was announced shortly after confirmation of this fixture that the match will be played behind closed doors, but we have secured an allocation of 100 complimentary tickets for active 2026-2028 England Supporters Travel Club members."

Which fans are eligible to attend England's Nations League game against Croatia?

The statement added that the only eligible fans who can register are active 2026-2028 England Supporters Travel Club members and they can register for themselves only.



Tickets will be allocated based on all-time caps, with active caps used to separate those who have the same all-time caps total.

Eligible members have until 12pm on Friday to register.

The upcoming Nations League clash between England and Croatia is not the first time they have played each other behind closed doors.



England's last visit to Croatia, back in 2018, was contested with no fans present due to fan violence.

Along with the England fixture on October 3, Croatia are banned from having fans attend their clash against Czechia on September 26.

3 This year's World Cup was the first time England and Croatia faced off since June 2021 Credit: Getty

Croatia will hope to exact revenge on England in the upcoming fixture after Thomas Tuchel's side prevailed 4-2 in their World Cup group opener.



The two sides both netted twice in the opening half before goals from Jude Bellingham and Marcus Rashford got England's World Cup campaign off to a winning start.

Both nations qualified for the knockout stage, but Croatia's run ended shortly afterwards as they were beaten 2-1 by Portugal in the round of 32.

As for England, they went on to finish third, the nation's best finish since winning the World Cup in 1966.

The Three Lions' trip to Croatia is one of four fixtures they will play in the upcoming international break.



When do England play in the upcoming international break?

Tuchel's side will face Spain in their first game following the World Cup, with the clash to take place at Wembley on September 26.

3 Tuchel's long-term focus has now switched to Euro 2028, which will be played on home soil Credit: Getty

The Three Lions then travel to Czechia three days later on September 29.

England then face Croatia on October 3 before rounding out the international break at Wembley against Czechia on October 6.



talkSPORT will have live commentary of all four matches.

Sports.title: When will Man United’s £2bn new stadium open? Latest news amid ‘opening date’ reports
Sports.content:
When will Man United’s £2bn new stadium open? Latest news amid ‘opening date’ reports

Manchester United remain hopeful their new stadium will open before the 2035 Women's World Cup despite reports of a setback.

United unveiled plans for a 100,000 venue last year dubbed the 'Wembley of the North'.



3 An expected opening date for United's new stadium has been reported Credit: PA

The renovation of their current Old Trafford stadium would cost £2billion.

Whilst initial plans from INEOS outlined hopes to secure public funding for the project, that has since been ruled out.

Instead, the club confirmed in Match that private funding will be sourced for Sir Jim Ratcliffe's planned stadium.



Stadium development CEO Collette Roche had said it was hope the new stadium would open its doors for the 2032/33 season.

United stadium opening date

City AM reported on Wednesday that the ground could take 10 years to build without any delays.



The report claims to have seen official documentation outlining 2035 as the current opening date of the stadium.

If delayed, it would put United's hopes of hosting the 2035 Women's World Cup final in doubt.



However, talkSPORT understands the Red Devils still intend to open the stadium before the event.

The Red Devils have publicly outlined their desire to be chosen ahead of Wembley Stadium for the showpiece clash.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will co-host the tournament in nine years' time.

3 Ratcliffe and United hope the stadium will be open in time to host the 2035 Women's World Cup final Credit: PA



Old Trafford has been listed as one of 22 proposed venues for the event, provided the new stadium is not delayed.

United stadium latest

It was revealed in June that the club had cleared a major hurdle in the project.

United have now secured the majority of land required to build the new stadium.

Meanwhile, an official site was confirmed the following month.

The new stadium will be located 350 metres north west of the current Old Trafford.



United have played their home matches at the 74,158-capacity ground since it opened in 1910.

3 United's proposed new stadium is currently set to open before 2035 Credit: PA

However, Old Trafford has not been renovated since an expansion of 8,000 seats 20 years ago.

Sports.title: Eight Man United wonderkids left and only three became stars as JJ Gabriel seeks messy exit
Sports.content:
Eight Man United wonderkids left and only three became stars as JJ Gabriel seeks messy exit

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United - but what road will he go down? Will he flop or will he thrive?

Man United's academy is famed for its stories, with multiple club icons coming through the ranks to achieve greatness.



9 Gabriel has asked to leave Man United in a decision that caught the club by surprise Credit: Getty

Ryan Giggs, Paul Scholes, David Beckham, Gary Neville, Mark Hughes, Nicky Butt and many more rose to the top at United.

In more recent years, Marcus Rashford is a prime example of a teenage sensation-turned-senior star, despite his blip.

It has always been part of the Red Devils' DNA - seeing homegrown talent burst into the first team and thrive at Old Trafford.



But rather than going down the route of some of the club's legends, Gabriel has forced their hand, and they may now end up losing one of the world's highest-rated young prospects.

It was revealed on Tuesday that the 15-year-old wanted to leave and have his registration with the academy cancelled.



He has Real Madrid, Barcelona, Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City and Bayern Munich among the huge teams interested.

However, as much as Man United have seen success come from their academy, history shows that not all wonderkids shine.



So what will it be for Gabriel?

Well, his incredible stats and performances for United's youth teams, including a debut hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League last week, hint that he really is destined for greatness.

But high potential at a young age doesn't always lead to bigger things, as these few players know all too well...

9 Should Gabriel leave United, he will hope his career thrives rather than flops Credit: Getty

Man United's wonderkids who struggled

Febian Brandy

After joining Man United at the age of nine, Febian Brandy went on to become one of the highest-rated youngsters in England.



Brandy, a forward, was looked at by Real Madrid and Barcelona - just like Gabriel - as he starred in competitions like the FA Youth Cup and Champions Youth Cup in 2007.

But he never played a senior game for United and would end up leaving the club in 2010, beginning a journeyman career.

Injuries hampered his progress and he ended up playing for 16 clubs, retiring from football after a few years in non-league.

His most appearances for a team after departing Old Trafford were 34 games for Walsall in the 2012/13 campaign.



9 Brandy had similar suitors to Gabriel as a youngster but his career never took off Credit: Getty

Ravel Morrison

A name that a large majority of fans will relate to the failed wonderkid tag is Ravel Morrison, who Sir Alex Ferguson once labelled 'the best he had ever seen'.

Signing for Man United in 2009 as a scholar, Morrison looked destined for the top and Ferguson clearly thought so.

However, that sadly wasn't the case, as troubles off the pitch and a lack of discipline meant he didn't live up to his potential.



He left Man United in 2012 and has since played for 14 clubs, including stints at West Ham, Lazio, Derby and DC United.

Morrison is a prime example of 'what could've been'.

9 Morrison was tipped for big things as he came through at Man United Credit: Getty

Federico Macheda

In April 2009, 17-year-old Federico Macheda announced himself at Old Trafford, scoring an iconic debut goal against Aston Villa.

His last-minute turn, strike and celebration are famous - but sadly for him, that has remained his career highlight ever since, as he only scored another three goals for the club altogether.



After spending seven years at Man United in the academy and first-team, he left in 2014 following six separate loan spells.

Macheda joined Cardiff City and then also played for Nottingham Forest, Italian side Novara and Greek giants Panathinaikos, where he did find some success, playing over 100 games.

At 35-years-old, he is still playing in Greece with Asteras Aktor.

9 Macheda scored an iconic goal as a teenager but he failed to build on it Credit: Getty - Contributor

Mads Timm

At the turn of the century, a highly rated Mads Timm joined Man United's academy and went on to sign a professional deal.



Striker Timm won the FA Youth Cup with the academy and made his first-team debut in the Champions League in 2002, but that ended up being his only senior appearance.

The Danish youth international was sent on two loan spells in Norway before joining Walsall and playing 12 games in 2006.

However, that move came before Timm received a 12-month sentence in a young offenders institute for reckless driving following an incident with a teammate which ended in a crash.

That ended his career at United as he was released, but he was given a second chance in Denmark before retiring aged just 24.



9 Timm's career fell down due to issues off the pitch rather than on it Credit: Getty

Isak Hansen-Aaroen

A more recent addition to this list is Isak Hansen-Aaroen, who was once considered a wonderkid at Man United.

Hansen-Aaroen joined the Red Devils' academy in 2020 aged 16, arriving as a very highly rated talent from Tromso.

He went on to play 30 games for the U18s and 50 games for the U21s, but he never made it into the first team, which angered him.



The young midfielder, who departed in 2024 to join Werder Bremen in search of senior football, admitted that he 'felt ready' for the men's game, and he wasn't happy with the lack of openings, which appears to be a similar stance to Gabriel's.

Hansen-Aaroen only played four first-team games for Werder Bremen though, recently leaving to join Dutch side NEC.

9 Hansen-Aaroen believed he was ready for first-team football, so he left United Credit: Getty

Man United's wonderkids who left and became stars

Paul Pogba

Now, moving on to the success stories of some Man United wonderkids, who Gabriel will hope to follow the path of, rather than those who haven't gone on to better things.



Paul Pogba became a superstar after leaving the Red Devils as a teenager amid frustration over first-team opportunities.

Aged 19, following talks with multiple clubs in the final year of his deal, he signed on a free for Juventus - and the rest is history.

The Frenchman won four straight Serie A titles and two Italian Cups, becoming one of the world's best midfielders.

United, of course, then ended up re-signing the man they let go for free for a world-record fee of £89million in 2016, two years before he went on to win the World Cup with France.



9 Pogba was let go for free by United and became one of the best in the world Credit: Getty

Gerard Pique

Barcelona icon Gerard Pique joined Man United's academy as a highly-rated defender aged 17 in 2004 and ended up playing 23 games for the club.

But he had to compete with Nemanja Vidic and Rio Ferdinand for a regular spot, leading to his departure just four years later.

He signed for Barca again in 2008 and became a club legend, winning a whopping 30 titles over the next 14 years.



Pique won three Champions Leagues and nine La Liga titles, becoming known as one of the world's best defenders.

The Spaniard also won the World Cup in 2010, with him going on to retire in 2023 as Barca's fifth-highest ever appearance maker.

9 Pique became a Barcelona icon after leaving Man United in 2008 Credit: AFP

Alvaro Carreras

At 17, defender Alvaro Carreras joined Man United from Real Madrid with the 'wonderkid' tag already on his back.



Carreras went on to spend two years in the Red Devils' academy, featuring regularly in the UEFA Youth League and FA Youth Cup.

But he never broke into the first team and failed to make a senior appearance before being sold to Benfica in 2024 following multiple loan spells, which included a year with Preston North End.

From there though, he has gone from strength to strength, with the Spaniard re-joining Real Madrid last summer.

He has since played 45 times for Real, becoming a regular starter and scoring under Jose Mourinho already this season.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told to stop Matheus Cunha experiment as ideal Man United front three named
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick told to stop Matheus Cunha experiment as ideal Man United front three named

Michael Carrick has been urged to start Benjamin Sesko and move Matheus Cunha back on the wing.

That's the view of talkSPORT's Angelina Kelly after Manchester United were beaten 1-0 in the Manchester derby

3 Cunha has been the assumed striker after Amad Diallo and Sesko were sidelined Credit: Getty

Slovenia international Sesko made his return to the starting XI in the Champions League clash against Sabah following a spell on the sidelines.

The 23-year-old worked his way back to fitness following a shin injury and scored in the 4-0 victory.

The forward is yet to start in the Premier League this season, scoring once off the bench against Everton.

Meanwhile, Cunha has primarily led the line for new permanent United boss Carrick.

The Brazil international started up front for the Red Devils in Sunday's Manchester derby defeat, with Bruno Fernandes operating behind him while Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford were on the wings.

However, Carrick's side appeared largely blunt in attacking areas in the 1-0 defeat by rivals Manchester City, despite playing against ten men for almost 70 minutes.

On talkSPORT's Inside Devils, Kelly suggested: "I think Carrick should have reacted to the red card and brought Sesko on sooner. He should have been starting, if I’m completely honest, but the Cunha experiment is not working.

"Sesko was the only person who was going to test Gianluigi Donnarumma."

Attacking woes at Old Trafford

While Manchester United's defensive frailties have been widely highlighted this term, an underperforming front line is creating equal concern.

Cunha has struggled to make an impact as a central focal point in the Premier League as the false nine with only one assist in four games.

Meanwhile, Marcus Rashford has fitted into Cunha's position on the left following his loan spell at Barcelona.

He has failed to record a single goal or assist this season.

Fellow Inside Devils pundit, Ryon Scott-Douglas, later added: "I would much rather favour last season's front three than Rashford being part of it. He has looked bright at points, I want to see the final product.

3 Despite not scoring so far this season, Rashford has created nine chances Credit: Getty

"He’s such a radical change, I don’t think he’s the problem. I’m looking at the current situation and we’re not scoring much and we were last season.

"I’m favouring Cunha starting over Rashford every time, the front three need to be Cunha, Sesko, and Mbeumo."

A proven formula

Kelly responded: "Troy Deeney said on talkSPORT’s All Access that Rashford is a bit all for himself.

"I’m not here to criticise him, but in my personal opinion it’s more likely that Rashford will still be departing Man United rather than staying for the next five years so we need to be playing the team that’s going to be there next season.

"He should play when he’s playing well, but when Sesko is fit he should start. Cunha, Sesko, and Mbeumo is what we live off."

During the 2025/26 season, United’s revamped front three consisted of summer arrivals Mbeumo, Sesko, and Cunha.

3 The return of Sesko has been a huge boost for Carrick, but he needs to use him more Credit: Getty

Under Carrick, the trio combined for an impressive goal tally across all competitions.

All three players hit double digits in the league alone as both Mbeumo and the Slovenia international finished the season as the club's joint-top goalscorers with 12 goals each in all competitions.

Cunha secured his tenth on the penultimate weekend against Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Stranded LIV Golfers left in the cold by PGA Tour as commissioner takes robust stance on their lucrative return
Sports.content:
The PGA Tour is not going to lower its drawbridge to the stranded golfers of LIV any time soon.

If the likes of Jon Rahm were hoping for a sweetheart deal in the style of one taken by Brooks Koepka earlier this year, he will have been left disappointed by the robust stance taken by the tour commissioner Brian Rolapp on Tuesday.

Unlike Koepka, who jumped ship in January, Rahm, Cameron Smith and Bryson DeChambeau all rejected the opportunity to return eight months ago and Rolapp has made it clear that will be no repeat of the offer in the wake of LIV filing for bankruptcy.

In outlining the PGA Tour's position, Rolapp said: 'In terms of where we are today, we are not currently contemplating a returning-member program like the one you saw in January. Everyone at the PGA Tour, myself included, has been focused on what is best for the organisation.'

Unless the word 'currently' serves as a precursor to a U-turn, it would seem that any LIV rebels will have a limited choice if they are to find a way back to the sport's prime tour.

Under the PGA Tour's existing rules, that would mean a minimum wait of 12 months since their last LIV start and most likely needing to qualify via the DP World Tour.

American star Bryson DeChambeau is among the LIV Golf stars pondering his next move

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp took a robust stance on defectors coming back to the main tour

Jon Rahm may have to wait a minimum of 12 months and qualify via the DP World Tour

As a member of the European-based circuit, Rahm is expected to take that option, with the understanding that LIV's bankruptcy will allow him to escape the remaining years of his contract on the breakaway league.

He is playing this week at the BMW Championship at Wentworth and indicated on Tuesday that it might be November before there is any clarity on his future.

'Nothing's changed,' he said. 'There's a long legal process they have to go through before a lot of things fall into place. I really can't give you an answer right now.

'Hopefully I'll play good this week, and at the end of the year, whether we play in Abu Dhabi, Dubai or elsewhere, so until this current season is done (in November), I really won't be able to give you an answer.'

LIV, whose chapter 11 filing was logged in court earlier this month, are currently pushing to launch a rebranded 2.0 version of the league for 2027, having secured a provisional agreement for $300m of backing from London-based BC Partners.

Sports.title: Max Verstappen to race 100 influencers TODAY: Red Bull star escapes Formula One struggles as David Coulthard insists former champion needs crazy challenge amid frustrating season
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen to race 100 influencers TODAY: Red Bull star escapes Formula One struggles as David Coulthard insists former champion needs crazy challenge amid frustrating season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

David Coulthard believes Max Verstappen needs challenges such as Wednesday's 'Max vs 100' karting race to keep his love of motorsport alive as the four-time Formula 1 world champion grows increasingly frustrated with the modern F1 car.

Verstappen will start at the back of a 101-kart field at Silverstone later today and attempt to overtake 100 rivals in a unique event broadcast live on Disney+.

And Coulthard, who raced against Verstappen's father Jos in Formula 1, believes the spectacle is about more than entertainment: it gives a driver whose passion for racing extends far beyond F1 an opportunity to simply race.

'Unquestionably,' Coulthard told me when asked whether Verstappen needs challenges like this to enjoy himself after growing frustrated this season.

'If you look at his year to date, he's been out testing a lot. His GT3, he raced at the Nurburgring 24 hours, was leading when the car failed. So that's an event where you have teammates and you share the responsibility of driving that car.

'In that respect, with no disrespect to the other Formula One drivers, Max is actually the most active and most passionate racer.'

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen is taking part in unique event 'Max vs 100' karting race on Wednesday

Former Red Bull driver David Coulthard believes the spectacle is about more than entertainment

That appetite has become increasingly significant during a difficult 2026 season for Verstappen.

Red Bull have fallen away from the front of the field under the current regulations, leaving Verstappen sixth in the championship after 14 rounds with 145 points.

Kimi Antonelli leads on 292, with Lewis Hamilton third on 191. Verstappen has taken three podiums in the last three Grands Prix, but has yet to win a race this season.

The Dutchman has also been open about his dissatisfaction with this generation of Formula 1 machinery.

Coulthard believes that criticism should not simply be dismissed as the frustration of a driver who is no longer winning every weekend.

'He doesn't like this particular generation of cars,' Coulthard said. 'I guess you could say, well, if he was winning, he would like it more, and of course that would be the case.

'But it doesn't take away from the fundamentals that he feels that with the hybrid era, it's taken away an element of the pleasure for him driving, and that may well be why we've seen him more actively going out and doing GT racing and other forms of racing, which isn't at all the norm for Formula One drivers.'

Verstappen's commitment to racing away from F1 was underlined by his Nurburgring 24 Hours appearance earlier this year.

He led the race in his Mercedes-AMG GT3 before his team was forced out by a driveshaft problem with just over three hours remaining.

Verstappen nevertheless said he had 'really enjoyed the experience' and would be open to similar events.

Verstappen is currently sixth in the championship standings with Kimi Antonelli (left) the comfortable leader

He has also remained active in esports, with Coulthard pointing to the fact that members of the public can race against Verstappen through his sim-racing operation.

And, Coulthard argues, the key point about Wednesday's event is simple: Verstappen would not be doing it if he did not want to.

'Whether it's his esports team, which is active and the general public can go and race against a four-time world champion in esports, or whether it's his GT racing, and then obviously this has been put together by Red Bull,' he said.

'But if he didn't want to do it, we wouldn't be having this conversation.'

The challenge itself is unlike anything Verstappen normally encounters. He will start behind 100 competitors drawn from the worlds of sport, gaming, social media and motorsport.

The pool of contestants includes ultrarunner Arda Saatci, basketball shooting specialist Chris 'Lethal Shooter' Matthews, freestyle mountain biker Matt Jones, streamers TheGrefg, Caedrel and TheDonato, and Daily Mail's very own sports presenter, Henry Williams. Coulthard expects Verstappen's instincts to take over.

'If it was a Monte Carlo-esque car track, it would be very, very difficult,' he said. 'But thankfully, Silverstone is a wider, wider circuit. They've lengthened the track, and therefore he will look to overtake quickly.

'He's a great racer. He will find spaces. If you try and block the inside, he'll go the outside.'

Coulthard suspects the field may ultimately need to work together to deny Verstappen.

'You almost need a couple of them to team up with each other to basically make it where the track is effectively blocked in front of him,' he said.

The Dutchman Verstappen will start at the back of a 101-kart field at Silverstone and attempt to overtake 100 rivals

'But I doubt very much that anyone's thinking about team strategy. They'll all be thinking about individual glory.

'This is an opportunity for an unknown person, other than their family and friends, to suddenly be the one that beat Max.'

The wider F1 backdrop could hardly be more different. While Verstappen is using the event as a return to his roots - having first karted at four years old, Hamilton's first season with Ferrari has become increasingly difficult from a championship perspective.

Hamilton is third in the standings on 191 points, 101 behind Antonelli after the Italian's eighth victory of the season in Madrid on Sunday.

Hamilton retired from the Spanish Grand Prix with a brake problem, while Antonelli beat Verstappen to another victory.

Coulthard believes Hamilton's mathematical hopes of an eighth world title are now extremely remote, even if Ferrari can make a significant step forward.

'I don't think, based on historical, you know, watching a Formula One, I don't think he's going to find the upgrade and be able to pull that points deficit back,' Coulthard said.

But he stressed the fundamental limitation facing any driver in F1.

'At the end of the day, our sport is, yes, the driver makes the difference, but you can only drive the car you're given.

Daily Mail sports presenter Henry Williams is taking part in the event which is broadcast on Disney+

'Ours is a technology sport, so it's really the team against the next team, and then the driver makes a difference. So right now he doesn't have the best package, but it's not far away.'

Hamilton's position is particularly intriguing given the man who replaced him at Mercedes.

Antonelli, only 20, has already won eight of the 14 races this season and leads team-mate George Russell by 81 points.

His Monza victory also made him the first Italian to win the Italian Grand Prix since 1966. Coulthard has been struck not only by Antonelli's speed but by his attitude.

'The guy has been phenomenal,' he said. 'And what's been really cool to see is how grounded and how approachable he is.'

Coulthard recalled interviewing Antonelli at Monza for Channel 4 and being given a hug afterwards.

'I think it just shows that kind of sincerity of how much he's enjoying this moment,' he said.

'So I think we should all enjoy it because, of course, he's not going to be 20 forever, and as the journey goes on, it demands and his time will increase, and he'll probably become a little bit more guarded.'

Coulthard believes Antonelli is already establishing himself as a defining figure of the next generation.

'He's well on his way to becoming the first Italian world champion since the 50s, I think it was,' he said. 'Even the Pope will know his name.'

*Max vs 100 is produced by Whisper, created by Red Bull and will be live on Disney+ and ESPN at 1700 BST on 16th Sept*

Sports.title: Man United flop Tyrell Malacia trains with MLS side: Defender, 27, undergoes trial with FC Cincinnati after Old Trafford nightmare as search for new club continues
Sports.content:
Man United flop Tyrell Malacia trains with MLS side: Defender, 27, undergoes trial with FC Cincinnati after Old Trafford nightmare as search for new club continues

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Manchester United defender Tyrell Malacia is training with MLS side FC Cincinnati as he seeks his next challenge after leaving Old Trafford.

Malacia's United nightmare finally came to an end in the summer when he was released by the club after four years.

The 27-year-old left-back is looking to relaunch his career after managing just 15 minutes of senior football in his final season at the Red Devils.

Malacia is currently on trial at FC Cincinnati, training with the first team until a decision is made on whether the US side will sign him permanently.

'FC Cincinnati has a good relationship with Malacia's agent; training with the team is an opportunity for both parties to see if they are a good fit,' the club have said.

Malacia's career in Manchester was blighted by a serious knee injury, which saw him miss 17 months of his Old Trafford career due to the problem.

Former Man United defender Tyrell Malacia is on trial with MLS side FC Cincinnati

The Dutchman joined United in a £13million switch from Feyenoord in 2022 and featured 50 times for the club in total.

11 of those appearances came across three years after his first season at the club, with Malacia undergoing two knee surgeries during that spell.

He endured a brief loan spell at PSV Eindhoven during 2025, where he managed 12 appearances.

Sports.title: 'Where's OUR apology?': Enzo Maresca claims Man City have waited THREE years for call from referees' boss Howard Webb as he hits back at Erling Haaland row
Sports.content:
'Where's OUR apology?': Enzo Maresca claims Man City have waited THREE years for call from referees' boss Howard Webb as he hits back at Erling Haaland row

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Maresca declared that Manchester City are still waiting on an apology from referees’ chief Howard Webb for a controversial derby goal in 2023.

The weekend victory at Old Trafford was enveloped by controversy, Pro Ref admitting a mistake by the VAR officials for awarding Erling Haaland’s 60th-minute goal despite Enzo Fernandez interfering with play in an offside position.

Webb was in contact with Manchester United in the immediate aftermath, with VAR Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus stood down for the coming week’s Premier League matches.

Maresca questioned why that process was different to the one City experienced when he was Pep Guardiola’s assistant in City’s Treble campaign.

Bruno Fernandes had equalised for United at Old Trafford in January 2023 despite Marcus Rashford seemingly interfering with play while stood offside. A discombobulated City then conceded another to Rashford minutes later.

Enzo Maresca questioned why that process was different to the one City experienced when he was Pep Guardiola’s assistant in City’s Treble campaign

Bruno Fernandes had equalised for United at Old Trafford in January 2023, despite Marcus Rashford seemingly interfering with play while stood offside

‘Sometimes it goes for you, sometimes it goes against you,’ Maresca said. ‘Three years ago when I was here, the same thing happened to us against Man United and we lost to them in the derby there.

‘The goal was not a regular goal if you remember. And no one apologises. We are still waiting for the apology for that. Sometimes it goes for and against.’

Maresca chose to shift focus on to City’s performance on Sunday, a result celebrated wildly in front of the away section, opening up an eight-point gap between the rivals after four games.

‘To talk about one moment after that game when we played for 70, 75 minutes with 10 players is quite poor,’ the Italian added. ‘I think the performance was unbelievable and I'm pleased.

‘It is not easy for the VAR and those in front of the screen who make a decision in 10-20 seconds. It is not easy for them. People make mistakes, I make mistakes, players make mistakes.

‘It is not easy to be in front of the screen and make a decision in 20 seconds, two minutes. It is complicated also for them.’

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr REFUSE to display t-shirts supporting Spain's sovereignty of Ceuta amid migrant crisis - with Real Madrid stars divided over message
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr REFUSE to display t-shirts supporting Spain's sovereignty of Ceuta amid migrant crisis - with Real Madrid stars divided over message

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A storm is brewing in Madrid after Real's two biggest stars, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr, concealed the club's message of Ceuta solidarity on pre-game t-shirts.

Far from putting on a united front on the issue, the pair, joined by Ibrahima Konate, deliberately rolled up their shirts to show their opposition to the club and league's stance.

The t-shirts displayed a 'We are all Caballas' slogan in support of the Ceuta community following the migration crisis in the Spanish North African enclave.

Earlier this summer, a state of emergency was declared when Spain faced a serious border crisis, with 80,000 migrants, mostly young Moroccan men, arriving on July 30 and 31. At least 57 people died trying to make the journey and Morocco has disputed Spanish sovereignty of the territory since independence in 1956.

The Ceuta president has said 13,000 of those migrants remain and it is still a red-hot political issue, which Real Madrid and other clubs have now waded in on.

Prior to their 3-2 win over Elche on Tuesday night, the whole squad were given t-shirts for an initiative designed to show solidarity with the residents of Ceuta.

Vinicius Jr (left) and Kylian Mbappe (right) showed their opposition to the message of Ceuta solidarity displayed on Real Madrid's t-shirts

Ibrahima Konate, Vinicius Jr and Mbappe were the only three players to roll up their shirts

In an embarrassing turn for Real, that message was then undermined by Mbappe, Vinicius Jr and Konate in front of the watching world.

The trio wanted to clearly demonstrate their opposition to the sentiment, deliberately hiding the slogan, effectively saying 'we do not agree with this stance.'

None of the players have come out publicly to explain their view on Ceuta but the pictures and footage from Tuesday evening speak volumes.

The rest of Jose Mourinho's squad posed for customary photos and lined up as usual ahead of the LaLiga clash kitted out in their specially designed green and white t-shirts.

Footage showed Vinicius Jr with his shirt rolled up to cover the message, before Mbappe grimaced when putting his on.

He then saw what Vinicius Jr had done and repeated the move.

The initiative for clubs to promote a message of Ceuta solidarity was put forward by league organisers for this round of fixtures.

No other players in the nine other fixtures over the weekend chose to demonstrate their protest to the Ceuta solidarity message.

Pictured: People play football at a settlement in Benitez Beach, created after the mass crossing of migrants from Morocco, in Ceuta, Spain, September 13, 2026

The three Real stars who opted to defy the club have angered plenty of supporters.

One wrote: 'I hope they boo them until the day they leave Real Madrid, utter disgust.'

Another posted: 'I hope Florentino fines them with 3 months' suspension without a job or pay. That way, the nonsense would end quickly. They're way too full of themselves.'

While a third gave his damning verdict: 'Shame that @realmadrid allows this contempt toward our compatriots from Ceuta by these millionaires who live in luxurious gated communities with private security.'

A Moroccan player for Real Betis in Seville, Ez Abde, also wore the t-shirt before his side's game against Villarreal and received a barrage of abuse online from his countrymen.

The issue is a hugely sensitive one and Ceuta's crisis has been front and centre of the political agenda in Spain since July.

Mbappe has not publicly spoken about his views on the migrant crisis in Ceuta

Spain is preparing accommodation for up to 10,000 migrants in Ceuta and the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, has insisted the situation was not mishandled. 'What happened is that we couldn't cope with the influx,' he said this week.

He added that authorities had taken in the migrants before returning the majority to Morocco, adding that nine in ten had gone back.

Sánchez said accommodation for 6,000 people would be available by the end of the week, with capacity eventually rising to 10,000.

He said the government hoped to have the situation under control by the end of the year and appealed for patience from residents of Ceuta, which has a population of around 84,000.

Sports.title: JIMMY MONTGOMERY EXCLUSIVE: Sunderland's FA Cup hero on the hijinks of the Black Cats' last European adventure, having his gloves stolen in Lisbon - and his verdict on Robin Roefs
Sports.content:
JIMMY MONTGOMERY EXCLUSIVE: Sunderland's FA Cup hero on the hijinks of the Black Cats' last European adventure, having his gloves stolen in Lisbon - and his verdict on Robin Roefs

In the hall of Jimmy Montgomery’s peaceful house in the Sunderland suburbs is a framed black-and-white photograph of the save in the 1973 FA Cup final for which he will forever be remembered.

It’s a simple picture, an iconic moment beautifully captured.

The players of Sunderland and Leeds are in classic football strips, free of clutter and sponsors' logos. Long hair and black boots. Meanwhile a goalkeeper dives low into history to parry a header wearing a pair of woollen gloves that look like they could have come from a local garden centre.

‘I haven’t got those gloves anymore,’ Montgomery tells the Daily Mail from his seat on the sofa.

‘When we played in Lisbon (against Sporting) in the Cup Winners' Cup the next season, I put them in the back of the net with my cap as I always did. And somebody stole them.

‘Ball boy? Cameraman? I have no idea. So that was one souvenir gone in a flash.

‘Not that it really mattered. I hardly wore them. When they were wet they were about as much use as a chocolate watch!’

Sunderland legend Jimmy Montgomery has fond memories of the club's last European campaign in 1973-74 - apart from having his goalkeeper gloves stolen in Lisbon!

Montgomery has a framed photo of the save in the 1973 FA Cup final against Leeds for which he will forever be remembered

We are here on Wearside to talk, for once, not about that stunning double save that helped second-tier Sunderland win the Cup at Wembley 53 years ago, but about the European campaign that followed.

It was the club’s first foray into Europe and, until today, their last.

As Regis Le Bris’ impressive modern team face AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League tomorrow night, Montgomery will be in the stand that, since the start of last season, carries his name.

‘We played our first tie in Budapest behind the Iron Curtain and it was the exact same XI that had won the cup final,’ recalls Montgomery. ‘I don’t think that was sentiment. I think we deserved it.

‘These days the team will have a dossier on the opponents and take their own chef and staff with them.

‘We had our manager Bob Stokoe, his assistant and maybe the club secretary. That was it.

‘In terms of the opposition (Vasas Budapest) we didn’t know a thing about them apart from what the press men on the plane told us.

‘It took us for ever to get there and even longer to get back. But we won 2-0 and also beat them at home. Marvellous.

‘It ended for us in the next round at Sporting Lisbon. That was a strange night.

‘They had ball-boys throwing the balls on but when they did, the Lisbon players would throw them straight off again, sometimes straight into the crowd.

‘We looked at the ref and he just stared back at us. I guess it was time-wasting. But I have never seen anything like it before or since.’

Sunderland captain Bobby Kerr is held aloft by his team-mates, including Montgomery (fourth from right) after the 1-0 win over Leeds in 1973

Now, at the age of 82, Montgomery is revered to such a degree he literally has his name written throughout the modern Sunderland

Facing a shot from Newcastle's Jim Scott in the Tyne-Wear derby at Roker Park in 1968

Montgomery made a record 627 appearances for his hometown club across 18 years. As a boy he would watch his team at Roker Park with his father. As an apprentice, he would later sweep the terraces and paint the seats.

Now, at the age of 82, he is revered to such a degree he literally has his name written throughout the modern Sunderland.

As well as the stand at the Stadium of Light, this year’s goalkeeping jerseys have his signature, number of appearances and even an outline of his famous save embossed in them.

‘It’s hard to believe,' he says. ‘I am just a kid from down the road.’

Montgomery has served Sunderland as player, goalkeeping coach and worked at its centre of excellence.

‘I have actually been let go four times and that was hard,’ he says. ‘Different managers would want different things. So yeah I got kicked out.

‘But I kept getting invited back again!

‘I even had a year coaching at Newcastle with Kevin Keegan and, as hard as it is for Sunderland fans to hear, Pavel Srnicek was perhaps the best I worked with.’

A welcome visitor to Sunderland’s training ground whenever his health allows, Montgomery has talked football with the ever-respectful Le Bris and goalkeeping with current No 1 Robin Roefs.

‘They sometimes bring the goalkeepers over for a chat,’ he explains. ‘I think the young ones want to talk. That’s very humbling and typical of the club now.

Montgomery made a record 627 appearances for his hometown club across 18 years

Montgomery (second left) poses with the Cup alongside (from left) Ian Porterfield, Micky Horswill and Kerr

‘Robin is an excellent keeper, a brilliant keeper. Sometimes I just wish he wouldn't try to play from the back so much. I'm not a great fan of it. I get wound up.

‘It’s a risk. I would much rather goalkeepers get it forward, push the team up, and start from there.

‘I'm a big believer in once the goalkeeper's got the ball, he's in charge of it. He does what he thinks right.

‘If he doesn't want to play it short, he shouldn't have to. Look at the Arsenal goalkeeper on Saturday. He dictated everything. He was fully in charge. I like that.’

If Montgomery was impressed with David Raya, he was less enamoured with Arsenal.

‘I have no time for them,’ he says. ‘Goodness I couldn’t watch that every week. What is that type of football?

‘Their manager is complaining like mad about giving the penalty away but if you're going to get mixed up in that, it will go against you eventually.

‘It’s amazing what goes on at corners now. They don’t even look at the ball. We never grappled like that. I just knew that when the ball came over I was gonna get smashed.

‘Wyn Davies of Newcastle and good old Nat Lofthouse. Every time. Bang. There was no protection. You just had to be ready for it.’

At the end of his career, Montgomery spent a season at Nottingham Forest under Brian Clough.

‘I played with Brian and he was brilliant, though he knew it too,’ he smiles. ‘I was playing the day he broke his leg on Boxing Day in 1962. So I was chuffed he thought I was good enough all those years later to be under-study to Shilts (Peter Shilton).

‘I was in my mid-30s and coming towards the end. I never played but was on the bench when Forest won the European Cup in Madrid in 1980. I got a medal.’

Montgomery – who rates the great Pat Jennings as perhaps the best goalkeeper he has known – has a photo of himself with the European Cup and it feels strange to see him in another club’s colours.

‘I have no time for them,’ says Montgomery of Arsenal. ‘Goodness I couldn’t watch that every week. What is that type of football?

But it’s that black-and-white picture of his Wembley save that we return to.

The first effort – the one on the picture – was from Trevor Cherry. The follow-up from five yards from Peter Lorimer was struck so powerfully ITV commentator Brian Moore shouted ‘goal’ before it struck the underside of the bar.

Afterwards, it was the late Jimmy Hill who declared it had been the tips of Montgomery’s fingers that had touched it up on to the woodwork.

Montgomery’s favourite line is to say he wished he had caught the first shot so he wouldn’t have had to spend his life talking about the second.

‘But I don’t mean it,’ he smiles. ‘I love what it still means to people.

‘It was only when standing with my pint of milk afterwards that I realised the significance of it. They just kept showing it.

‘I was lucky it was on TV, mind. I had made one from a lad playing for Hull a few weeks before that was even better…’

Sports.title: 'He can become one of the ultimate legends of the game': England bowling guru TROY COOLEY on what he loves about his attack, how Jofra Archer is still improving, why Josh Tongue is 'unique' and the other bowlers on his Ashes radar
Sports.content:
It’s not hard to see why Troy Cooley – world cricket’s fast-bowling whisperer – gets on so well with his charges, easy to grasp why England were so keen to lure him back after 20 years away.

Ask him anything about his trade and he responds with a laugh and a quip, followed by an answer that is both engaging and engaged. He’s a people person, a believer in the art of his job as well as the science. He got the best out of England’s famous 2005 Ashes pace quartet, and is now trying to contain his excitement about Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.

And, armed with a dislike of batsmen that is both hammed-up and genuine, he has no doubt which of cricket’s two main skills is the tougher.

‘Batters get a stress fracture of the brain when they do too much,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport while on manoeuvres at Grace Road, where he is keeping an eye on the quicks of Leicestershire and Hampshire. ‘Bowlers get a stress fracture of the body.’

Cooley is 60, having stayed close to the peak of the game since his three-year stint with Duncan Fletcher’s England side ended in 2006 – between their 2–1 Ashes win of 2005 inspired by Steve Harmison, Matthew Hoggard, Andrew Flintoff and Simon Jones, and their harrowing 5–0 Ashes whitewash in 2006-07.

By then, the Tasmanian-born Cooley had become bowling coach of his native Australia, and it was tempting to note that he had a curious habit of helping the victors. Now, after long spells in Australia and India, he was re-signed by the ECB in January, and intends to be on the winning side once more when the Ashes battle resumes next summer.

England's fast bowling coach Troy Cooley, 60, is impressed with England's current attack of Gus Atkinson, Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue

Robinson, who averaged 8.76 against Pakistan, can transfer his skills overseas, insists Cooley

To hear him talk about the current fast-bowling foursome, who knocked over Pakistan for five successive scores below 200 before being belted over all Edgbaston by tailender Razaullah, is to believe it’s perfectly possible.

Asked whether he thinks Archer, who touched 94mph this summer, can get better, he replies: ‘Of course he can. He’s had a history of trying to get himself on the park, and he’s learned how his body adapts and works. He’s got the mentality that he wants to get better.

‘He’s got the skill level to become one of the ultimate legends of the game, one of those great champions everyone talks about.’

He believes that Robinson, who averaged 8.76 against Pakistan, can transfer his skills overseas, and raves about his control.

‘Out… stand… ding,’ he says, breaking the word into its syllables. ‘He’s tall. He’s got bounce. He moves the ball, so he misses the middle of the bat on most occasions –left and right, up and down.

‘One of the key things I say to our bowlers is all we’ve got to do is miss the middle of the bat. Then the batter gets frustrated and he’s going to make a stupid mistake. We lay the beautiful trap.’

As much as anything, Cooley is excited by variety. Where Harmison offered bounce, Hoggard swing, Flintoff pace and Jones reverse-swing, the current crop all have their USPs too – not least Tongue, with an action that goes beyond the perpendicular, luring right-handers into playing at deliveries better left alone.

Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson bring unique skills to the England attack

And Jofra Archer, says Cooley, 'can become one of the ultimate legends of the game'

‘He’s unique, and that’s what we’re after,’ Cooley says of Tongue. ‘But he doesn’t just release the ball from a different position: he bowls at bloody 90mph, and for most batters decision-making starts to get interrupted at about 85.’

Only Atkinson failed to help himself to wickets against Pakistan, and while Cooley insists he adds ‘an integral glue to this group’, citing his ‘great arm speed, ability to move the ball and sharp bouncer’, he also admits: ‘He’s just got to work out which bowler he wants to be.’

He adds: ‘I like the fact that he’s dogged. He’s just got to stay fit, which was one of his big issues before: we’d play a couple of games and then he’d be down on pace and his hamstring is hanging off. But he’ll be OK.’

So what about that third evening in Birmingham, when England’s quicks were battered into submission by Razaullah’s nine sixes, and Joe Root rushed off the field, presumably for dressing-room advice?

‘I just thought that maybe they needed a bit of consolidation around what we’re going to do here,’ Cooley says. ‘Remember, our best ball has got the top order out so far. Let’s just hang in there a bit longer, let’s not try and finish this too early. When you get a bit emotional, the process goes out the window sometimes.

‘I think the captain and the rest of the team will learn from that. But there’s nothing like denting a bit of pride to get someone out of their comfort zone.’

Cooley points to the strength in depth of English fast bowling, and mentions Sussex seamer Henry Crocombe, as well as three others who have played Test cricket over the last two summers: Sam Cook, Matt Fisher and Sonny Baker, who on Tuesday night spoke about his winter touring ambitions after taking three for 12 in England’s T20 demolition of Sri Lanka in Southampton.

Cooley believes that Atkinson 'has just got to work out which bowler he wants to be’

Cooley helped England win the 2005 Ashes and would like to repeat the trick next year

Above all, he wants to create a fast-bowling unit that can perform abroad as well as it can at home – what he calls the ‘holy grail’ of his job. And, as ever, his tendency is to seek the clearest, simplest explanation.

‘I mean, it is still about hitting the top of off and taking responsibility that my job is to take a wicket, stop runs and stay fit to perform. And I’m going to be able to do that anywhere I rock up, because I have worked hard enough on the skills.’

Cooley laughs, but the message is deadly serious. England have the right man in place for a crack at Australia.

Sports.title: Football legend Ronald Koeman announces death of wife, 65, following breast cancer battle in heartbreaking tribute after 41-year marriage
Sports.content:
Football legend Ronald Koeman announces death of wife, 65, following breast cancer battle in heartbreaking tribute after 41-year marriage

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Football legend Ronald Koeman has announced the death of his beloved wife Bartina from breast cancer aged 65.

The former Netherlands and Barcelona boss and his other half were married for 41 years and he shared a heartbreaking message with the news on Instagram.

Koeman, 63, wrote: 'With intense sadness, but also with great pride and love, we say goodbye to my beautiful wife, our dearest mom and grandma.'

The image he shared to accompany the post was a black and white shot of the couple looking into each other's eyes and clasping their hands together.

Koeman, who established himself as a football legend during his decorated playing career for Barcelona, Ajax, PSV and Feyenoord, married Bartina back in 1985.

They had three children and four grandchildren together during a long and happy marriage.

Ronald Koeman posted this image of him and his late wife Bartina, announcing her death

Koeman, pictured with Bartina and his children in 1997 after a Feyenoord game, was married to Bartina for 41 years

Bartina was re-diagnosed with breast cancer in 2023 when he started his second spell in charge of the Dutch national team.

She had previously recovered from breast cancer in 2010 and it came back in 2018.

Bartina continued to fight the disease and Koeman said metastases had been detected last year, which his wife was receiving treatment for.

When he stepped down from the Dutch job, he made a point of thanking his wife for her support, saying: 'My wife Bartina supported and encouraged me every day, despite her own illness, to finish my work as national coach.

'That is a testament to incredible strength. I am more grateful to her for that than I will ever be able to put into words.'

Bartina thrived in her own successful career as an entrepreneur and had her own cosmetics and skincare line.

And Koeman has received an outpouring of support, with tributes flooding in on social media following the announcement.

The couple share a laugh in 2022 during a match between Telstar and Helmond Sport

Legendary goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar wrote: 'My deepest condolences and wishing you all much strength together as a family.'

Denzel Dumfries, Brian Brobbey, Ryan Gravenberch, Nathan Ake and a number of other Dutch stars who played under Koeman replied to his message with a heart emoji.

Koeman, who managed Southampton and Everton in the Premier League, has not taken another job since stepping down from the Netherlands job after their World Cup elimination by Morocco in the round of 32.

Sports.title: E1 Series commits to Africa with LeBron James and Will Smith backing in Angola
Sports.content:
E1 Series commits to Africa with LeBron James and Will Smith backing in Angola

The E1 Series brought its electric powerboat racing to Angola, with team owners LeBron James and Will Smith in attendance – and the championship has committed to a three-year stay in the country

View 3 Images Team Brady, the reigning two-time champions owned by Tom Brady, won in Luanda (Image: Getty Images)

Electric motorsport took a major leap forward into its thrilling future last weekend.

‌



Dubbed the ‘F1 of water,’ the E1 Series has surged into the sporting consciousness thanks to its celebrity-packed ownership group. But the real action unfolds on the water, where fully electric powerboats - bearing closer resemblance to spacecraft - battle for dominance at speeds exceeding 60 mph across some of the world's most stunning locations.

‌



So, why did E1 decide to bring LeBron James, Will Smith and electric global motorsport to Angola? “There are many different answers to that,” E1 CEO Jamie Copas told The Mirror in Luanda. “We're a global championship, it's important to us to go to new locations, it's important to us to tell our stories where we go. We find locations through long conversations with many different people.

‌



Tiger Woods makes first public golf appearance since car crash after taking break for treatment READ MORE :

Bradley Wiggins insists best is yet to come from Team GB's cycling phenom READ MORE :

“Africa is a really important location for us to come to. We raced in Lagos in Nigeria last year, and it was always the intention to find other locations in Africa where we can race, tell our stories, work with like-minded people, and have the same understanding of the foundational stories that we have and the things we're trying to do.

“When we choose our locations, it's not just about country: it's the backdrop and the location so that we can actually put on a spectacle. We need a waterway that’s long enough, wide enough, deep enough, safe enough, calm enough where we can do this. In Luanda, the Yacht Club was the perfect destination for us.

“From there, our conversations with the government, with the ministry and everyone were just so simple. We have 17 containers full of kit that gets moved around the world, and every venue we go to has different infrastructure so we need support, and we feel we’ve been given that in the local market.”

‌



Copas is convinced Africa is vital to E1's expansion, and left the door open to hosting more than one race per season on the continent. Last year, Lagos proved a resounding success, with a packed-out fan zone underlining the significance of making the sport accessible to as wide an audience as possible.

Luanda drew an equally impressive crowd, with fans going wild for LeBron and Smith. Copas also harbours hopes of recruiting an African pilot to join the paddock in the not-too-distant future.

View 3 Images Westbrook Racing owner Will Smith and Team Alula champion LeBron James both attended the race on Sunday

‌



As far as E1 is concerned, Angola and the wider continent could play a pivotal role in shaping the series' future.

“The reason we do what we do is to tell three foundational stories,” Copas continued. “One's about sustainability, the second one is about gender parity, and the third one is about innovation. Racing is the foundation of what we do, and it gives us the platform on which to produce an amazing spectacle and do the sport that we love doing. But actually, the stories are really important, and that’s why we do what we do.

“We're a global championship, and if you actually look at our audience, we have quite a large market from Africa. We're constantly analyzing the data to see where people are watching, how many people are seeing the spectacle that we create, the racing that we've got on, but also those three stories because the more we can talk about sustainability, gender parity and innovation, the more change we can make.

‌



“Africa is at a point of its development that's incredible, and if we can help with those stories, if we can get more people to see what's happening in the destinations that we go to, wherever it is in the world, especially in Africa, why wouldn't we? We want to work together.

View 3 Images Luanda is set to become a staple of the E1 calendar, with the city inking a three-year deal with the series (Image: Getty Images)

“We're not going to change the world tomorrow, we're not here on that sort of mission, but we are trying to change electric mobility because that brings great benefits around the world and that can help here, that can help in Italy, it can help in America, wherever we go to. But we've got a great opportunity here to tap into a very wide audience and tell those stories more and more that will have an effect on everything we do tomorrow, the day after and the day after that.”

Article continues below

E1 has pledged a three-year commitment to Angola, demonstrating a dedication to advancing the series in a nation and region frequently neglected by international sporting events. Copas added: “It's for us to help tell Angola stories, and I think it’s also for Angola to help tell ours. It’s about that collaboration and partnership. I think the more we can be doing to help with sustainability, green energy, the better.

“Hopefully next year it will be even bigger, the following year it will be even bigger and we can continue to tell the stories. Earlier this week, some of the pilots and some of our team visited a mangrove and planted seeds there. It will be great to come back next year and see how that’s grown. The opportunity to come back is something we welcome.”

Sports.title: Man Utd could lose millions on JJ Gabriel as favourites to sign youngster emerge
Sports.content:
Man Utd could lose millions on JJ Gabriel as favourites to sign youngster emerge

JJ Gabriel has reportedly asked to leave Manchester United, with Real Madrid and Barcelona said to be among those interested in the 15-year-old, which could cost United millions in lost transfer fees

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has asked to leave Manchester United. (Image: (Photo by Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United losing JJ Gabriel could cost the club millions after the 15-year-old's shocking request to rip up the contract. The Red Devils have been left rocked by the decision from the teenager, who was viewed as one of the shining lights of the club's future.

‌



Gabriel has an Irish passport and will be eligible for a move overseas when he turns 16, next month. Due to current rules, English players are restricted from moving abroad until the age of 18, but there are a host of European giants circling for the coveted attackers' signature.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Spanish giants Real Madrid and Barcelona are reportedly monitoring Gabriel's situation. If the 15-year-old was to leave for an overseas club, United would only be due around £300,000 in compensation, but moves within England could be a lot more with fruitful - with Liverpool forced to pay at least £2.8m to Chelsea for Rio Ngumoha.

‌



Referee backed over Man Utd VAR decision as Premier League release official verdict READ MORE :

According to the Daily Mail, Gabriel and his family have long harboured ambitions of a move to Spain, with Madrid and Barcelona amongst the interested parties.

United were left blindsided when the prodigious talent made his desire to cut ties with the Old Trafford club known.

PSG, Bayern, alongside the Spanish heavyweights, are reportedly keen on securing Gabriel's signature, leaving United facing an uphill battle to fend off rival clubs when he turns 16 on October 9.

‌



Gabriel had been set to feature in the squad for the Carabao Cup clash with Brighton and Hove Albion, following his hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League victory over Sabah, but that prospect now appears remote.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has yet to make his senior debut for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Old Trafford insiders remain uncertain about what prompted the 15-year-old's desire to depart the club, though alarm bells first rang when he wiped all United content from his social media accounts last week.

‌



Gabriel has established himself as a regular fixture in Michael Carrick's first-team preparations and was given his debut during pre-season against Atletico Madrid in Sweden.

The 15-year-old was on course to become the fourth youngest Premier League appearance maker had he been introduced against Hull City on the opening day of the campaign.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Article continues below

However, their loss and the nature of that match prevented such an opportunity, while the 5-2 triumph over Ipswich also presented a suitable moment.

United believe they have exhausted every avenue to demonstrate to the youngster that he represents the club's future, but he will not be given the opportunity to become the youngest ever player in Wednesday's Carabao Cup third-round fixture.

Gabriel became the youngest winner of the Jimmy Murphy award for the club's best young player and scored 26 goals in 29 games last season. He has five in three games this term, including two in his first two matches at Premier League 2 level.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods makes first public golf appearance since car crash after taking break for treatment
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods makes first public golf appearance since car crash after taking break for treatment

Tiger Woods has given an update after a clip of him hitting balls was shared

View 2 Images Tiger Woods has returned to the golf course (Image: Getty Images)

Tiger Woods has shared footage of him hitting golf balls for the first time since his car accident and break from the game. The 15-time major champion was seen practising on the range at Liberty National in New Jersey ahead of the upcoming Nexus Cup, an amateur event Woods is hosting to raise funds for his TGR Foundation.

‌



The 50-year-old also held a clinic at which the master of ceremonies asked him about his game. He said: "I can hit pretty much anything."

‌



The PGA Tour also posted a video, which Woods shared, of him hitting a crisp iron shot off a practice tee. The caption reads: "Tiger Woods is back on the range! His last PGA Tour start was July 2024."

‌



While it is unclear whether he was preparing for a comeback, the tone of the PGA Tour's post suggests it isn't out of the question.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Woods escaped unhurt after rolling his Land Rover in March and subsequently took time out of the public eye to "seek treatment and focus on my health." Earlier this month, he pleaded no contest to a charge of reckless driving and accepted a five-year suspension of his driving licence and a £742 fine. He pleaded not guilty to the original DUI charge.

‌



Tiger Woods avoids jail with last-minute plea deal over reckless driving charge that ended in horror crash READ MORE :

LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection as star players owed £33m free to leave READ MORE :

A no-contest plea is not an admission of guilt, but means the accused will offer no defence. The plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal justice system.

He arrived at the courthouse in County Martin, Florida, with his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, the former daughter-in-law of President Donald Trump . She sat behind him during the proceedings, which were held in a mostly empty courtroom.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Neither Woods nor the person in the other vehicle was injured in the crash but the star's Land Rover caused £3,700 in damage to the truck, according to a police report.

Woods is considered among the greatest golfers of all time and has won 15 major titles. That includes three Open Championship and US Open titles apiece, four editions of the PGA Championship and The Masters six times.

View 2 Images Woods leaves the courthouse in Florida (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The last of his major championship victories came in 2019 amid huge fanfare at Augusta. He hasn't appeared in a PGA Tour event since the 2024 Open at Royal Troon, where he failed to make the cut.

Sports.title: Dean Richards revolution sparks optimism at Doncaster Knights ahead of new season
Sports.content:
Dean Richards revolution sparks optimism at Doncaster Knights ahead of new season

The arrival of former England and British & Irish Lions No.8 Richards, who has enjoyed a successful coaching career at Leicester, Harlequins and Newcastle, has ensured there is plenty of reason for optimism at the club.

View Image Corey Tait and Kieran Wilkinson of Doncaster Knights at the Champ Rugby 2026/27 media day (Image: 2026 The RFU)

The Dean Richards era has begun at Doncaster Knights and with some savvy arrivals on the pitch and behind the scenes, as well as renewed rivalry, excitement abounds at Castle Park.

‌



Following a tricky season during which Donny made the decision to go from full-time to a hybrid set-up, it would have been easy to start to worry about the club’s trajectory. But the arrival of former England and British & Irish Lions No.8 Richards, who has enjoyed a successful coaching career at Leicester, Harlequins and Newcastle, has ensured there is plenty of reason for optimism at the club.

‌



Among those who have also joined in the summer are former Caldy fly-half Kieran Wilkinson, and coach Alan Dickens, who was in charge at Newcastle last season.

‌



Reflecting on Richards’ impact, hooker Corey Tait said: “It can only been good for the club. We've already seen the impact he has had in the little time he has been there. You look at the coaches he's brought in, Alan Dickens is really quality from what we have seen so far. We're grateful to have him and Dicko come in.

“It's more been his backroom impact so far. He's a very approachable person, you can go and have a conversation with him and speak to him about different things. But the difference has been the backroom stuff, he's brought players in, he's brought Dicko in and the prestige he brings to the club and the experience in the PREM, he's got a lot of knowledge and experience behind him.”

Doncaster finished eighth in Elior Champ Rugby last season, paying the price for a slow start as their run of four straight wins to finish the season proved too little, too late. They are hoping to be right in contention for the top six and a play-off spot this time around, particularly after seeing Worcester come from fourth spot to win it all last year.

‌



And with Rotherham Titans’ promotion, they also have a derby date to look forward to, and the prize of the Yorkshire Cup on the line for added spice.

Tait said: “You've got your usual suspects, the likes of Ealing and Worcester and you go from there. That top six come Christmas time is going to be incredibly competitive and it's going to come down to those last few weekends to decide those play-off spots. We all know what can happen from there.

‌



“It's a big rivalry (with Rotherham), we've got the Yorkshire Cup that gets played and it's not been played for a few seasons. That will be a big thing, we're looking forward to those home and away fixtures. We've got a couple of lads from Roth in our squad so I'm sure they will be looking to go after it.”

Another change in Elior Champ Rugby this year is the introduction of free-to-air coverage with BLAZE showing matches on Sunday afternoons in addition to Clubber TV’s offering that was transformative last term. Doncaster will be at the heart of thew new broadcast deal, having been selected for the first two weekends as they travel to Cornish Pirates before welcoming Hartpury.

Wilkinson added: "It's testament to Clubber and now BLAZE coming through, showing the game and what it can bring. We want to show the exciting rugby that Champ has to offer. We want to make it as competitive as we can so I think it's really exciting to see BLAZE coming in showing free-to-air TV is exciting.
