Security camera footage released by the government showed Amini in the downtown Tehran re-education centre collapsing onto the ground, as a chador-clad policewoman scolded her. She was taken to a nearby hospital and pronounced dead three days later on September 16, 2022.

Authorities claimed Amini had pre-existing health conditions and denied any wrongdoing. But her father, Amjad Amini, said fellow prisoners told him her daughter had been beaten inside the police van.

Two female journalists, working for local newspapers, helped break the story and grabbed the attention of the nation. The reports included a heart-wrenching image of her parents embracing in front of the intensive care unit where Amini died. The journalists were later imprisoned on national security charges.

Small demonstrations took place in front of the hospital, and then in her hometown of Saqqez, in the western province of Kurdistan, after her funeral. Within several weeks, protests had spread across Iran, calling for greater freedoms for women and Iranians in general. The protests lasted into early 2023 and received support from across the globe.



The United Nations’ Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran later corroborated reports by foreign-based rights groups that at least 550 Iranians were killed during the protests, including 68 children and 49 women in 26 of Iran’s 31 provinces.

A Kurdish saying, “Woman, Life, Freedom”, became the slogan of this unprecedented movement, which has significantly altered how Iranians dress and think.

“I thought we would never be able to choose the way we want to dress, but the movement created massive cultural change and a more progressive identity that can never be taken away now,” Bahar, a 26-year-old woman living in Tehran, who used just her first name for security reasons, told Al Jazeera.

Bahar said she never believed in the mandatory hijab and always wished she could choose what to wear, as most women across the globe do, including in almost all other Islamic countries.

For months after the protests died down, she would keep a headscarf around her neck for fear of reprisals by the authorities. Despite the lingering risks, she no longer carries that headscarf, either.

Setareh, another young resident of the capital, has the support of more family members for her choice of what she wears and how she looks. She faces fewer instances of verbal abuse on Tehran’s streets for how she dresses, and is rarely turned down by ride-hailing drivers for not wearing the hijab.

“People and families, especially men, are now more accustomed to women dressing more naturally, even if they don’t like it,” she told Al Jazeera.

Many Iranians have reflected on the movement online, with one post recalling the time two young women took the then-unprecedented step of eating breakfast in a traditional downtown Tehran restaurant without mandatory hijabs.

They were arrested and later released, but their actions opened the way for countless others after them to do the same.

What are the authorities saying?

Wearing a hijab has remained mandatory for women in Iran since shortly after Iran’s 1979 Islamic revolution, and authorities have frequently attempted to reinstate it where possible.

When the protests started in late 2022, the government tried to push its own narrative by staging counter-demonstrations. State-linked and more traditional voices continue to criticise and attack those who ignore the dress code required by the state.

A harsh hijab bill was passed in late 2023 that envisioned tougher punishments for offenders, but President Masoud Pezeshkian said he could not enforce it since most people rejected the law and it could lead to more unrest. This was happening at a time when Iran was facing eternal pressure from the US and its allies, he added.



Mai Sato, special UN rapporteur on human rights in Iran, said in a statement on Wednesday that even though that law was suspended, numerous cafes, restaurants and shops continue to be closed by authorities and some staff or customers are arrested for breaking the hijab rules.

This week, local reports said several women were arrested over the hijab laws and put into vans and buses by armed security forces in the city of Isfahan. Reports of other crackdowns have emerged in Rasht and Mashhad, although the authorities have not confirmed or commented on the incidents.

Videos circulating online on Wednesday showed that some businesses were closed in Saqqez and other Kurdistan cities to mark the anniversary of Amini’s death, with security forces present in main squares and streets, likely anticipating protests.

Gholam-Ali Haddad-Adel, a senior official and the father-in-law of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, told local media this week that a “decadent Western lifestyle” was being propagated by Iran’s “enemies” inside the country through women’s unveilings.

Iran remains in a state of war since the United States and Israel launched strikes on February 28, killing much of the Iranian leadership and 120 children at a school in Minab.

“Due to war conditions, for now we can’t enter the arena of hijab the way we should,” he said, indicating that police had been lax on enforcing the law due to the current situation.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij paramilitary force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and another figure close to the office of the supreme leader, said the authorities must deal with hijab through unity.

“We must not allow such issues to disturb our domestic cohesion,” Taeb said during a speech this week to a group of Basij commanders.

In an extensive report released on Wednesday, Amnesty International reiterated its previous findings that Iranian authorities had committed “crimes against humanity” during the Mahsa Amini protests, and called for accountability.

It named 87 Iranian officials who it said should be criminally investigated, spanning national, provincial and local command structures, including the IRGC, police and Interior Ministry authorities.

Names included Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and armed forces commander Mohammad Bagheri, both of whom were killed during the war, as well as Ahmad Vahidi, the incumbent commander-in-chief of the IRGC, who was interior minister at the time.

World.title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'
World.content:
Setting out the EU's political and policy priorities for year ahead, von der Leyen also proposed the formation of a European Security Council, which would include the UK and Ukraine, amid an ongoing threat to the continent from Russia.

"For a long time, we have discussed a leaders' format focused on the security of our continent, with partners like Canada, Norway, Ukraine, the United Kingdom and others involved," she said in the wide-ranging address.

"This is even more urgent now, given the nature and scale of the risks at play. This is why we will set out our ideas to make a European Security Council a reality."

Calls for such a body have been growing since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

It was initially a French-German conception but more countries have shown support, particularly as Trump has questioned the Nato military alliance. Other nations worry such a council could unhelpfully rival Nato.

Von der Leyen said the EU was "strengthening our work with Nato" and that expanded defence spending would be "fully aligned" with the alliance.

But at the core of such a security council would be the ability to trigger an emergency meeting if one member felt under threat, similar to Nato's Article 4.

The EU chief said it would be a "mechanism to flank" Article 4, a term that could be interpreted as complementing Nato functions or - if taken in a military context - bypassing them.

Alongside global threats, von der Leyen also said many European families were worried about the cost of living, and the "dizzying speed of change" of technology and its impacts on jobs and society.

Other proposals included inviting the world's largest AI labs for talks on how to support industry efforts to pace the frontier, as well as slashing bureaucracy for businesses in the EU.

Plans to curb social media use among children, including banning platforms for under 13s, were also put forward. Under the proposal, children aged 13 to 15 would only be able to set up social media accounts which are supervised by parents.

A new emergency tool to help countries better deal with mass migration movements following the deadly influx of migrants to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July would also be outlined.

The pledge chimes with the message of European politicians on the right and hard right who have gained support in recent years for proposing a tougher approach.

Some of them called the mass attempt to enter the EU through Ceuta an "invasion" and argued asylum rules should be suspended to deal with such a crisis.

Von der Leyen said the new emergency tool would "only be triggered under a strictly defined set of criteria" and for a specific period of time, and that fundamental rights would be protected.

Human rights groups worry such a move would see vulnerable people, including women and children, turned back and denied the protection afforded to them under international law.

World.title: Eight children among 21 killed after war-damaged Gaza building collapses, rescuers say
World.content:
At least 21 people have been killed, including eight children, and dozens are missing after a war-damaged building collapsed in the Gaza Strip overnight, local rescuers and medics say.

Witnesses told the BBC that the six-storey building in the Tal al-Hawa area of Gaza City had been left tilting dangerously to one side after an Israeli strike more than a year ago. Displaced families were living inside because they were desperate, they said.

UN agencies and an Egyptian team have joined the search for survivors, but officials say it is proceeding slowly due to a lack of equipment.

In the initial rescue effort, members of the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency resorted to using their bare hands.

"We are still hearing voices from under the rubble, so there is still hope to find people," said Raed al-Dahshan, the director of the Civil Defence in Gaza City.

He added: "The limited availability of shelter options forced residents to move into this building, believing it was safe. However, at one point it collapsed entirely, tragically crashing down on people as they slept."

World.title: US accuses Russia of trying to kill Ukrainian allies overseas
World.content:
The US Department of Justice (DoJ) has accused Russia of plotting to murder Ukrainian allies in the US and Europe.

In a statement on Tuesday, the DoJ charged five men allegedly connected to the Russian Intelligence Services (RIS). The men are accused of paying, or trying to pay, people in the US and overseas to target those "aligned, or perceived to be aligned, with Ukraine".

"It is our job to stop America's adversaries from unleashing violence and terror on American soil," Attorney General Todd Blanche. All those accused remain at large.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Wednesday Moscow will not comment until it hears or sees "any credible evidence" or "tangible facts".

It is not clear if the five accused are in the United States, or in a different location.

Washington has charged all five men with participating in a conspiracy to finance terrorism, which carries a maximum 20-year prison sentence.

Three of the defendants are "high-ranking members of the RIS network", the DoJ said.

Among them are Russian father and son Yuri Khrameev, 63, and Kirill Khrameev, 27. Khrameev senior was a colonel in the Russian intelligence services and his son is an officer in the Federal Security Service of Russia (FSB).

The third high-ranking suspect is Oemis Romagoza Durruthy, a 35-year-old Cuban national who the US describe as "an influential member of the Cuban diaspora living in Russia who has coordinated attacks for the RIS network".

Yaidel Delgado Suarez, 35, and Angel Eduardo Castro, 22, are the other two defendants.

The pair are accused of recruiting or attempting to recruit US-based individuals to "surveil and attempt to murder a prominent US-based Russian dissident".

The FBI's James Barnacle said the group "conspired to intimidate, threaten, or murder people on US soil and around the world".

One of the incidents is as recent as this summer. The DoJ described how the RIS network was able to recruit someone in the US to surveil and eventually murder a Russian dissident in the US.

Suarez allegedly sent the recruit to two locations linked to the victim with "explicit instructions on how to conduct surveillance". In exchange, the recruit was offered between $1,000 (Â£743) and $1,500.

Suarez and Castro are said to have offered an additional $40,000 if the US resident could "eliminate" the dissident.

The DoJ said the RIS recruit did not go through with it, which led Suarez to try and recruit "multiple other individuals within the United States". He allegedly offered "substantial sums of money to carry out the targeting of US based victims".

The release by the DoJ goes on to list other instances in which the accused allegedly tried to recruit others to kill those who were a perceived threat to Russia.

It said that in 2025, Khrameev junior allegedly recruited a US citizen to surveil and murder someone in Lithuania who was "telling lies about Russia". The release quotes Khrameev as saying the purpose was to target "all the countries that are helping Ukraine".

His father, Khrameev senior, is said to have offered the recruit $25,000 to kill the individual in Lithuania for "spreading dirt about my country" and "distorting history".

Khrameev senior, Suarez and Castro are the only ones also charged with "participating in a conspiracy to commit murder for hire". If found guilty, this charge carries a maximum 10-year prison sentence.

It is not the first time authorities thwart threats of this kind.

Last month, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities had detained an individual allegedly working for the Kremlin and who was plotting to murder an American-Ukrainian citizen in Warsaw.

Tusk told reporters the American-Ukrainian citizen "was uncomfortable for the Putin regime", adding: "We have to accept the assumption that the Putin regime will try to eliminate people who are inconvenient for various reasons."

In 2024, German authorities were reportedly warned by US intelligence of a Russian plot to kill Armin Papperger, the head of Germany's biggest arms company Rheinmetall.

Moscow dismissed the accusation at the time, with Kremlin spokesman Peskov saying: "It's all presented in the style of another fake story, so such reports cannot be taken seriously."

The fresh accusations from the DoJ come at a time of closer relations between Moscow and Washington following US President Donald Trump's return to the White House in 2025.

A few weeks ago, the head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) visited Moscow for talks with figures from Russia's intelligence services - an unconventional move that led to speculation.

The Kremlin confirmed that talks between John Ratcliffe and the intelligence services had taken place. President Trump did not say what was discussed but described the meeting as "semi-routine".

World.title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms
World.content:
The boss of ChatGPT-maker OpenAI says people should have more faith in AI firms to keep the tech safe, amid rising public concerns about the risks.

"The world should trust that we are going to do the right thing because it's the right thing and we feel the magnitude of this," Sam Altman said on Tuesday during a conference in San Francisco.

He accepted people were justified in being concerned about AI, as the capability of the tools has progressed rapidly.

But critics say firms cannot be trusted to self-regulate, with left-wing Senator Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon, a former adviser of US President Donald Trump, among those calling for greater governance of AI.

Trump himself has criticised calls for more guardrails on the fast-moving technology, calling fears about AI's safety a "hoax".

He said the only "guardrails" needed for AI was a "strong and smart" president.

Altman's comments on Tuesday came during an appearance at an annual conference hosted by software firm Salesforce.

"It doesn't take as much imagination as it used to for [us] to imagine how this could go wrong," he said. "I think the world is right to be afraid of this."

But AI bosses themselves have also admitted it may be difficult to regulate a technology which is changing so quickly.

In an interview with Axios published on 3 September, external, Altman said he had expected Congress to create a "basic framework" for advanced AI after his 2023 testimony, but that has yet to happen.

He suggested lawmakers have struggled to keep pace with the technology and to regulate it without "slow[ing] down innovation".

New safety legislation on AI is unlikely to emerge from the US Congress anytime soon, despite the fact lawmakers returned from their summer break on Monday.

There is a lack of consensus within both US parties on how any regulation would happen - and the House is set to enter recess again at the end of the week ahead of the midterm elections in early November.

World.title: Eight German state premiers back Merz amid speculation over future
World.content:
The leaders of eight German states have backed the nation's chancellor amid growing speculation about his political future.

The premiers - all of whom are part of Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) - wrote that restoring trust in their party lay in "listening âand taking political action, not in debates âover personnel".

Merz, who has only held the post for 16 months, is facing poor approval ratings while the anti-immigration, far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party is surging, prompting questions about whether he is an electoral liability.

He has vowed to carry on but two more state elections on Sunday have been seen as a key test of his leadership.

Rumours of a "Kanzlertausch" - or "Chancellor swap" - have been around for months, but they have increased since the conservative CDU tumbled to a distant second behind the AfD in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt at the start of September.

The AfD shot up to 43.8% of the vote while the CDU plummeted to 17.2%, marking the first time since World War Two that a far-right party has come close to controlling a German state.

It is still three seats short of an outright majority and the major parties would not enter into a coalition with the AfD, though it could seek to form a minority government.

Merz came out fighting after the loss, describing the AfD - which wants to rebuild ties with Russia - as a "destructive force" whose migration policy amounted to an "ethnic cleansing" of skilled workers.

The AfD responded to his remarks by saying it was filing a defamation complaint against the chancellor over what it described as "baseless" and "disgusting" claims.

The chancellor's abrasive communication style and personal unpopularity - with just 14% thinking he is right for the job, according to a recent Bild poll - have raised questions about his viability as leader of both Germany and the CDU.

The CDU's eight state premiers wrote, however, that "now more than ever, â Germany's political landscape needs stability".

"Our country will continue to need a stable and effective federal government with its own majority in the Bundestag [German parliament]," said the leaders of Schleswig-Holstein, Saxony, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia, Berlin and North Rhine-Westphalia.

World.title: Saudi Arabia says it shot down Houthi drone south of Mecca
World.content:
The Houthis have recently seized control of large swathes of Yemen's Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed pro-government forces.

Last week, they captured the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the southern gateway to a key shipping route that links Asia and Europe via the Red Sea and the Suez canal.

The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping but reiterated that they would target vessels from Saudi Arabia, which has relied on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

At the same time, Saudi Arabia's key East-West Pipeline, which was being used to transfer crude oil from the Gulf to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, had to be closed after it was badly damaged in a strike that the kingdom blamed on Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

Some experts have said it could take more than a month to repair the pipeline, but US Energy Secretary Chris Wright predicted on Tuesday that oil should be flowing through it within days.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the country's de facto ruler, has personally pressed US President Donald Trump to take military action against the Houthis, two sources familiar with the matter told CBS News, the BBC's US media partner.

Trump has so far declined to involve the US military directly, offering instead to assist with intelligence and targeting support, the sources said.

A senior Trump administration official told the BBC: "We are in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen government regarding regional stability."

The United Nations Security Council held an emergency meeting on Tuesday, during which both Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia called for more decisive action against the Houthis, who they accused of choking the Bab al-Mandab Strait as a way of applying economic pressure.

Council members agreed that freedom of navigation in the Red Sea must be maintained to prevent disruption to global supply chains.

More than 90,000 people have been displaced in Yemen by the fighting between the Houthis and pro-government forces, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

"Families are being forced to flee for the second or third time in this conflict, with almost nothing left," Amy Pope, the IOM's director general, warned last week.

The World Health Organization (WHO) said on Sunday that at least 500 people had been reported killed since the start of August, including 297 over the previous week.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

World.title: Charlie Kirk's family alleges 'stunning failures' by Utah officials led to his assassination
World.content:
Charlie Kirk's family has accused the Utah Valley University and state officials of "stunning failures and reckless decisions" that they say led to the conservative activist's 2025 assassination during a campus event.

In a legal notice, lawyers for the family say Kirk's Turning Point USA event at the university campus was not properly secured or monitored, making him an easy target.

Kirk, 31, was speaking to a crowd of thousands on the university campus, when he was shot and killed by a gunman positioned on a roof.

The university said it was aware of the claim but did not comment further on the allegations, according to a statement shared with the BBC's US partner CBS News.

"We are aware of the notice of claim. UVU addresses legal matters consistent with our established processes, " the university said in its statement. "Our focus remains on supporting our campus community."

The legal notice was filed on 9 September, a day ahead of the one-year anniversary of Kirk's death, and is typically a precursor to a lawsuit.

It names Utah Valley University, local police, the state of Utah, and other university officials as parties who were allegedly aware of the threats against Kirk and did not take steps to protect him.

"Through a series of stunning failures and reckless decisions, the UVU Parties created a foreseeable danger to Charlie," the notice alleges.

"Placing a politically controversial figure like Charlie Kirk in an outdoor event in the quad surrounded by tall buildings and other elevated observation platforms is accurately described as walking him into a fishbowl," it says.

Kirk's family alleges the university failed to conduct a meaningful security assessment ahead of the event, failed to assign enough police officers, and did not have an ambulance available on site.

The family also alleges the university ignored warnings about securing the rooftops surrounding the courtyard where Kirk was speaking.

"The risk of a rooftop shooter should have been especially top-of-mind given the attempted assassination of President Trump, Charlie Kirk's close friend and political ally, by a rooftop shooter the previous year," the family's attorney D Loren Washburn wrote in the court filing.

Tyler Robinson, a 23-year-old man from Utah, who has been accused of shooting Kirk from a roof, is due to appear in court next month to hear the date of his trial.

Robinson denies aggravated murder, a capital offence in the state, as well as six other charges.

Prosecutors have called for the death penalty.

World.title: Journalist and pilot among three killed after news helicopter crashes in LA
World.content:
Photojournalist Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw have been named as being among three people killed after an NBC Los Angeles helicopter crashed in the city's suburbs, the station has confirmed.

NBC Los Angeles said its NewsChopper4, which also operated for Telemundo 52, was in the area on Tuesday reporting on a deadly bus crash which killed two people.

Fire officials said an unidentified pedestrian was also killed, and two others were taken to hospital.

Tributes, including from the local news community, have started to come in led by the station's hosts, who called the victims "valued friends and colleagues". One CBS editor said their "hearts are shattered".

World.title: FG commissions 3MW hybrid mini-grid project in Abuja varsity
World.content:
The Federal Government of Nigeria commissioned a three-megawatt hybrid mini-grid project and a Renewable Energy Workshop and Training Centre at Yakubu Gowon University (formerly University of Abuja) on Wednesday.

The project was commissioned under Phase 2 of the Energising Education Programme (EEP), which encompasses seven universities and two teaching hospitals, including institutions in Maiduguri and Calabar. The initiative is currently in the implementation stage of Phase 3.

The Yakubu Gowon University installation features a 3.3 MWp solar array with 3MW of AC output capacity and 2 MWh of battery storage to support critical loads after solar hours. It also includes a dedicated grid connection to serve non-critical demand outside daylight periods.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, praised the Rural Electrification Agency (REA) Board, led by Ayodele Fayose, and its management, headed by Abba Abubakar Aliyu, for their leadership in driving sustained investments to improve Nigerians’ lives.

The minister commended the project, noting that it will benefit 58,726 students and that its 388 streetlights will enhance campus illumination and security.

He further observed that electrifying the university will strengthen research, reduce reliance on diesel generators, and ease pressure on institutional budgets.

“This connection between infrastructure and human capability is central to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Under his leadership, investment in electricity is being directed towards services and productive activities that improve people’s lives.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This sustained investment is a testament to this administration’s constancy of purpose. Continuing a national programme through successive phases, bringing projects to completion, and preparing the next phase reflects the discipline that development requires. For the young people who depend on these institutions, that continuity matters. It means that the commitment to their future remains active beyond any single project or ceremony,” he said.

Addressing the sustainability of the facility, the Minister urged students to take ownership of the infrastructure and report any acts of vandalism.

He also disclosed that the government is establishing a national call centre to receive and resolve electricity complaints nationwide.

“The promise of this investment now places a responsibility on all of us to preserve it. I expect the student community to support our ongoing efforts to stem the tide of vandalism. I therefore charge all of you to report any such act whenever you see it, not just on this solar system, but on other power assets such as transformers and transmission towers.”

“My office is working on a call centre where electricity complaints across the country can be lodged and resolved. This initiative will provide sustainable job opportunities for our youth nationwide. In addition, we plan to provide a dedicated channel where vandalism of critical assets can be reported for immediate action and remediation. We are also working through a joint team of the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, and the EFCC to curb the vandalism of electricity assets across the country,” the Minister added.

In his remarks, the Managing Director of the REA, Abba Aliyu, stated that the true value of the EEP lies not merely in megawatts but in functional laboratories, reduced budgetary pressure, and safer learning environments.

He charged the University governing council to ensure the project remains productive and beneficial to the University community long after the commissioning.

“Over the years, the EEP has taught us that when you build, you have to think about what happens five years from now and whether the investment will continue to create value into the future.”

“The Renewable Asset Management Company (RAMCO) is our solution. We must now become rigorous about asking how we protect and preserve the value of what we have built. RAMCO addresses this sustainability challenge. It recognises that building and managing infrastructure are two distinct responsibilities, and that modern renewable energy is decentralised. The Federal Government has created a platform to manage, monitor, maintain and optimise assets over time. RAMCO cannot survive alone; it requires the support of all stakeholders in shared stewardship. The ultimate value of this project will depend not only on what we have installed, but on how well it is sustained,” the REA MD said.

Mr Aliyu added that beyond the mini-grid, the agency established a Renewable Energy Workshop and Training Centre (WTC) to build local technical capacity.

He encouraged the university to turn the facility into a research hub for distributed energy resources, challenging the institution to pioneer new academic courses, drive technological innovation, and push the technical boundaries of the installation.

He also revealed that the EEP has so far delivered over 100MW of power across 22 federal institutions and university teaching hospitals, while thanking the Minister for his continuous support in ensuring energy investments deliver tangible benefits to Nigerians.

Also speaking, the Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University, Akinwunmi Fawehinmi, emphasised that the institution cannot effectively teach, conduct research, or provide a conducive learning environment without reliable electricity.

He praised the Federal Government for its coordinated intervention, stating that the project directly addresses the university’s energy needs, and pledged that the management will ensure the facility is fully utilised and meticulously maintained.

Commending the REA leadership, the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Power, Enyinnaya Abaribe, hailed Abba Aliyu for the project, noting that it is critical to improving the quality of education nationwide.

He also applauded the establishment of RAMCO, stating that sustainability is key to ensuring that projects continue to benefit Nigerians long after commissioning.

World.title: Tinubu mourns veteran actor Olu Jacobs
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the passing of veteran Nollywood actor and film executive Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, who passed away at age 84 on Wednesday.

After his training at London’s Royal Academy of Dramatic Arts, Olu Jacobs built a career in British television and international film before returning home to Nigeria, where he became a major force in the film industry.

He won major industry honours and awards for his pioneering work and was also conferred with the title of Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR).

President Tinubu described the late Olu Jacobs as one of Nigeria’s most distinguished actors and a towering figure whose remarkable career spanned theatre, television and film globally.

The president acknowledged his contributions to the development and professionalisation of Nigeria’s entertainment industry, stating that the late Jacobs inspired generations of actors and filmmakers through his exceptional talent, discipline and dedication to his craft.

President Tinubu also praised the late actor’s remarkable ability to bring depth, dignity, and authenticity to the characters he portrayed, earning him admiration in Nigeria and beyond.

“He was a giant of the Nigerian creative industry. His passing is a great loss to Nigeria, the African film industry and the global community of lovers of the performing arts. His remarkable body of work will continue to speak to generations yet unborn.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The nation recognises the enormous contributions of Nigeria’s creative practitioners to the country’s cultural identity, global image and economic development. Olu Jacobs played a big role in creating this identity,” the President says.

The president condoled with the bereaved family, particularly his wife and veteran actress, Chief Joke Silva, their children, relatives, colleagues in the Nigerian film industry, and the entire creative community, over the loss of the celebrated thespian.

He prayed for the repose of his soul.

World.title: How my decision delayed telcos’ entry into Nigeria’s financial space — Sanusi Lamido
World.content:
Former Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Governor, Sanusi Lamido Sanusi, has admitted that he would have made some decisions differently during his tenure, particularly his decision to delay the entry of telecommunications companies into Nigeria’s financial services sector.

Mr Sanusi, who is the Emir of Kano, said he was responsible for delaying the entry of telcos into the financial services space, a decision he now believes limited the pace of financial inclusion.

The monarch made the disclosure during a fireside chat on financial inclusion in Abuja on Wednesday, when asked what he would do differently if given another opportunity to lead the CBN.

Mr Sanusi said he could identify three areas where he would have acted differently, but disclosed only one of them during the discussion.

“One of them was on financial inclusion. I’m responsible for delaying the entry of telcos into this space,” he said.

Mr Sanusi served as CBN governor from 2009 until his suspension in February 2014. During his tenure, he oversaw major reforms of Nigeria’s banking sector following the 2009 banking crisis.

Telcos Delay

Mr Sanusi explained that his decision was influenced by concerns arising from Nigeria’s banking crisis at the time, particularly over the regulation and control of funds.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Part of the challenge, of course, was that we had just come out of a banking crisis, where we were worried about illicit funds. And I wasn’t comfortable allowing companies that I was not the primary regulator of to have access to a huge pool of funds,” he said.

He acknowledged, however, that the decision, despite being based on concerns he considered valid at the time, ultimately had unintended consequences.

“So again, this is one case where you have a good intention, where you take a wrong decision,” Mr Sanusi said.

He said he opposed the proposal despite pressure from stakeholders in the financial sector.

“I fought the World Bank. I fought everybody. I fought Stanbic. I fought everybody who suggested it,” he said.

With the benefit of hindsight, however, Mr Sanusi said allowing telecommunications companies into financial services earlier could have accelerated financial inclusion.

“I do think if I had allowed that to happen, we would have made much more progress,” he said.

According to him, telcos have an advantage over traditional banks due to their extensive nationwide reach.

“I think we made more progress in the last few years than we did in the first because the banks simply don’t have the boots on the ground. They don’t have the footprints to do it,” he said.

Beyond financial access

Mr Sanusi’s reflection came during a broader discussion on how Nigeria can move from simply expanding access to financial services to ensuring that financial inclusion produces tangible economic benefits for households.

He argued that financial institutions alone could not create economic prosperity, saying appropriate fiscal and structural policies must support financial-sector reforms.

“We have the infrastructure. We have the base. The question is, how do you now build on that?” he asked.

He also called on the CBN to leverage data generated by fintech and payment companies to develop savings, pension and insurance products for underserved Nigerians.

“If I were in the Central Bank today, I would call in MoneyPoint and OPay and say, ‘Guys, you have all this data. You are transferring money. Tell me how you can build pension products on top of this. How can you build savings for us on top of this?’”

Mr Sanusi said the extensive reach of payment companies could be used to connect low-income Nigerians to financial products, particularly savings and insurance.

He also stressed the importance of financial literacy, saying Nigerians should be encouraged to build savings gradually through small, regular contributions.

Regulatory coordination

The former CBN governor also called for better coordination among Nigeria’s financial regulators, particularly in consumer protection.

He expressed concern about potential overlaps between the CBN’s consumer protection functions and those of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC).

According to him, consumers could become confused when different regulators have overlapping responsibilities for complaints involving financial institutions.

He suggested that regulators should establish a clear responsibility matrix defining their respective roles.

“Draw a RACI matrix and let everybody know where their lines of responsibility are,” he said.

Mr Sanusi said consumer protection was critical to financial inclusion and that regulatory fragmentation could undermine confidence in the financial system.

He disclosed that while he had identified three things he would have done differently during his tenure as CBN governor, he would leave the other two for his forthcoming book.

“Now, the other two, you’ll have to wait for my book,” he said.

World.title: Sterling Holdings appoints Jaiyeola, Ikwudinma as Sterling Bank’s directors
World.content:
Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc has appointed two independent non-executive directors, Laoye Jaiyeola and Chinedu Ikwudinma, to the board of Sterling Bank Ltd, a subsidiary of the company.

The appointments were announced in a regulatory filing signed by Sunny Kanabe, the company secretary, on Wednesday, which noted that the Central Bank of Nigeria has approved them.

The company also disclosed the retirement of the bank’s directors following the expiration of their respective tenures.

The directors are Michael Ajukwu, who is retiring as an Independent Non-Executive Director; Olusola Oworu, who is retiring as an Independent Non-Executive Director; and Olaitan Kajero, who is retiring as a Non-Executive Director.

Also, Tunde Adeola is retiring as an Executive Director of the bank upon reaching the prescribed retirement age for Executive Directors.

“The Board expresses its sincere appreciation to the retiring Directors for their dedication, leadership and valuable contributions to the growth of the Bank and wishes them continued success in all their future endeavours,” the company said.

Profiles, Laoye Jaiyeola

Mr Jaiyeola’s appointment as an Independent Non-Executive Director of Sterling Bank Ltd will be effective from 17 August.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He is a seasoned board leader, financial strategist and policy advocate with over 35 years of experience spanning financial services, corporate governance and public policy in Nigeria. He is the Founder and Pro-Chancellor of Hillside University of Science and Technology (HUST).

Mr Jaiyeola has held key leadership positions in the financial sector that have strengthened Nigeria’s banking and capital markets.

He served as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Kakawa Discount House Limited (now Quest Merchant Bank), where he contributed to the development and stability of Nigeria’s financial markets.

Before joining Kakawa Discount House, Mr Jaiyeola spent nearly two decades with the Central Bank of Nigeria, where he held various positions.

He has also held several prominent leadership and board positions, including President of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), where he contributed to policy dialogue and initiatives to improve Nigeria’s business environment.

He currently sits on the Board of FMDQ Group Plc, the NESG Advisory Board and the Policy Innovation Centre.

Mr Jaiyeola holds a Bachelor’s degree in Economics from Obafemi Awolowo University, a Master’s degree in Banking and Finance from the University of Lagos, and an MBA from Bangor University.

He is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria and the Chartered Institute of Directors, as well as a Chartered Member of the Chartered Banker Institute, Scotland.

He is also a Senior Executive Fellow of Harvard Kennedy School.

Chinedu Ikwudinma

Chinedu Ikwudinma was also appointed as an Independent Non-Executive Director of Sterling Bank Ltd, effective 20 August.

Mr Ikwudinma possesses over three decades of international banking and financial services experience, with expertise spanning risk management, corporate and investment banking, commercial banking, transaction banking, strategic leadership and governance across African and global markets.

He recently served as Group Chief Risk Officer of Ecobank Transnational Incorporated, with enterprise-wide responsibility for risk management and internal controls across the Group’s banking affiliates and other non-bank financial entities.

He previously served as Group Chief Credit Officer, where he played a key role in maintaining strong asset quality and risk management standards.

Before his time at Ecobank, Mr Ikwudinma spent over two decades with Citibank, holding senior leadership positions across Nigeria, Zambia and Uganda.

He served as Managing Director and CEO of Citibank Uganda and as an Executive Director and Country Risk Manager for Citibank Nigeria, overseeing a multibillion-dollar credit portfolio.

READ ALSO: Sterling HoldCo appoints two directors to board

He also held senior roles in corporate and investment banking, commercial banking and regional business management.

Mr Ikwudinma was the pioneer Managing Director of Nova Merchant Bank Limited. He currently serves as the Chairman of CS&C Associates Limited.

He holds a Bachelor of Engineering (Civil Engineering) degree from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka; an M.Sc. in Structural Engineering and an MBA in Finance from the University of Lagos; and a Diploma in French from Alliance Française, Paris, through its Lagos programme.

Mr Ikwudinma is a Fellow of the Nigerian Institute of Credit Administration (FICA) and a Member of the Institute of Directors (MIoD).

Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc is a leading Nigerian financial services group committed to enriching lives through innovation and impact.

Its portfolio includes Sterling Bank Limited, The Alternative Bank Limited, and SterlingFI Wealth Management, among other businesses.

World.title: 2027: Ex-VON DG asks Tinubu to ignore APC governors’ concerns, embrace Wike’s Rainbow Coalition
World.content:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Osita Okechukwu, has urged President Bola Tinubu to embrace the Rainbow Coalition being promoted by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, ahead of the 2027 elections.

Mr Okechukwu, a former director-general of the Voice of Nigeria (VON), alleged that some APC governors were pretending to support Mr Tinubu’s re-election but lacked the capacity to mobilise voters in their states.

He made the claim in a statement on Wednesday in Abuja.

“To the best of my knowledge, some of these Few Pretender Governors FPGs have wittingly or unwittingly used their electorates and recklessly abandoned them, and now want Mr President to dump Wike,” he said.

Mr Okechukwu argued that the governors should have addressed their concerns about the coalition through the party’s internal mechanisms rather than publicly opposing it.

“In my 48 years of participation in Nigerian party politics, I have never seen where such an elementary issue was pretentiously thrown open. May I ask the FPGs: don’t you have access to Mr President, and what is the proverbial caucus meant for?. My summation is simple: Mr President, beware of pretenders,” he said.

The formation of the coalition has generated disagreements between Mr Wike and governors of the ruling APC over allegations that the minister is using the platform to support politicians who lost the APC’s primaries and are now contesting elections on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Progressive Governors Forum (PGF), the union of the APC governors, chaired by the Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, had opposed any political coalition or alliance that could threaten the chances of the party and its candidates in the 2027 elections.

Mr Uzodimma, who is also the secretary of the Tinubu Campaign Council, said aligning with such a political arrangement could undermine Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid and weaken the APC ahead of the elections.

Mr Wike, in response, said he had never promised that the PDP would not field candidates in the 2027 elections. He also urged the governors to pay greater attention to Mr Tinubu’s re-election campaign than they did during the 2023 election.

The PDP has also publicly expressed support for Mr Wike to continue using the coalition to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu’s second term, despite the party having its own presidential candidate, Sandy Onor.

Amid the disagreement, the APC national leadership has not publicly taken a position on whether it supports Mr Wike’s coalition, leaving observers to wonder how the party will manage the dispute between the minister and the governors.

Wike’s electoral value

Mr Okechukwu urged President Tinubu not to disregard Mr Wike’s efforts to mobilise support for his re-election, referencing the minister’s role in the 2023 election.

“Truly, it is not improper for Mr President to dump Wike after we harvested the Wike masquerade, which not only boosted our great party’s votes in 2023, but also denied His Excellency Atiku Abubakar substantial votes and will mobilise voters in states where the FPGs had alienated the electorate by personalising power,” he said.

He argued that allowing Mr Wike to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu does not amount to disregarding the APC governors, but could serve as an additional strategy for securing votes in the 2027 election.

“Mr President has never overlooked the governors. All he wants is supplementary votes from Wike, especially in states where the electorate is angry and where some of the FPGs have alienated the people.

“The governors should therefore concentrate on strengthening their relationship with the electorate rather than asking Mr President to abandon a political alliance that could broaden the APC’s electoral reach,” Mr Okechukwu stated.

World.title: Airlines blame airport congestion, weather for flight delays
World.content:
Nigerian airlines have attributed a significant share of flight delays and cancellations to airport congestion, inadequate infrastructure and adverse weather, saying some disruptions occur outside their control.

The operators, however, acknowledged that airlines are responsible for delays within their control and said passengers should also understand their rights when disruptions occur.

They spoke on Tuesday during the Aviation Day of the 23rd Akwaaba African Travel Market in Lagos, themed “Delayed and Cancelled Flights: The Rules and the Rights of Passengers — The Airline Perspective.”

The discussion comes amid growing concerns over flight disruptions in Nigeria.

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) recorded 7,961 domestic flights in August, of which 4,765 were delayed, and 36 were cancelled.

More than 600 of the delays lasted at least two hours, with 407 lasting between two and three hours and 235 lasting more than three hours.

Air Peace recorded 1,330 delays from 1,864 flights, while United Nigeria Airlines recorded 943 delays from 1,231 flights.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The figures have renewed scrutiny of how airlines plan their schedules and handle passengers when flights are disrupted.

Airlines defend delays

Speaking on the issue, the Chief Commercial Officer of United Nigeria Airlines, Adedayo Olawuyi, said it would be misleading to attribute all delays to airlines without considering conditions at airports and other factors affecting flight operations.

Mr Olawuyi compared airport congestion to having several vehicles competing for a single parking space.

He said an aircraft could be ready to depart at its scheduled time but remain on the ground because other aircraft were occupying the ramp or waiting to use the runway.

“Sometimes that’s what we face because of congestion at the airport,” he said.

According to him, an aircraft scheduled to push back at 6:59 a.m. could end up taking off more than 30 minutes later due to congestion, even though the airline had done what was required of it.

He said airlines also faced technical problems that required aircraft to be taken out of service until the faults were resolved.

“We operate machines. Have you ever woken up, and your car did not start? Sometimes we have technical challenges,” he added.

Mr Olawuyi said safety considerations meant airlines could not release an aircraft for service until necessary checks and repairs had been completed.

Weather, he added, could further compound delays.

He cited a recent United Nigeria flight from Lagos to Kano that was delayed due to bad weather in Kano.

The flight eventually departed Lagos at about 10:30 p.m., but when it approached Kano, a thunderstorm affected the runway lighting, preventing the aircraft from landing.

The aircraft returned to Lagos and landed at about 1 a.m., he said.

“That’s not the fault of the airline,” he noted.

Mr Olawuyi also said many Nigerian airports had limited night operating capabilities, meaning that delays earlier in the day could eventually result in cancellations when operations extended into the night.

Airlines question NCAA delay figures

Reacting to the NCAA data showing that about 60 per cent of domestic flights were delayed in August, Mr Olawuyi said the figures should distinguish between delays within an airline’s control and those caused by external factors.

“I will use an analogy. You go to school, and 60 per cent of the students fail. Is that the fault of the school?” he asked.

He said the data would provide a clearer picture if controllable and uncontrollable delays were separated.

“When you remove the controllable delays, and you have a high number of 60 per cent, then you can say the problem is the airlines.”

Mr Olawuyi argued that responsibility for flight disruptions should not be placed solely on airlines, saying airports, regulators and other operators within the aviation system also contribute to the conditions under which flights are operated.

His comments come shortly after the NCAA raised concerns about airlines’ operational capacity amid widespread delays.

At meetings with airlines in September, the NCAA Director-General of Civil Aviation, Capt. Chris Najomo questioned whether some carriers were operating schedules beyond their available aircraft and crew.

The regulator has also stressed that while delays and cancellations may occur for reasons beyond an airline’s control, carriers remain responsible for complying with passenger protection requirements during such disruptions.

Passenger rights

Mr Olawuyi also spoke about airlines’ obligations to passengers during disruptions.

He said passengers should understand the protections available to them under the NCAA’s passenger protection regulations, while airlines also expect travellers to cooperate during disruptions.

“Passengers should know that their rights protect them,” he said.

He explained that passengers are entitled to refreshments when a domestic flight is delayed for the applicable period and that airlines have obligations to assist passengers during prolonged disruptions.

He also urged passengers to check airline messages for updates, arrive on time and use online check-in where available.

“When there are challenges, we expect you to remain calm,” he said.

Under NCAA Part 19, airlines are required to provide specific assistance during qualifying delays and cancellations, including refreshments and communication after two hours of a domestic delay, while longer disruptions may trigger reimbursement, re-routing, accommodation or compensation depending on the circumstances.

The regulations also distinguish between disruptions caused by circumstances within an airline’s control and extraordinary circumstances beyond its control.

This distinction has become increasingly important as airlines defend their performance against the rising number of delays recorded by the NCAA.

ValueJet cites airport congestion

The Chief Commercial Officer of ValueJet, Trevor Henry, also attributed many delays to airport congestion and operational bottlenecks.

He cited presidential movements, weather, check-in congestion, security checks, and crowded boarding gates as factors that can slow operations.

According to him, congestion can continue even after passengers have boarded and the aircraft is ready to depart.

“When the aircraft taxis to the runway, especially in the morning, there can also be congestion from the taxiway to the runway before takeoff,” he said.

Airport operator proposes slot system

The Chief Operating Officer of the Murtala Muhammed Airport 2 (MMA2), Remi Jibodu, proposed better coordination of flight schedules to reduce congestion at peak periods.

He said thousands of passengers arriving at the airport around the same time could create avoidable pressure on airport facilities.

Mr Jibodu said it was not unusual for more than 10 airlines to schedule flights around 7 a.m., creating congestion at check-in points, boarding areas, taxiways and runways.

“What we can do then is to have a coordinated system,” he said.

He proposed that airlines and airport operators consider staggering departure times rather than having several carriers attempt to operate at the same peak period.

“The truth is that at this point, we have to look at the slot system to see how we can coordinate it. It may not be a full slot system, but we must be able to give a little bit of concession to that,” Mr Jibodu said.

World.title: CBN begins work on new financial inclusion strategy, targets deeper access
World.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) says it has commenced work on the National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 4.0, with the regulator seeking to move beyond expanding access to financial services to ensuring meaningful usage, affordability, safety and improved financial health.

This was disclosed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, while delivering his remarks at the launch of the 2026 Access to Financial Services (A2F) Survey Report in Abuja on Wednesday.

The event was organised by the Enhancing Financial Inclusion and Advancement (EFInA) under the theme: “Access, Opportunity, Growth: Advancing Financial and Economic Inclusion for all Nigerians”.

Mr Cardoso, who was represented by Aisha Isa-Olatinwo, CBN’s Director, Consumer Protection and Financial Inclusion, said the review of the country’s NFIS 3.0 had been completed, and that work had begun on the next phase.

“Within this stability and resilience framework, the CBN is advancing a new generation of inclusion reforms. The review of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 3.0 has been completed, and work has begun on NFIS 4.0, which will raise the way we take financial inclusion to another level,” the CBN said.

The bank said the emerging strategy would adopt an integrated, data-driven, and accountable framework to address gaps in Nigeria’s financial system.

According to the CBN, the approach would shift the focus from broad access targets to responsible inclusion, with greater emphasis on consumer protection, trust and digital financial safety.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The regulator said it would also move from fragmented information to shared intelligence and strengthen subnational delivery of financial inclusion initiatives.

Financial inclusion

The CBN said the 2023 A2F Survey recorded progress in financial inclusion, with total financial inclusion rising to 74 per cent from 64 per cent in 2020.

Formal financial inclusion also increased to 64 per cent from 56 per cent, while financial exclusion declined to 26 per cent.

The bank attributed the gains to the expansion of digital payments and agent banking, improvements in identity infrastructure, risk-based customer due diligence, financial education, regulatory innovation and collaboration among stakeholders.

However, it acknowledged that significant gaps remain.

“Rural communities remain more excluded than urban communities. Regional gaps persist, and women continue to face a significant inclusion gap,” the bank said.

It also noted that credit, insurance, pensions and other financial products capable of building long-term resilience remained underutilised.

“The policy challenge before us is therefore no longer simply to open accounts or expand access points. It is to ensure meaningful usage, affordability, reliability, safety, trust and measurable improvements in financial health,” the CBN said.

Geospatial mapping

The regulator said it plans to undertake geospatial mapping of financial access points to create a national repository showing where financial services exist, where gaps remain and how payment channels perform.

It said the initiative would combine location, institutional, operational and transaction information to support risk-based supervision, evidence-based policymaking and targeted investment in underserved communities.

The CBN also highlighted efforts to improve women’s access to finance through the Women’s Entrepreneurship Finance Code, implemented in collaboration with the Bank of Industry and the Development Bank of Nigeria.

It said the initiative promotes senior-level accountability, gender-disaggregated data and concrete measures to expand financing for women-owned micro, small and medium enterprises.

BVN, agent networks

The bank also disclosed that Bank Verification Number enrollment had reached 67.8 million by the end of 2025, while the agent network supported through the Shared Agent Network Expansion Facility had exceeded 2 million agents.

It said the SabiMoni financial literacy programme was also being used to engage communities and equip Nigerians with knowledge to make informed financial decisions, avoid fraud and use financial services responsibly.

The CBN stressed that effective mechanisms for resolving consumer complaints must accompany increased access.

It said it had deployed a redesigned complaints-management system and was upgrading it into a unified complaints-tracking system that would give the regulator real-time online visibility of complaints in the banking sector.

Price stability and inclusion

The regulator linked its financial inclusion agenda to its broader monetary and financial-sector reforms, arguing that financial inclusion cannot thrive amid persistent macroeconomic instability.

It said high inflation erodes household purchasing power, weakens savings and increases the cost of credit, with disproportionate effects on low-income and underserved Nigerians.

The CBN said exchange-rate volatility also complicates business planning, discourages investment and increases the cost of essential inputs.

“Restoring price stability and confidence is therefore not separate from financial inclusion. It is fundamental to it,” the bank said.

The CBN governor added that since 2024, it had refocused on its core mandate of monetary and price stability, while strengthening monetary-fiscal coordination and liquidity management.

The bank also said it was transitioning towards an inflation-targeting framework, which it described as a forward-looking approach that places price stability at the centre of monetary policy while strengthening transparency and accountability.

Responsible innovation

The CBN said technologies and regulatory reforms, including open banking, regulatory sandboxes, digital identification, interoperable payments and improved credit infrastructure, could lower costs and broaden access to financial services.

However, it warned that safeguards must accompany innovation.

“But innovation must serve people. It must be secure, transparent and supported by appropriate safeguards, particularly for those who are new to formal finance or vulnerable to fraud, data misuse and unfair practices,” it said.

The regulator called on financial institutions, fintechs, payment service providers, telecommunications operators, identity-management agencies, development partners, civil-society organisations and researchers to deepen collaboration on financial inclusion.

It said the ultimate objective was to build a financial system in which Nigerians could save securely, make and receive payments efficiently, obtain responsible credit, protect themselves against risks, build assets and participate productively in the economy.

The CBN said the findings of the 2026 A2F Survey should guide product design, regulation, supervision, investment, financial education and targeted interventions.

“We must use disaggregated data by gender, age, income, location, disability status and enterprise profile to identify gaps, allocate resources and measure outcomes,” it said.

“What gets measured must be acted upon.”

The bank urged stakeholders to use the launch of the 2026 A2F Survey as an opportunity to move “from access to impact, from promises to measurable outcomes, and from financial inclusion to genuine financial well-being and shared prosperity.”

World.title: Team Lagos dominates Southwest zonal elimination ahead of National Sports Festival
World.content:
Team Lagos emerged as the dominant force at the Southwest zonal elimination for the 23rd National Sports Festival, winning four competitions and securing seven podium finishes across five team sports.

The zonal elimination, held from 13 to 16 September, featured teams from Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Osun, Ondo and Ekiti competing for places at the National Sports Festival.

Lagos recorded its strongest performance in volleyball, winning both the men’s and women’s competitions. The state’s men’s basketball team also emerged as champions, while the women’s football team finished top in its category.

The results gave Lagos four first-place finishes and three runner-up positions across the 10 male and female categories contested.

Lagos finished second in women’s basketball, while its men’s and women’s cricket teams also placed second.

The performance puts Lagos in a strong position ahead of the 23rd National Sports Festival in Enugu later this year.

The Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, attributed the results to the state’s approach to talent development and competitive sports.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This performance shows the quality of talent in Lagos and the impact of the work we are putting into athlete development. Our athletes have shown that Team Lagos is ready to compete at the highest level, and we will continue to give them the support they need to succeed.”

Mr Fatodu commended Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu for what he described as his support for sports infrastructure and athlete development.

“We appreciate Governor Sanwo-Olu for his strong commitment to sports. His investment in facilities, programmes and athlete development is creating the platform for our athletes to compete, win and inspire the next generation.”

He said the state’s objective goes beyond medal-winning to developing a system that identifies talent early, develops athletes systematically and creates pathways for sporting careers.

“Our goal is not simply to win competitions. We are building a sustainable pipeline of talent from the grassroots to the elite level. Every medal matters, but what matters even more is that we are creating opportunities for young Lagosians to discover their abilities, develop them and compete with confidence.”

The Southwest result comes as Lagos continues its focus on grassroots sports, talent identification, athlete support and sports infrastructure.

The state’s teams will now begin preparations for the 23rd National Sports Festival in Enugu, with Lagos aiming to build on its performance in the zonal elimination.

World.title: South Africa’s president Ramaphosa falls ill after BRICS summit
World.content:
In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa arrives before the start of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12, 2026. (Photo by Alexander KAZAKOV / POOL / AFP)

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has withdrawn from public engagements after returning from the BRICS summit in India, his office said on Wednesday, citing ill health.

His absence comes as Deputy President Paul Mashatile continues to recover from a minor medical procedure, leaving both of the country’s top leaders away from public duties.

Ramaphosa, 73, returned from the BRICS summit in India on Monday and had been advised by his doctors to rest and recover, the presidency said.

Leaders of the BRICS bloc, which includes Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, concluded a two-day summit in New Delhi on Sunday, where discussions focused on inclusive global growth and the Middle East.

“Where possible, the president has asked the respective ministers to represent him at scheduled engagements,” his office said in a statement.

Mashatile said on Tuesday that his “recovery is progressing well” and that he was “regaining strength each day”.

“On the advice of my doctors, I will continue resting until advised otherwise while work and delegated responsibilities continue to be underway in the capable team in my office with other stakeholders in government, business and other sectors,” Mashatile said.

The simultaneous absence of Ramaphosa and Mashatile comes as South Africa enters an increasingly busy political season ahead of local government elections on November 4.

AFP

World.title: Why FG should write off airlines’ legacy debts – Finchglow GMD
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Finchglow Holdings has urged Federal Government to write off legacy debts incurred by domestic airlines, saying such debts are old and have become doubtful.

Recently, there was a dispute over the non-remittance of the Ticket Sales Charge, TSC, by airlines, following a rise in operational costs and an increase in fuel prices attributed to the United States-Iran crisis.

Subsequently, the Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON, sought relief from federal government, which approved a 30 per cent waiver on the charges.

Speaking at a recent conference in Lagos, Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, said following the presidential waiver, airlines met with the “NCAA and the Minister. We held several meetings. In one decisive meeting, NCAA requested that airline operators pay 10 per cent of the legacy debts within a specified period, and then pay the rest in instalments over a period of time, and each airline was to meet with NCAA’s Director of Finance.”

However, Group Managing Director of Finchglow, Mr Bernard Bankole, who addressed newsmen in Lagos, said federal government should reconsider its position on legacy debts, saying debts that had remained outstanding for years should be written off.

He said: “When you are talking about legacy debts, let us revisit that. It is a basic thing they taught us in accounting. In accounting, you write it off. You cannot continue to carry bad debts that have become doubtful. If we are being forced to reconcile our books and write off, why can’t the government write it off?

“When we’re talking about legacy debts, it means the debt is old. It has become doubtful and should be written off. There’s nothing wrong for a business to file for bankruptcy. Government of Bola Tinubu is different from Muhammadu Buhari. Why are you still chasing something from five, 10 years ago? And you say you want to collect it?

“I’m suggesting that any debt that has been classified as legacy debts should be written off. When you say something is legacy, it means that it is stale. How do you reconcile accounting? Debt of 15 years ago, you are collecting it now.”

Meanwhile, Bankole disclosed that Finchglow Holdings was seeking final approval from the Ogun State government to establish a flying school at Gateway International Airport.

He said: “The moment we get our final approval from Ogun State government, we are going to move into Gateway to start planning how to establish our flying school. We are waiting for them. They have given first-level approval. We are waiting for the final approval so we can start our operations there. We are constantly pushing. The thing about the industry we have found ourselves in is that it is the gateway to any country.

“Our name is still going to go through the NCAA, but we don’t see that as a problem. You know why? Because they have a licence already. This is just going to be an addition to our existing licence. It’s not like they’re starting anything fresh. It’s just going to be one of the courses that they’re taking.

“They will approve the extension. They will come and inspect it. And once they inspect it once, we have a land allocation from Ogun State government. Then the rest is history.”

World.title: Navy hails conviction of nine crude oil thieves
World.content:
The Nigerian Navy has welcomed the conviction of nine persons by the Federal High Court in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for crude oil theft, describing the judgment as a significant development in the fight against economic sabotage.

The nine convicts were sentenced on September 14, 2026, to five years’ imprisonment on Count One and 10 years on Count Two, without the option of a fine, according to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, on Wednesday.

The Navy said its personnel arrested the suspects on February 7, 2026, during an intelligence-led operation while they were allegedly stealing crude oil from an oil wellhead identified as ASABO-D in Ibeno Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State.

It said the conviction demonstrated the importance of effective prosecution and judicial determination in complementing enforcement operations against crude oil theft.

The development comes as the Navy sustains operations against crude oil theft, illegal bunkering and other forms of economic sabotage under Operation DELTA SENTINEL, its anti-crude oil theft operation.

According to the Navy, the operation, launched in January 2026, has dismantled more than 241 illegal refining sites, disrupted criminal networks, recovered over 6.44 million litres of suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined petroleum products, and led to the arrest of more than 230 suspects.

The Service said the operations were aimed at protecting critical national infrastructure and supporting energy security.

It attributed the renewed operational efforts to the leadership of the Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, particularly his emphasis on intelligence-led operations, inter-agency collaboration and enhanced maritime domain awareness.

The Navy said the efforts were also in line with the Federal Government’s policy of increasing crude oil production to 2.5 million barrels per day by 2027.

The Service stressed that successful interdictions would have greater impact when they resulted in timely convictions, which it said would strengthen deterrence against crude oil theft.

The Navy commended the judiciary for the judgment and the Department of State Services for what it described as professionalism in seeing the case through to conclusion.

It also called for accelerated adjudication of pending crude oil theft cases, saying this would strengthen accountability and efforts to protect the country’s oil and gas resources.

The Navy warned individuals, groups and organised criminal networks involved in crude oil theft and related activities to desist, saying the latest conviction showed that perpetrators could not rely on the remoteness of oil-producing communities, waterways or oil installations to evade justice.

It also appealed to law-abiding citizens and host communities to provide credible information on activities threatening critical oil and gas infrastructure.

The Service said it would sustain operations against crude oil theft and other forms of economic sabotage while strengthening collaboration with the judiciary, other security agencies and relevant stakeholders to protect Nigeria’s maritime domain and oil and gas infrastructure.

World.title: Peter Obi urges Nigerians to buy Dangote Refinery shares
World.content:
Peter Obi

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Anambra State governor and presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to invest in the ongoing Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals.

Obi made the call in a post on his official X handle on Wednesday, while expressing his support for the investment and commending Aliko Dangote for the refinery project.

He said many Nigerians at home and in the diaspora had sought his opinion on whether they should invest in the IPO.

“In the course of my engagements with Nigerians at home and in the diaspora, many of them have sought my opinion on investing in the ongoing Dangote Petroleum Refinery Initial Public Offering,” Obi said.

“While encouraging them to buy, I must say that I remain very proud of the commitment and breakthrough of Alhaji Aliko Dangote’s investment in the real sector of our country’s economy, across different sectors.

“This validates my position that we should move Nigeria from consumption to production.”

The Dangote Refinery IPO opened on September 14, offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares valued at N5,250.

The offer, which is expected to raise about N2.15 trillion if fully subscribed, is scheduled to close on October 13, 2026.

Dangote has described the offering as an “IPO for the people”, with the initiative aimed at widening ownership of the refinery among Nigerians and other eligible investors. The company is also targeting millions of shareholders through the public offer.

Obi, who has consistently advocated a shift from consumption to production in Nigeria’s economy, called on other Nigerian businesses to follow Dangote’s example by investing in productive sectors.

“I, therefore, encourage other Nigerian businesses to invest in the productive sectors of the Nigerian economy and also give fellow Nigerian citizens the opportunity to be part of the re-industrialization of the country by offering their shares to the public through public offerings,” he said.

The former governor’s comments come as the Dangote Refinery IPO continues to attract attention from retail investors following its opening on the Nigerian Exchange.

The Securities and Exchange Commission has advised prospective investors to use only officially designated and approved channels for applications and payments relating to the offer and to carefully read the approved prospectus before investing.

The official IPO information states that investing in the shares carries risk, with the value of shares capable of rising or falling after listing and dividends not guaranteed.

World.title: 2027: S’Court reserves judgment in appeal to restore voided portions of Electoral Act
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA — The Supreme Court, on Wednesday, reserved its judgment in an appeal the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) filed to challenge the nullification of portions of the Electoral Act 2026 by the Court of Appeal.

The Abuja Division of the appellate court had, on July 16, struck down sections 77(5), (6) and (7), as well as 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which regulate membership registers of political parties and the procedure for the nomination of candidates for the 2027 general elections.

The court, in a unanimous decision by a three-member panel, held that the sections were inconsistent with provisions of sections 221 and 222 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which give political parties the right to decide whom to sponsor in an election.

The judgment followed an appeal marked CA/ABJ/CV/750/2026, which the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) lodged against the INEC.

The ZLP had gone to the appellate court to challenge the dismissal of a suit it filed to query the constitutionality of some provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 relating to membership registers of political parties and the conduct of primary elections.

Section 77(5) of the Electoral Act stipulates that only persons whose names are contained in the register submitted to INEC not later than 21 days before the date fixed for primaries, congresses or conventions would be eligible to vote.
