Ahora que han comenzado las obras, los esfuerzos se centran en que afecten lo menos posible al día a día de los vecinos. Para ello, la clave es anticipar Jorge Serrano, director técnico de Crea Madrid Nuevo Norte

A juicio de Miguel Hernández, la clave fue “lograr despolitizar la iniciativa y abordarla como un proyecto estratégico de ciudad”. “Entendimos que era necesario abordar una discusión en torno al modelo de ciudad para lograr establecer unos principios en los que todos estuviéramos de acuerdo. Así se entendió y el pleno lo aprobó por unanimidad, algo que no es tan común”.

Con las obras en marcha, la dimensión de Madrid Nuevo Norte ha conseguido reclamar la atención de algunas de las principales capitales del mundo. “Aquí han venido a aprender cómo lo estamos haciendo equipos técnicos de Ámsterdam, París, Corea del Sur, Japón, Estados Unidos... Ciudades y países que son referencias urbanísticas”, cuenta con orgullo Hernández. “A Madrid le faltaba un proyecto con el que la ciudad se sienta absolutamente emocionada. Y trabajamos para que sea este”.

World.title: Soy propietario de un piso en alquiler en Madrid cuyo contrato vence en 2027. ¿Cómo puedo subir el precio? ¿Es mejor no renovarlo?
World.content:
Pregunta. Soy propietario de una vivienda alquilada en una zona no tensionada de la Comunidad de Madrid. El contrato se firmó el 9 de mayo de 2022 y, por tanto vence, en 2027. Los inquilinos pagan puntualmente y la relación es buena y fluida. El precio del alquiler está alrededor de un 20% por debajo del precio de mercado. La consulta es si renuevo el contrato por periodos anuales aplicando el IPC, si renuevo el contrato aplicando un nuevo precio pactado o si, por el contrario y ante la incertidumbre legal, lo más conveniente es comunicar al inquilino que el contrato vence y no voy a renovarlo. En este caso la utilizaría como mi vivienda habitual. A. del Amo.

Respuesta. Según se indica en la consulta, se trata de un contrato de arrendamiento de vivienda habitual que comenzó el 9 de mayo de 2022. En consecuencia, el 9 de mayo de 2027 se cumplirán los cinco años de duración previstos en los artículos 9 y 10 de la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos, momento en el que nace para el arrendador el derecho a no prorrogar el contrato. Para ello, deberá comunicarlo al arrendatario de forma fehaciente con, al menos, cuatro meses de antelación a la finalización de dicho plazo.

Si el objetivo es incrementar la renta por encima de lo que permite el índice pactado entre las partes, será necesario contar con la aceptación del arrendatario. Esta cuestión puede negociarse desde este mismo momento y, en caso de alcanzarse un acuerdo, formalizarse mediante la firma de un anexo al contrato que recoja la modificación de la renta. Conviene recordar que, en las zonas no tensionadas, la determinación de la renta es libre para las partes.

En este proceso de negociación es fundamental no perder de vista la fecha de mayo de 2027. Por ello, si se acerca el vencimiento legal sin que se haya alcanzado un acuerdo, deberá remitirse al arrendatario, con una antelación mínima de cuatro meses al cumplimiento del quinto año, un burofax manifestando la voluntad de no prorrogar el contrato. Si no se envía dicha comunicación y tampoco se firma un anexo modificando la renta, el contrato se prorrogará automáticamente por un plazo adicional de tres años en las mismas condiciones inicialmente pactadas.

La comunicación de la no prórroga permite, además, que el arrendatario se pronuncie expresamente sobre la propuesta planteada. En caso de no alcanzarse un acuerdo, el arrendador podrá destinar la vivienda a uso propio o arrendarla a otras personas.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Qué hacer en Yuste, un enclave con alma europea en el corazón de Extremadura
World.content:
Un viaje para descubrir Cuacos de Yuste, su monasterio y atractivos en los alrededores como Jarandilla. Un rincón en la comarca de La Vera que combina historia, arte y naturaleza con su vocación de promover los valores europeos

Una pequeña villa agrícola extremeña de la comarca de La Vera, Cuacos de Yuste, se convierte cada 9 de mayo, Día de Europa, en una de las capitales de la Unión Europea cuando el rey Felipe VI entrega en la iglesia de su monasterio de san Jerónimo el Premio Europeo Carlos V. Equivalente en prestigio al Premio Carlomagno de Aquisgrán, reconoce desde 1995 a quienes han fomentado el proceso de integración europeo y sus valores culturales e históricos. Por aquí han pasado personajes de la talla de Mijaíl Gorbachov, Angela Merkel, António Guterres o Mario Draghi para recoger el galardón; o, por ser académicos de la Fundación Yuste (Fundación Academia Europea e Iberoamericana de Yuste), Mstislav Rostropóvich, Antonio López, Umberto Eco, José Saramago, Paul Preston, Václav Havel o Edgar Morin.

Dicha fundación, creada en 1992, promueve los Premios Carlos V. Está considerada Organización de Interés Cultural Europeo por contribuir con sus actividades y seminarios a la construcción europea y servir de puente con Iberoamérica, como su campus de verano que siguen alumnos de todo el mundo. También tienen lugar en el monasterio de san Jerónimo de Yuste, incomparable marco con una gran carga simbólica. Entre sus muros murió, en 1558, el último gran emperador del Sacro Imperio Romano Germánico, Carlos V —Carlos I en la línea sucesoria española—, “el último de los herederos de Carlo Magno y el precursor de los federalistas de la Europa de la época moderna”, como dijo, citando a Salvador de Madariaga, el entonces presidente de la Comisión Europea Jacques Delors al recoger su Premio Carlos V en 1995.

Más información La última frontera nazarí: ruta por los castillos y torres vigías de los guardianes de Boabdil

Exterior del monasterio de Yuste, donde murió Carlos V. Around the Corner / Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Empecemos pues nuestra visita a este rincón de la provincia de Cáceres en el monasterio de san Jerónimo de Yuste, Real Sitio del Patrimonio Nacional. Construido en 1402, se halla en una privilegiada zona boscosa que transmite la profunda calma que buscaba Carlos V cuando vino desde los Países Bajos para curar su gota. Lo regentó la Orden de los Jerónimos. De su interior resaltan sus impresionantes y ajardinados claustros: el gótico, del siglo XV, y el renacentista, del XVI, ornado con escudos de armas. La residencia del emperador se empezó a construir adosada al cenobio en 1556 y se acabó a principios de 1557. Muy modesta y austera, la forma un pasillo que separa la antecámara y el dormitorio del comedor y la sala de audiencias; con un mirador sobre los jardines y el estanque en el que pescaba y donde, quizá, contrajo el paludismo. Una abertura en su dormitorio le permitía seguir los oficios religiosos que se celebraban en la iglesia. Sencilla, de una sola nave con bóvedas de crucería, tiene un presbiterio elevado que domina un retablo renacentista con el escudo imperial y una copia del cuadro de Tiziano La Gloria en el que aparece Carlos V con sudario orando junto a su mujer Isabel de Portugal y su hijo Felipe II. Bajo el altar está la cripta en la que fue sepultado hasta 1574 —sus restos reposan hoy en El Escorial—.

La cama del emperador Carlos V en el monasterio de Yuste. Around the Corner / Alamy / CORDON PRESS

En la Guerra de Independencia, los franceses saquearon e incendiaron el monasterio. Su estado se agravó por el abandono provocado por la desamortización, lo que denunció Unamuno en 1908. Empezó a ser rehabilitado en 1942. Hoy viven allí unos monjes paulinos polacos, tras la salida de los Jerónimos en 2009.

Desde el monasterio se puede subir andando por un robledal a la Barrera de Yuste, desde cuyo mirador se disfruta de una impresionante panorámica. Bajamos después a Cuacos, a dos kilómetros del monasterio. En el camino nos encontramos con un sorprendente cementerio militar alemán donde reposan aviadores y marinos de la Primera Guerra Mundial (26) y de la Segunda (154). Tiene la estética de todos los cementerios militares alemanes de la Volksbund Deutsche Kriegsgräberfürsorge (Comisión Alemana de Tumbas de Guerra): cruces de granito oscuro en un prado verde con los nombres, grado y fechas de nacimiento y muerte que revelan la juventud de los allí enterrados. Las tumbas se hallaban diseminadas por España y fueron reagrupadas aquí en 1983. El cementerio anima a reflexionar sobre la importancia que ha tenido la integración europea para evitar nuevas guerras en el continente. Así lo evocaron el canciller alemán Helmut Kohl y la presidenta francesa del Parlamento Europeo Simone Veil —superviviente de un campo de concentración y que perdió a su familia en el Holocausto— al recoger sus respectivos premios Carlos V en 2006 y en 2008.

El cementerio militar alemán en Cuacos de Yuste. Cavan Images / Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Cuacos, situado en la falda de la sierra de Tormantos y el cerro de san Salvador, es Conjunto Histórico —uno de los cinco de La Vera—. Sus callejuelas y plazas están llenas de casas solariegas típicamente veratas, con fachadas de adobe y entramados de madera, en las que se alojó el séquito del emperador. Como las que rodean con sus balconadas y soportales el anfiteatro que ocupa el centro de la ovalada plaza Don Juan de Austria, nombre que recibe porque aquí se halla la Casa de Jeromín que habitó de niño el futuro héroe de Lepanto, hijo ilegítimo de Carlos V. Jeromín tuvo un altercado con los niños del pueblo que lo apedrearon sin saber de quién se trataba —él tampoco sabía que Carlos V era su padre—. Los niños y sus progenitores fueron perdonados por el emperador, por lo que la gente de Cuacos es conocida como “Los perdonaos”. Este episodio, como otros en los que los lugareños distrajeron alguna vaca y truchas del emperador, alimentó una leyenda negra, recogida por viajeros extranjeros, que llevó a Pedro Antonio de Alarcón a no entrar en Cuacos cuando visitó el monasterio en 1873, como cuenta en su libro Viajes por España.

En la plaza Don Juan de Austria también se halla una de las emblemáticas fuentes de Cuacos, bajo un peñasco y una higuera que le da nombre. Bajando por la calle de Entrefuentes se llega a otra fuente, la de la plaza de España, la más grande de La Vera. Centro neurálgico de Cuacos, está en parte porticada con alguna columna de piedra del monasterio. En sus inmediaciones se halla la casa del escribano Rafael Castaño, del siglo XVI, con escudo de armas sobre su puerta de arco de medio punto y bajo una bonita ventana bífora.

La plaza de Don Juan de Austri, en Cuacos. DCarreno ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Cerca de la coqueta plaza de la Fuente de los Chorros, del siglo XV, donde se hallaba la judería, se encuentra la iglesia de Nuestra Señora de la Asunción. Su contundente torre vigía del siglo XIII denota que su origen fue defensivo. Su atractiva portada gótica isabelina lleva a su sobrio interior románico. Alberga un órgano barroco construido en Amberes, procedente del monasterio, y la pequeña talla del venerado san Gil, objeto de un viejo litigio con la vecina Aldeanueva. Se encontraba en una ermita que hubo en los lindes de ambas localidades, en unos terrenos con restos romanos y visigóticos; el conflicto se resolvió quedándose los de Aldeanueva con las tierras y los de Cuacos con la imagen del santo.

Un lugar imprescindible de visitar en los alrededores son las Ollas, un paraje natural con mirador que ofrece la garganta de los Cascarones. Toda la zona, que llega a Aldeanueva y Jarandilla, goza de marmitas de gigante o piscinas naturales excavadas por el agua en la roca, gargantas de formas caprichosas y cascadas rodeadas de bosques, donde relajarse con el rumor de sus gélidas aguas camino del río Tiétar o darse un baño para combatir los rigores estivales, como en la parte llamada “El Bañaero”.

Las Ollas, un paraje natural tallado por la fuerza del agua durante milenios. Manoli Perez ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

No se puede visitar Cuacos sin pasar por Jarandilla, rodeada de verdes montañas, tierra del conquistador Gaspar de Loaysa. Mientras le construían su morada en el monasterio de san Jerónimo, Carlos V vivió entre noviembre de 1556 y febrero de 1557 en el impresionante castillo de los condes de Oropesa, actual Parador Nacional. Conserva las originales murallas, torreones y foso. Merece la pena alojarse en este castillo del siglo XV y tomarse algo en su agradable patio de armas de estilo plateresco. Pero también hay una gran oferta hotelera en toda la zona con confortables hoteles, casas rurales y campings.

El exterior del Parador de Jarandilla de la Vera. robert harding / Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Jarandilla también requiere un paseo por sus viejas callejuelas llenas de casonas y puentes medievales como el Parral. Veremos su picota con tres cabezas de dragones, símbolo de villazgo y lugar de ejecuciones, y la iglesia fortaleza de Santa María de la Torre, del siglo XII. Construida sobre un castro celta, como indica el verraco ubicado en un muro de la torre, su interior alberga una pila bautismal visigoda y una capilla renacentista del siglo XVI.

Este es un lugar idóneo para el tapeo del que ya disfrutaron Carlos V y su séquito en la desaparecida bodega de Pedro Acedo de la Berrueza. Tradición que siguen otros restaurantes donde degustar los caldos y la cocina extremeña, como en un clásico de curioso nombre, Puta Parió, que fue morada del mayordomo del emperador. Hablando de restauración, el pimentón de La Vera es un condimento básico de la gastronomía local, de sus sopas de patata y tomate, caldereta y cuchifrito de cabrito y cochinillo, patatas revolconas, setas, migas veratas, quesos y embutidos. Fueron los monjes de San Jerónimo los que empezaron a desecarlo. También salieron del monasterio otros platos típicos, como el bacalao estilo monacal (con huevo duro, espinacas y patatas), los huevos de vigilia y la trucha en salsa de almendras.

Una terraza donde se está secando pimentón de la Vera en Cuacos de Yuste. geogphotos / Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Otro lugar destacable cerca de Cuacos es la localidad de Garganta la Olla. Además de su iglesia de San Lorenzo con su torre renacentista, encontraremos notables casonas de los siglos XVI y XVII: la del Museo de la Inquisición, donde operó el Santo Oficio durante 228 años; la Casa de las Muñecas, pintada de azul añil y con una mujer esculpida en el arco de granito de la puerta, que sirvió de prostíbulo al séquito imperial; y la de Isabel de Carvajal, la Serrana de La Vera, cuya leyenda inspiró, entre otros, a Lope de Vega, según la cual vengó una desdicha amorosa asesinando hombres después de seducirlos.

La Casa de las Muñecas (el edificio azul), en la localidad de Garganta la Olla. DCarreno ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Planes para senderistas

Toda la zona es ideal para los amantes del senderismo. Se puede hacer la Ruta del Emperador, los 10 kilómetros que siguió desde Jarandilla al monasterio de san Jerónimo porteado en silla de manos o a hombros de los lugareños a causa de la gota. Pasa por Aldeanueva de La Vera, donde se puede contemplar la iglesia de San Pedro y la Fuente de los Ocho Caños, cuyos vecinos llevan con orgullo el nombre de “pencones” que les dio el emperador porque solo le cobraron un penco de vino por llevarle a hombros. El último tramo, desde Cuacos al monasterio, arranca en el monumental conjunto escultórico del mexicano Carlos Terrés dedicado a Carlos V. Es una larga pendiente boscosa conocida como la “ruta del colesterol” porque es habitual cruzarse en ella con personas de cierta edad. La Ruta del Emperador se puede hacer a pie, en bici o a caballo. Es típico andarla en torno al 3 de febrero, cuando se recrea el traslado de 1557 del emperador; toda una fiesta con actuaciones teatrales y musicales.

Memorial de Carlos V en una ruta senderista por Cuacos de Yuste. geogphotos / Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Para senderistas más curtidos, la Ruta de Carlos V, que empieza en Tornavacas, en la cabecera del valle del Jerte, son unos 25 kilómetros. Pasa por robledales y castañares, por los collados de las Losas y de la Encinilla y el Puerto de las Yeguas, por gargantas como la de Serrá, ermitas como la del Cristo del Humilladero y puentes como el de Carlos V.

Estas dos no son las únicas rutas. Se puede hacer senderismo en toda la sierra de Tormantos y en el cerro de San Salvador, donde se halla la ermita homónima en la que, según la leyenda, fueron degollados por los sarracenos varios clérigos y caballeros durante la Reconquista.

En resumen, Cuacos, Jarandilla y sus aledaños son una zona de La Vera en la que impregnarse de historia y espíritu europeísta, pero también donde disfrutar de la calma y el aire puro de sus magníficos paisajes de frondosos bosques que cubren las laderas montañosas y gargantas profundas esculpidas en la roca por el agua, de sus pueblos con encanto y de una sabrosa gastronomía. Por algo vino a estas tierras Carlos V, no a morir, sino a vivir.

World.title: Recorriendo Esposende, un museo moderno al aire libre único en Portugal
World.content:
A orillas del Atlántico, entre pinares, dunas y antiguas casas de veraneo, esta localidad guarda una sorprendente colección de arquitectura moderna. Una ruta permite descubrir las viviendas y edificios que, entre los años cuarenta y setenta, levantaron arquitectos como Viana de Lima, Fernando Távora o Alcino Soutinho

A primera hora de la mañana, el viento empuja restos de niebla para que la playa de Ofir reciba a los primeros bañistas y los tempranos rayos de sol. Ambos nos dan la bienvenida a este enclave atlántico protegido por dunas salvajes que se desvela al caminar sobre pasarelas de madera mientras uno escucha el rumor del alba y de las olas como quien espera a que la luz sea creada. Estamos en Esposende, un pequeño municipio del distrito de Braga, en el estuario del río Cávado, a tan solo media hora en coche de Oporto. Además de por su riqueza natural, Esposende nos reclama por ser la cuna del despegue de la arquitectura del movimiento moderno en Portugal. Hemos venido para realizar la ruta del Modernismo en Esposende o, dicho de otro modo, para entender un capítulo fundamental de la arquitectura portuguesa y, por qué no reconocerlo, visitar un museo al aire libre único en el mundo. El conocido Roteiro modernista cuenta con 18 paradas —entre casas y hoteles— no muy alejadas entre sí, concentradas en Esposende y sus alrededores.

Nuestra primera cita es en Marinhas, en las afueras de Esposende, con Paulo Guerreiro, arquitecto, profesor y artífice de la ruta, que no por casualidad nos espera en la Casa das Marinhas (1954-1957), una de las obras maestras de Alfredo Evangelista Viana de Lima (1913-1991), considerado uno de los pioneros en la introducción de la arquitectura del movimiento moderno en Portugal. Esta casa familiar, concebida como lugar de veraneo es, según Guerreiro, la recepción de ese macromuseo vivo que es la arquitectura racionalista en Esposende.

Más información Cómo atravesar los Alpes en bici sin necesidad de ser un experto ciclista

Atardecer junto al mar en Esposende. robert harding ( Alamy/ CORDON PRESS )

El propio Viana de Lima definió esta casa como “el solar de los tiempos modernos”. Todo empezó con un viejo molino que adquirió el arquitecto, entregado a la pureza de su forma, a partir del cual aplicaría las medidas del Modulor de Le Corbusier en la escala, la forma, la dimensionalidad y los colores. Es, por tanto, una construcción que concentra los preceptos del movimiento moderno y, al mismo tiempo, expresa el equilibrio entre los conceptos de modernidad y tradición, como demuestra el uso de la piedra y su textura rústica en la fachada, esencia de la arquitectura popular portuguesa, que le da un aire regionalista y culturalista. Lo internacional y lo nacional.

El juego de colores de las ventanas remite inevitablemente a la arquitectura y el mobiliario de Charles y Ray Eames, como también el diseño de los Bancos VL que se ven en el interior, mezcla de depuración y artesanía. El jardín trasero refleja el programa modernista y su falsa ventana en el muro imita la de Le Corbusier en la Villa du Lac, en Suiza. El cuerpo cilíndrico del molino funciona como entrada y como acceso al segundo piso a través de una escalera circular. En el primer piso, el espacio es fluido. La cocina, una auténtica Frankfurt Kitchen —la famosa cocina diseñada por Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky en los años veinte para el complejo de vivienda Social Römerstadt de Fráncfort, que supuso una revolución en el modelo de vivienda social—, es un derroche de funcionalidad. La sala de estar, con doble altura y generoso acristalamiento con vistas al mar, a lo lejos, se articula suavemente con la planta superior, donde se encuentran las habitaciones y el estudio del arquitecto.

La Casa das Marinhas, del arquitecto Viana de Lima. Luís Ferreira Alves ( Arquivo Casa da Arquitetura )

Viana de Lima se formó en la Escuela de Bellas Artes de Oporto. Participó en varios CIAM defendiendo los principios expresados en la famosa Carta de Atenas de 1933, bajo la influencia de Le Corbusier. Su enorme currículum incluye varios iconos de la arquitectura portuguesa, como el Complejo Hospitalario de Bragança, la Facultad de Economía de la Universidad de Oporto, la Casa Arístides Ribeiro, el Casino Park Hotel de Funchal —en colaboración con Niemeyer— y, evidentemente, esta Casa das Marinhas, incluida en la selecta red internacional Iconic Houses, cuya misión es identificar y preservar viviendas de relevancia arquitectónica del siglo XX que puedan visitarse. Las visitas, a cargo de Guerreiro, pueden concertarse a través de la web y resultan una experiencia luminosa.

El interior de la Casa das Marinhas. Luís Ferreira Alves (Arquivo Casa da Arquitetura)

A principios del siglo XX, Esposende era un reducto de fortunas: los tornaviagem de Brasil —emigrantes que habían hecho fortuna y volvían— tenían dinero suficiente como para encargar obras a los arquitectos más destacados de entonces, ninguno tan determinante como Miguel Ventura Terra, cuyas aportaciones siguen dando personalidad a Esposende: el Museo Municipal —antiguo Teatro Club—, el Palacete de Valentim Ribeiro da Fonseca —de un art nouveau de manual— o el Hospital de Esposende. Todo ello, siempre bajo el influjo de Raúl Lino, que además de arquitecto publicó libros teóricos en los que defendía la arquitectura popular como La casa portuguesa (1929), Casas portuguesas (1933) y L’évolution de l’architecture domestique au Portugal (1937), que posteriormente se recogieron en un libro de título maravilloso: No es un artista el que quiere serlo. Luego, en los años treinta, la ciudad siguió despertando el interés de las familias adineradas cuyos negocios prosperaban bajo el régimen del Estado Novo, que veraneaban aquí y apostaban por edificios residenciales acordes con los tiempos.

Mientras nos dirigimos a la siguiente parada, Guerreiro explica: “Esto era un lugar ideal para el descanso, ya que estaba cerca del triángulo industrial formado por Oporto, Braga y Guimarães. Hoy es un paisaje único que combina la vegetación, el mar y la luz, y que esconde algunos de los secretos arquitectónicos mejor guardados”.

Secretos como la casa de Pádua Ramos, en la Rua Azevedo Coutinho de Fão, que visitamos de la mano de su hija y que se reconoce por el uso del color amarillo en las persianas. Otra casa de vacaciones con gran dificultad de integración en el tejido urbano, algo que condicionó su aspecto, su color, sus cubiertas y su volumen.

Exterior de la casa de Pádua Ramos. Arquivo Pádua Ramos

El arquitecto Luis Duarte Pádua Ramos nació en Mozambique en 1931 y falleció en Matosinhos en 2005. Se formó en la Escuela de Bellas Artes de Oporto entre 1949 y 1957. En 1955, fue invitado a trabajar en el estudio de arquitectura de José Carlos Loureiro, junto a quien realizaría gran parte de su obra. En todo caso, la influencia de Pádua Ramos es muy expansiva y cabe reseñar, además de su labor como arquitecto, cuánto aportó al diseño industrial y como coleccionista de arte de los siglos XVI al XX, atesorando miles de piezas entre las que destacan joyas, muebles, esculturas, cerámicas y pinturas de célebres firmas como Ruhlmann o Lalique —el refinamiento del art déco—, Braque o Dalí.

La casa de Fão condensa bien esa triple función y demuestra cómo Pádua Ramos —responsable de edificios de Oporto que forman parte de la memoria sentimental de la ciudad, como el Hotel Dom Henrique— representa ese momento en el que la arquitectura portuguesa empieza a liberarse de la ortodoxia del movimiento moderno y se abre a un lenguaje mucho más libre, casi lúdico. Ello se percibe claramente en la atención al diseño de interiores, a los objetos y al mobiliario, que se inscribe en la posmodernidad y que a veces roza lo kitsch.

El día precisa de una parada técnica para restaurarnos con un delicioso arroz com ovas de peixe y un cherne recién pescado en el restaurante Camelo, en Apúlia, algo así como el templo gastronómico de la zona, aunque también podemos decantarnos por lugares más populares como Rita Fangueira —donde se recomienda pedir los filetes de pulpo rebozados con arroz de pulpo, un plato sumamente sexi— y, para los muy golosos, la pastelería Marbela de Esposende, donde conviene probar los folhadinhos.

El pinar de Ofir, que se extiende ante el hotel Axis Ofir —una obra de Alfredo Magalhães—, además de brindar las mejores sombras, ofrece una lección de arquitectura. Entre los árboles se esconden algunas de las casas que cambiaron la manera de construir en Portugal, porque este pinar entre el Atlántico y el Cávado, alejado de contaminación acústica y visual y que desemboca en las dunas que preceden al poder narcótico del mar, se convirtió, durante los años cincuenta y sesenta, en un auténtico laboratorio de la arquitectura portuguesa moderna. Al ser un lugar privilegiado para construir segundas residencias, permitió a arquitectos como Fernando Távora, Viana de Lima, Lixa Filgueiras o Alcino Soutinho experimentar con una nueva manera de habitar el territorio, mucho más respetuosa con la topografía, la vegetación y el clima.

Veamos, por ejemplo, la Casa del Dr. Fernando Ribeiro da Silva, de 1956, conocida simplemente como Casa de Ofir, una de las obras fundamentales de Fernando Távora y, probablemente, la que mejor explica el nacimiento de la arquitectura portuguesa contemporánea. No es una vivienda más dentro de su producción: es un manifiesto. Muy contenida, rotunda en su aparente sencillez, no pretende imponerse al paisaje. Távora la concibió como un composto, una arquitectura nacida del encuentro entre el bosque, el océano, la tradición constructiva portuguesa y las necesidades de su propietario. Para él, un edificio debía ser el resultado de muchos factores que actúan conjuntamente: el lugar, el paisaje, la cultura, el cliente, el programa, la técnica, la tradición, la experiencia del arquitecto...

Calle en la pequeña localidad portuguesa de Esposende. Jun Zhang ( GETTY IMAGES )

Hasta mediados de los años cincuenta, la arquitectura portuguesa parecía debatirse entre el racionalismo internacional y el regionalismo autóctono promovido por el Estado Novo. Távora propone una tercera vía. No copia la arquitectura popular, pero tampoco ignora el lugar. Integra la topografía, el pinar, el clima, la tradición constructiva y los nuevos materiales en una síntesis extraordinariamente natural. Así empezó a tomar forma una manera de construir que acabaría definiendo la Escuela de Oporto y marcaría a arquitectos como Álvaro Siza o Eduardo Souto de Moura.

La Casa de Ofir parece haber estado siempre aquí. Sobre ella, Siza escribió unas líneas preciosas en 1987 refiriéndose a la chimenea, que se ha convertido en el elemento más emblemático de la vivienda: “No es más que otra chimenea entre las luminosas y esenciales construcciones del litoral minhoto; provoca, en esa naturalidad, una auténtica sorpresa renovadora; en esa época, poca gente era sensible a la utilización de una estructura espacial moderna y nórdica”. No resulta difícil adivinar por qué Siza admiraba esta casa. En la disposición quebrada de las cubiertas y en la forma de acomodarse entre los pinos ya aparecen algunas de las preocupaciones que unos años después desarrollarían obras como la Casa de Chá da Boa Nova, un proyecto que, dicho sea de paso, empezó Távora, quien acabó cediéndoselo.

La Casa del Dr. Fernando Ribeiro da Silva, conocida simplemente como Casa de Ofir, es una de las obras fundamentales de Fernando Távora en Esposende. u. lahoz

Estamos cerca de la casa privada de João Pinto de Sousa, un hombre excepcional que conocía y admiraba al arquitecto Alcino Soutinho, al que encargó una casa superlativa en la que lleva viviendo, él solo y con sus perros, más de 20 años, porque le resulta imposible abandonarla. No hay que ser un genio para entenderlo. Considerado por la crítica como un arquitecto de la Escuela de Oporto, Soutinho obtuvo el Premio AICA —Asociación Internacional de Críticos de Arte— en 1984 y el Premio Europa Nostra —Federación Internacional para la Protección del Patrimonio Cultural y Natural de Europa— en 1982. También participó en importantes proyectos arquitectónicos a escala nacional, como el Ayuntamiento de Matosinhos —inaugurado en 1987 y considerado una obra fundamental de la arquitectura contemporánea portuguesa, por ser el primer edificio institucional construido después de la Revolución Democrática del 25 de Abril de 1974—.

Fachada de la casa privada de João Pinto de Sousa, una obra diseñada por el arquitecto portugués Alcino Soutinho en 1984.

Esta casa se reconoce por su color rosa desvaído —cómo no acordarse de Barragán—. Un lenguaje expresivo con reminiscencias de arquitectura palladiana. El dueño nos guía por el interior resaltando la presencia de pilares de mármol independientes de la estructura. Para definir la experiencia de habitar aquí repite varias veces la palabra “tranquilidad”. Dice que es una casa que inspira tanto al contemplarla como al vivirla. Y, al constatar el buen estado de su forma y de su humor, no nos extraña lo más mínimo. Cualquiera con dos dedos de frente y mucho dinero para vivir de rentas se atrincheraba en este refugio con ventanas circulares en las habitaciones que, si se cierran a medias, adquieren la forma de la luna en todas sus menguantes.

Otro de los platos fuertes de esta ruta es el vecino Hotel Parque do Rio, del arquitecto Júlio Oliveira. Es una obra maestra que visitamos con la nieta del arquitecto, Anna, quien, junto a su hermano, regenta este alojamiento de inspiración Bauhaus, con ecos de racionalismo italiano, que se hizo más o menos famoso al servir de escenografía de las películas Viver Mal y Mal Viver, del director João Canijo, premiadas en Cannes.

Primero vino la piscina, una obra extraordinaria por sus formas orgánicas; luego vino el hotel, concebido como una “obra de vida” por el arquitecto. El mobiliario del comedor, de Daciano Costa, y las lámparas de Tom Dixon aportan una elegancia que realza el espacio. Atención al “espatulado” tan orgánico de las paredes de la sala de estar y a la madera de pino de las escaleras. Pernoctar aquí es entender que la buena arquitectura y el buen diseño mejoran la vida.

Como nota a pie de página, conviene recordar que una parte de la película Una quinta portuguesa (2025), con Manolo Solo como protagonista, que tan buena acogida ha tenido este año, se rodó en Esposende, concretamente en su estuario y en el Hotel Suave Mar. Una institución para este rincón de Portugal en el que la masificación es ciencia ficción.

World.title: Opposition urge cabinet to pick a route as budget debate begins
World.content:
The left-wing opposition party Pro is willing to talk to the coalition parties about reducing healthcare costs, but only if the cabinet abandons its €6.5 billion cuts to welfare spending, party leader Jesse Klaver said on the first day of the Dutch budget debate.

Klaver said it would be a “scandal” if the government fell over its first budget, but he also pressed Rob Jetten’s administration to make up its mind whether to seek support from left or right.

As the first speaker in the two-day debate on finance minister Eelco Heinen’s budget, Klaver said his party wanted to break the deadlock that led to pre-budget talks breaking down.

“After so much political unrest in recent years, I think it is in all our interests that this cabinet succeeds,” he said. “Sometimes I think the opposition is keener to make it a success than the coalition parties themselves.”

Jan Paternotte, leader of the largest coalition party D66, called on parties on all sides to work on a budget with broad appeal and look beyond “the left-right discussion in The Hague”.

But his words found little support from the opposition, which accused the coalition of D66, CDA and VVD of lacking leadership. “What kind of road map does the cabinet see before it?” Mirjam Bikker, leader of the ChristenUnie, asked.

The three parties have 66 seats in the lower house, 10 short of a majority, while in the Senate they need to find 16 extra votes to pass their legislation.

No perfect match

Pro, with 20 seats in the lower house and 14 senators, provides the most straightforward route, but the right-wing VVD is reluctant to make too many concessions to the left and favours a deal with parties such as JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP.

Paternotte said the coalition wanted to continue talking to parties on all sides in the coming weeks. “The perfect political match doesn’t exist, only the will to come to an agreement. My invitation stands.”

Klaver himself came in for criticism from other opposition leaders who said the proposed budget deal had already made too many concessions to the left.

Joost Eerdmans, leader of the hardline conservative JA21, said the cabinet needed to “make the choice” between his party and Pro rather than trying to reach out to both.

In contrast to Pro, JA21 argues the cabinet should cut even more from the welfare bill to create room in the budget for tax cuts and measures to ease the cost of living.

Eerdmans also said plans to invest billions in climate change measures should be redirected to help working families. “The idea that we can change the world’s climate is unrealistic,” he said.

Two budgets

Eerdmans suggested to Paternotte that the cabinet should write two budgets, one for the left-wing parties and one for the right, and let MPs debate them both.

But Paternotte urged Eerdmans to “take off the rose-tinted glasses”. “How does that get you to a majority in the Senate?” he said. “Pro or JA21 on their own aren’t enough.”

Klaver’s pitch to the cabinet also prompted Socialist Party leader Jimmy Dijk to ask how far Pro was willing to compromise on healthcare spending.

Pro would not “work to break things down”, Klaver replied, but he saw potential to make savings by tackling “all kinds of treatments that aren’t necessary” and “taking the market out of youth care”.

Draft published

Paternotte also said D66 was willing to discuss surrogate parenthood with the SGP, which wants the cabinet to block any moves to legalise the practice as a condition for its support.

MPs also voted to ask the cabinet to publish the original draft budget by finance minister Eelco Heinen which was rejected by his coalition partners, prompting an extra weekend of negotiations.

NRC reported that the original version preserved most of the plans to cut welfare spending, despite Pro pressing for them to be taken off the table. In both the draft and the final version Heinen proposed delaying around half the cuts by a year.

World.title: Unpublished princess Diana memorial books stolen in NL
World.content:
Copies of an unpublished book about Diana, princess of Wales, written by her brother Earl Spencer, have been stolen from a truck in the Netherlands.

Four copies of the book, which was en route from a printing plant to a warehouse, were taken while the truck driver was sleeping in his cab in a car park, according to the BBC. Dutch publisher Overamstel has the rights to the book in the Netherlands.

The book, titled Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is highly anticipated as it is said to contain details about her personal life and unhappy marriage to then prince Charles, now the king. It also describes the crisis in the royal family that followed her death.

A source told British paper the Daily Mail that the theft was highly suspicious. “Nothing like this has ever happened before. This is probably the biggest book of the year and the security surrounding it has been incredibly tight.”

“Every possible precaution has been taken to prevent it from being leaked ahead of its serialisation. Therefore this unprecedented incident is being taken extremely seriously.”

The Dutch police are reportedly investigating the theft.

World.title: Seven men arrested as police step up illegal fireworks crackdown
World.content:
Seven men have been arrested after police intercepted several consignments of illegal fireworks from Germany over the weekend.

The suspects, aged between 31 and 60, were stopped while transporting 2,600kg of explosives to Arnhem, Heijen and Urk on Saturday.

Police said the fireworks were in the most restricted category, F4, intended for professional use only, which were already illegal before a wider ban on importing and possessing fireworks came into force on August 1.

Only the lightest category, which includes sparklers and Roman candles, will be allowed from this year, following years of campaigning by doctors and emergency services.

Police have said they will adopt a zero tolerance approach to illegal explosives in the run-up to New Year, including monitoring border crossings and checking vehicles that have been used in the past to import fireworks.

Last month a 22-year-old man from Oss was arrested after police seized a consignment of 1,200kg of fireworks in Schaijk, Noord-Brabant, one of the first major hauls since the ban took effect.

World.title: Kosovo ex-president Thaci jailed for 25 years by Hague court
World.content:
Former Kosovo president Hashim Thaci has been sentenced to 25 years in prison by a court in The Hague for war crimes committed during the 1998–99 war with Serbia, prompting clashes between his supporters and riot police in the city.

The court is an EU-backed tribunal operating under Kosovan law, and found Thaci (58) guilty of the murder of 96 people, the arbitrary detention of at least 385, and for torturing at least 303 and cruel treatment of at least 49.

The victims were largely political opponents and civilians regarded as collaborators by the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), the ethnic Albanian guerrilla movement he led.

Three other former KLA commanders were also convicted today – Jakup Krasniqi was sentenced to 25 years, Kadri Veseli to 18 and Rexhep Selimi to 13.

All four were cleared of six counts of crimes against humanity, with judges saying prosecutors had not shown the crimes were part of a widespread and systematic attack on civilians.

Prosecutors had asked for 45-year sentences. All four men denied the charges and both sides can appeal.

Clashes on the Malieveld

Dozens of Thaci supporters had gathered on the Malieveld ahead of the verdict, and the protest turned violent shortly after it was read out.

Demonstrators threw stones, branches and flagpoles at police vans and officers, and several climbed onto a police vehicle, news agency ANP reported. Riot police used tear gas and a water cannon to disperse the crowd.

Thaci served as Kosovo’s prime minister and then president between 2008 and 2020, and helped set up the court while foreign minister in 2015.

He resigned in November 2020 to face the charges and has been in custody since. Tens of thousands of people rallied in Pristina in the days before the verdict, where the four men are widely seen as national heroes. Thaci faces a separate trial on witness intimidation charges later this month.

World.content:

A court has ordered 14 people who were arrested in the aftermath of a shooting in a village near Arnhem to be kept in custody for another 90 days while inquiries continue.

Police arrested 35 people after a group of armed men descended on Overasselt in the early hours of September 1 and opened fire on a farmhouse, killing a 51-year-old guard and seriously injuring two police officers.

The suspects, who had various nationalities including French, Belgian and Algerian, were caught hiding in fields or as they tried to flee by car or train.

Military police later recovered weapons that had been abandoned at the scene, including one location near a primary school.

More suspects are due to appear in court on Wednesday and Thursday, when a judge will be asked to extend their detention. The group is accused of murder or attempted murder of the guard and attempted murder of the police officers.

It is suspected the attack was part of a feud over cocaine dealing linked with the man living in the farmhouse, Jan G., who has been targeted in the past.

Local mayor Joerie Minses has ordered G. to stay out of the village for the next three months.

World.title: Five reasons you might unexpectedly need a temporary Dutch home
World.content:
A new job, a burst pipe, a divorce, a renovation gone on too long: there are more moments than you’d imagine when you might suddenly need somewhere to live. Here’s how serviced and flexible housing can step in, whatever the reason.

1. The new job or the temporary assignment

Relocating for work is the classic reason many people need a home in the Netherlands, but it’s far from the only version of it. Travelling nurses posted to a new hospital, researchers starting a fellowship, or consultants sent in for a few months on a project all arrive in the same position: they need somewhere to live, quickly, without signing up for a permanent rental contract.

Corporate Housing Factory (CHF) provides fully serviced apartments across the Netherlands – offering comfortable, home-style living for stays from one week up to a year, combining the convenience of a hotel with the privacy and space of a residence.

You request a quote, the team confirms availability, and in some cases you can get the keys as soon as the next day. Apartments come fully furnished, from kitchen appliances to Wi-Fi, with cleaning included. Companies are invoiced directly, and the booking system is connected to the Global Distribution System (GDS), so travel management companies can book on a client’s behalf just as easily as they could book a hotel.

CHF’s newest property, in Arnhem, is a case in point. The building dates back to 1878 and survived the bombing of the Second World War – one apartment still has a shrapnel hole, deliberately unfilled. It’s since been transformed into an industrial-chic block with high ceilings and top-quality furniture, right by Arnhem Centraal station and a local supermarket. The location was chosen for the wider Nijmegen-Arnhem-Wageningen region, where technology, healthcare, sustainability and logistics employers have long struggled to find decent corporate housing for their staff.

2. The housing emergency

Then there’s the reason nobody plans for: a fire, a mould problem, a burst pipe or damage that suddenly makes your own home unliveable. It’s the kind of situation that can leave the victim feeling like an emergency bunker is the only option. And after an already stressful event, most people would rather not compromise on comfort.

This is where Thuis in de Stad comes in: “Until recently, we focused on corporate clients, so it was always relocations, work trips or internships,” says Claudia Vrancken from CHF. “With Thuis in de Stad, we’re opening the spectrum more broadly to the other unexpected reasons someone might suddenly need temporary housing.” You can anticipate fully furnished apartments, all utilities included; arrive with a suitcase and the rest is taken care of.

3. The renovation project, or getting caught between selling and buying

The same goes for two other reasons someone might need to move out temporarily: a renovation that makes the house unliveable for a few weeks, or the gap between selling one home and getting the keys to the next. Neither is an emergency, but both mean needing a comfortable base at short notice, for an unpredictable length of time.

One detail that matters more than people expect in the Netherlands is the ability to register at an address – something most short-term rentals don’t allow, but which is essential for things like getting a BSN number or opening a bank account. (Just don’t forget to deregister when you leave!)

4. The divorce process

Separation is another situation that can leave someone needing a home almost overnight – often with the condition of staying close to children and family during a period of transition. Flexible, furnished housing means not having to make a long-term commitment while things are still being worked out, while still having a proper place to call home in the meantime.

It’s also worth knowing, whatever the reason for the move, that pets are welcome – unlike with most hotels or holiday rentals. “Our apartments are all located in mixed-use buildings, so you really have the feeling you’re living somewhere with local families, kids and pets, instead of in a hotel,” says Claudia.

5. The sudden business trip elsewhere in Europe

Not every unexpected need for a home happens in the Netherlands. A consultant might have to jump on a plane at short notice for a project in another European city, with everything needing to be arranged just as quickly as it would be here.

For that, there’s Your Serviced Apartment Agency (YOSAA): a boutique Europe-wide apartments platform. The general idea of YOSAA – connecting living, hospitality and real estate – is the same as CHF and Thuis in de Stad: the convenience of a hotel with the freedom and flexibility of your own apartment.

Whatever the reason – a new job, an emergency or a sudden change of plans – temporary housing isn’t just for expats. Sometimes life itself creates the need for a home between homes. If that sounds like you, contact the booking team via email at bookings@corporatehousingfactory.com to find the right temporary home for your situation.

World.title: Eindhoven chip firm Euclyd raises €200m
World.content:
Eindhoven start-up Euclyd has raised more than €200 million to develop AI chips, and former ASML boss Peter Wennink has become chairman of the board, the company said on Tuesday.

The company is designing chips for what the industry calls inference, which is when an AI model is being used rather than trained. Most of that work is currently done on US-owned Nvidia processors. Euclyd says its chips will use less power and cost less.

Wennink was chief executive of ASML in Veldhoven from 2013 until 2024. In the statement he said Europe has “world-class capabilities across semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and systems engineering” and that Euclyd could build these into “a globally competitive AI infrastructure platform”.

Kastrup said in the same statement that the money would go on hiring engineers and speeding up development. “AI is becoming a foundation of economic growth, scientific discovery, and national competitiveness,” he said, “but its potential will remain constrained unless we fundamentally change the infrastructure beneath it.”

World.title: Scrap of 1700-year-old copy of The Odyssey washes up in Utrecht
World.content:
A 1700-year-old scrap of parchment containing verses from the Odyssey has been discovered in the library of Utrecht University.

Researcher Mark de Kreij came across the fragile artefact two years ago while he was going through a collection of manuscripts that belonged to a German scientist.

The torn fragment measures just 6.6cm by 7.7cm, roughly the size of a playing card, and contains a handful of verses from book 12 of Homer’s epic work.

It describes the moment when Odysseus’s men kill and eat the sacred cattle of the sun god Helios, ignoring their leader’s warnings, which prompts Zeus to send a storm to destroy Odysseus’s fleet and kill his army.

De Kreij said the fragment had lain undetected in the library for years until he came across it while examining a collection of Coptic manuscripts that the university bought from a relative of the German academic Carl Schmidt.

The text, in ancient Greek, was nestled among a batch of Coptic papyri, Egyptian texts written in the Greek alphabet. It is thought to have been taken from a pocketbook edition produced in Egypt in the third or fourth century AD.

The university decided to publicise the discovery in the wake of the box-office success of Christopher Nolan’s recent screen adaptation, which has revived interest in The Odyssey and boosted sales of English and Dutch translations.

De Kreij, a lecturer in Ancient Greek, immediately recognised the verses when he came across the parchment. “Everbody who learns Greek learns Homer,” he told RTV Utrecht.

Enduring epic

Only a handful of fragments of copies of The Odyssey have survived from the period, but the discovery shows how the epic tale has endured and been passed down for millennia.

De Kreij said the fragment had probably survived because it comes from the midpoint of the book and so would have been protected by the outer pages.

“The strange thing about my job is that The Odyssey is about the least exciting thing you can find,” he said. “There are lots of boring passages in The Odyssey. But this is a great part.”

World.title: European Parliament strips Polish far-right leader of immunity to face Holocaust denial charge

The European Parliament has again stripped Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of legal immunity to face charges in his homeland of denying Nazi crimes, an offence that carries a potential prison sentence of up to three years. The decision marks the sixth time that the European Parliament has lifted Braun’s immunity, and the second time for charges of Holocaust denial. Braun is already on trial in Poland for an attack on a Jewish religious celebration in parliament and is facing a number of other legal cases. Parlament Europejski w głosowaniu w Strasburgu uchylił immunitet europosła Grzegorza Brauna. Sprawa dotyczy negowania przez niego Holokaustu. Więcej: https://t.co/rB3UPUiS8o pic.twitter.com/icRLEqsWmF — Gazeta.pl (@gazetapl_news) September 15, 2026 In a vote on Tuesday, a majority of MEPs voted in favour of a request, submitted in February by Poland’s justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, to lift the immunity enjoyed by Braun as an MEP. He has sat in the European Parliament since being elected in 2024. In his request, Żurek said that Polish prosecutors wish to charge Braun in relation to “denial of genocide crimes committed by functionaries of the Third Reich in the Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp and the Lublin concentration camp (Majdanek)”. Poland’s Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that has prosecutorial power, also revealed that the accusation relates to the use of gas chambers at those two camps. Neither the IPN nor Żurek confirmed at the time what specific words Braun had said that prompted the planned charges against him. However, the IPN noted that they had come at a live event broadcast online on 27 September 2025. On that date, Braun took part in a discussion with Jan Żaryn, a right-wing historian and former senator for the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, titled “The Polish Underground State and the Jewish Issue”. A recording of the event is still available online. During his remarks, Braun referred to the “fake gas chambers of Majdanek and Auschwitz”, calling them “a dark, monstrous fantasy that has no satisfactory historical or academic support”. He suggested that the idea of the gas chambers had been invented as part of “propaganda and black PR operations conducted by the Soviet and Anglo-Saxon security services during World War Two”, and that the false claim continues to be exploited by Jews today. The European Parliament has again voted to strip Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face further charges for Holocaust denial as well as various antisemitic, anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT incidents during last year's presidential campaign https://t.co/4EHVEuSDnM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 26, 2026 In actual fact, historians estimate that around 900,000 people were killed in the gas chambers at Auschwitz. The vast majority were Jews, but victims also included Roma, Soviet prisoners of war, and ethnic Poles. Meanwhile, gas chambers at Majdanek were used to kill tens of thousands, again mainly Jews. Today, the ashes of the camp’s cremated victims are preserved in a memorial at the site of the former camp. Braun, who has a long history of promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories, has repeatedly sought to cast doubt on the veracity of Nazi crimes against Jews. Last month, he was charged with denying Nazi crimes in a separate case over earlier comments in which he called Auschwitz’s gas chambers “fake”. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has been charged with denying Nazi crimes, a criminal offence in Poland that carries a prison sentence of up to three years, for statements he made suggesting that the gas chambers at Auschwitz are "fake" https://t.co/PCssZt5eXD — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 25, 2026 In December, Braun went on trial over a separate set of charges relating to four other incidents, including his attack on a celebration of the Jewish festival of Hanukkah in parliament in December 2023 and his disruption of a lecture by a Holocaust scholar. “I am standing before this court because I dared to defend myself against oppression and the ritual manifestation of Jewish supremacy,” declared Braun at the start of the trial, which remains ongoing. Braun is also facing various legal cases relating to his anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT actions. Last week, he posted a video of himself using a hammer to vandalise a monument in Poland dedicated to the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). Police are investigating that incident. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has published a video of himself using a hammer to attack a monument in Poland to soldiers from the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, a WWII group that fought against the Soviets but was also responsible for massacring Poles https://t.co/oCYRtNRO9N — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 11, 2026 Braun’s high-profile stunts have seen his popularity surge among a section of the electorate. He finished a surprise fourth in last year’s Polish presidential election, with over 6% of the vote, and his Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party is now polling around 8-9%. If it manages to secure that level of support at next year’s parliamentary elections, KKP could become a key player in deciding what kind of government can be formed after what looks likely to be a very close contest between the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, and the right-wing and far-right opposition. An MEP from the ruling coalition, Michał Kobosko, welcomed Tuesday’s decision to lift Braun’s immunity, saying that the far-right leader “deliberately and consciously…stokes hatred. Kobosko said that such actions are particularly dangerous at a time when Russia is “actively waging hybrid and cognitive war against Poland”. He noted that Braun and his party have taken a sympathetic position towards Russia, including calling for Poland to “normalise” relations with Moscow. We cannot do what we do without your support. China overtook Germany to become Poland’s biggest source of imports for the first time in July, according to new data from the central bank. It ends a period of around 35 years in which Germany had consistently held top spot. The shift came as imports of Chinese goods surged, driven in part by a sharp increase in Chinese cars, while imports from Germany declined. “In July 2026, China was the largest supplier of goods to Poland for the first time, overtaking Germany in that month,” wrote the National Bank of Poland (NBP) in an announcement on Monday. “A significant increase in imports of computer hardware, passenger cars and durable consumer goods influenced the shift in the geographical structure of imports,” added the bank. Znamy już pełne dane handlowe za lipiec 2026 – za miesiąc kiedy Chiny po raz pierwszy w historii stały się największym dostawcą towarów do Polski, przed Niemcami. W lipcu import ogółem z Chin wzrósł o 28,8% r/r, podczas gdy z Niemiec spadł o 1,8% r/r. Import pojazdów… pic.twitter.com/LfJ50nXzNM — PKO Research (@PKO_Research) September 15, 2026 In a comment on the new data, analysts at PKO, a Polish bank, said that the July shift was partly due to “one-time factors” and noted that Germany remains Poland’s largest supplier on a 12-month basis, although its lead has been steadily shrinking. In July, Polish imports from China rose 28.8% year-on-year, while imports from Germany fell 1.8%, according to PKO. Imports of motor vehicles from Germany fell 9.3% year-on-year, while imports from China rose 54.4%. Imports from China of computers, electronics and optical equipment rose 31.5% year-on-year in July, the strongest increase since 2022. More detailed data on trade with the two countries, published also on Tuesday by Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, provided further insight into the shift. According to GUS, Poland imported goods worth €36.7 billion from China in the first seven months of the year, giving China a 15.9% share of total Polish imports, up from 14.9% in the same period of 2025. Imports from Germany stood at €43.1 billion in that period, 18.6% of the total, down from 19.4% in 2025. Poland’s third-largest source of imports was the United States, with €12.7 worth of goods, a share of 5.5%, up from 4.9% in 2025. Poland has been NATO's biggest importer of arms over the last five years, according to new data from @SIPRIorg. Over 90% of Polish imports have come from South Korea and the United States https://t.co/jij0nfbhFc — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 9, 2026 Germany has been Poland’s largest trading partner since the collapse of communism, leading both in imports and exports. It overtook the Soviet Union, which had dominated Poland’s foreign trade during the communist era. But China has steadily gained ground as a source of Polish imports since the 2010s, rising to second place behind Germany by the 2020s. In terms of exports in the first seven months of this year, Germany dominates, receiving goods worth €69.8 billion, or 26.3% of all Poland’s exports. It is followed by the Czech Republic (€14.3 billion), France (€14.0 billion), the United Kingdom (€11.6 billion) and the Netherlands (€10.9 billion). Prime Minister Donald Tusk says that Poland has been “disgraced in front of the entire world” by a new Financial Times report on how Polish state energy firm Orlen lost $230 million (856 million zloty) trying to buy Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, unsecured payments and cryptocurrency transfers. Tusk called the case a further example of “dirty deals” conducted under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was in power at the time. Orlen was then led by Daniel Obajtek, who is now a member of the European Parliament representing PiS. Obajtek himself today said that he wants the issue to be clarified in court and suggested that the current authorities are using the case to distract from current soaring fuel prices. How Poland lost $230mn trying to buy Venezuelan oil with crypto https://t.co/Xo07JkYy1t — Financial Times (@FT) September 15, 2026 In a report today, the FT provided new details on a case that has already drawn public attention in Poland. In April 2024, Orlen revealed that its Swiss oil trading subsidiary had lost around $400 million in prepayments for Venezuelan oil and petroleum products that were never delivered. Orlen, which was under new management after Obajtek had been fired earlier that year following the arrival of Tusk’s government, said that the losses included around $240 million paid to a Dubai-based intermediary run by a 25-year-old from Hong Kong. A week later, Polish prosecutors announced that they had launched an investigation into the case, focusing on Orlen Trading Switzerland (OTS), the subsidiary that oversaw the Venezuela deal. Polish prosecutors have launched an investigation into OTS, @GrupaORLEN's Swiss subsidiary which had lost $400 million on prepayments for oil that was never delivered. It also announced that the homes of Orlen's former senior management had been searchedhttps://t.co/QQ5QJMsHg4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 1, 2024 The FT detailed how the then head of OTS, a Lebanese-born Polish citizen of Palestinian descent, who can be named only as Samer A. under Polish privacy law, had sought in 2023 to commission the import of Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, who were given a $230 million advance without any security or guarantees. Although the United States, under then-President Joe Biden, had temporarily suspended sanctions on Venezuelan oil, allowing companies such as Orlen to buy it, Venezuela’s state oil company, PDVSA, remained largely cut off from the global financial system. The FT detailed how the intermediaries therefore sought to use cryptocurrency to facilitate the deal. However, although oil tankers leased by Orlen to collect the oil sat waiting (accruing further large costs), the promised oil was not delivered, and Orlen’s advance payments were lost. The issue is now the subject of a criminal investigation in Poland and an ongoing arbitration case with the intermediary in Dubai, Hannon International. Speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said that the FT story is a “disgrace in front of the entire world”. He called the Venezuelan oil incident “the biggest scandal, or one of the biggest scandals, in our country’s history”. World.title: “Don’t be a creep”: Polish ice cream company launches campaign against sexual harassment of staff
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish ice cream chain has launched a campaign to stamp out sexual harassment of staff by customers, including empowering employees to refuse to serve such clients. The campaign is based around the fact that the Polish word for ice cream, “lody”, also has an informal vulgar meaning, referring to oral sex. The company, Good Lood, which runs 37 outlets, says that its female staff regularly suffer lewd comments from male customers incorporating this double entendre. In response, in late August it launched a campaign titled “Nie bądź oblechem”, meaning “Don’t be a creep”, with information displayed prominently at its ice cream stands and on its social media platforms. The firm said it condemned “crude remarks, inappropriate jokes and verbal harassment directed at service workers” and promised to support its staff in dealing with them. “Everyone deserves respect, without exception!” Good Lood advised employees to respond to inappropriate comments with a short, firm retort such as “Great, that’s the 20th time I’ve heard that” or “Perhaps you could repeat that more loudly, so the rest of the queue can hear?” It also called on other customers to react if they witnessed such behaviour. In a follow-up social media post last week, the company confirmed that staff had its backing if they decided not to serve a customer. “If someone is a creep and makes inappropriate comments and verbally harasses them, our team have the right to refuse them service.” That post alone has so far garnered more than 50,000 likes or other positive responses on Facebook. Good Lood says that its messages posted as part of the campaign have already received over 10 million organic views on social media. Comments on the company’s posts show overwhelming support, with many commenters sharing their own experiences. “At last someone has spoken out about this!” wrote one, who said she worked in an ice cream parlour as a teenager. “I remember how outraged I felt when I heard comments like that from men who could have been my fathers, or even my grandfathers. I wonder what would happen if someone spoke to their daughters or granddaughters like that.” Good Lood says it want to start a broader conversation on the “global issue” of harassment and disrespect towards front-line staff in retail and hospitality. “Working in service or hospitality does not mean consenting to disrespect. The safety and wellbeing of our team will always come before profit. We are not afraid to lose a customer who cannot show basic human respect,” the company said in a press release. Founded 10 years ago in Kraków, Good Lood now has 37 outlets there as well as in the Warsaw area. It also sells its products throughout Poland at Biedronka, the country’s largest supermarket chain. A moose wandered onto the tracks at Warsaw Central Station on Sunday evening, disrupting rail services in the Polish capital for more than 80 minutes before it was safely removed. The animal first appeared on a platform before moving onto the tracks, forcing Polish Railway Lines (PLK), the company responsible for Poland’s rail infrastructure, to suspend, cancel and divert several train services. View this post on Instagram A post shared by TVP3 Warszawa (@tvp3warszawa) Videos and photographs shared online showed the moose lying on the tracks and running along the railway line at Warsaw Central, the capital’s busiest station, which is mainly underground and therefore not easy for such a large animal to access. Police do not know how the moose ended up at the station, reports broadcaster TVN24. Officers were first alerted at 7:10 pm on Sunday and cordoned off the platform where the animal was located. When emergency services arrived, the moose was tranquilised. It was then placed on a large sheet and carried out of the station by police officers and emergency workers before being loaded onto a specialist vehicle to be returned to a forested area. PLK, which named the moose Emil, later confirmed that the animal had been safely removed and that normal train services were being restored. The company added that the disruptions lasted just over 80 minutes, using a pun combining the Polish words for moose (łoś) and 80 (osiemdziesiąt) to produce the word “łosiemdziesiąt”. ❗Aktualizacja❗Zwierze zostało bezpiecznie zabrane z torów. Przywracana jest rozkładowa organizacja ruchu pociągów. Utrudnienia trwały przeszło łosiemdziesiąt minut. https://t.co/Xui2B6SxyU — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) September 13, 2026 The Eurasian moose (also known as the Eurasian elk) has long been native to Poland, but by the mid-20th century hunting and habitat loss had brought the species close to extinction in the country. Its population subsequently recovered, reaching an estimated 6,000 animals by the 1980s and around 30,000 by 2019, helped by a moratorium on moose hunting introduced in 2001. Several hundred live in the Kampinos national park on the northwestern outskirts of Warsaw. They are therefore relatively frequent visitors to the capital, according to the Interia news website, although venturing onto train lines in the centre is unusual. The growth in the moose population, combined with urban expansion and changes to its habitat, has led to other high-profile encounters in areas inhabited by humans. In 2022, a moose was spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in the northern Polish city of Elbląg. A moose was this morning spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in Poland. World.title: Poland issued EU’s third most residence permits to immigrants in 2025
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland issued first residence permits to almost half a million immigrants in 2025, which was the third-highest figure in the European Union, behind Spain and Germany but ahead of Italy and France. However, the number of permits issued by Poland fell for the fourth year running, as the country continued to tighten its migration rules. Previously, between 2017 and 2022, Poland had led the EU figures for six years running, reaching a peak of almost one million permits in 2021. The new data, released on Friday by Eurostat, the EU’s statistical agency, show that Poland issued 467,314 first residence permits to immigrants from outside the EU in 2025. As was the case last year, Spain (635,438) issued the most, followed by Germany (605,292). Poland was then followed by Italy (433,099) and France (377,462). However, whereas in those four other countries the number of permits rose in 2025 (by 13.1% in Spain, 11.1% in Germany, 25.0% in Italy and 9.2% in France), in Poland the figure fell by 4.4%. That decline has come amid a tougher new migration strategy by the current government, a coalition that ranges from left to centre right, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Ahead of elections in 2023, Tusk, then in opposition, accused the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which had ruled Poland since 2015, of allowing “uncontrolled” migration, including through widespread abuses of the visa system. Shortly after coming to power in those elections, Tusk, a former president of the European Council, declared that the “survival of Western civilisation” depends upon preventing mass migration. His government has since introduced tougher entry requirements for foreign workers and students, suspended asylum rights for migrants who irregularly cross the border from Belarus, and stepped up deportations of immigrants who have committed crimes or entered the country unlawfully. Poland has introduced tougher new rules regulating the entry of foreign students and immigrant workers. “This is another step towards regaining control over migration and increasing the safety of Poles," says the government https://t.co/gYdikpc6pL — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2025 The new 2025 data show that, in relative terms (the number of permits issued in relation to countries’ populations), Poland was only ninth in the EU (12.8 permits per 1,000 people), behind Malta (56.9), Cyprus (46.7), Portugal (27.3), Lithuania (18.5), Ireland (13.4), Croatia (13.2), Luxembourg (13.1) and Spain (12.9). That marks a significant decline since 2021, when Poland issued 967,345 permits, which was the highest in the EU in absolute terms but also second-highest in relation to population. In 2025, as in previous years, Poland issued the most first residence permits to Ukrainians (241,126, 51.6% of the total), who are by far the country’s largest immigrant group. They were followed by Belarusians (128,468, 27.5%), Georgians (10,249, 2.2%), Indians (9,230, 2%) and Turks (7,533, 1.6%) – the same top five nationalities as in 2024. Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians https://t.co/hNiOqmeUfX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2026 Following a decade of unprecedented mass migration, the number of foreigners with residence permits in Poland this year passed two million for the first time, making up just over 5% of the country’s population. Around 1.5 million of those are Ukrainians. In June, the number of foreigners working in Poland reached 1.14 million, making up almost 7% of the workforce. While Ukrainians constitute two thirds of the total, the fastest-growing nationalities are Colombians and Indians, who are now the third- and fourth-largest groups of foreign workers. The rise in migration has come as Poland’s economy has boomed but the country has also faced a demographic crisis, with a shrinking, ageing population and one of the lowest birth rates in the world. In 2023, the state Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) calculated that, in order to maintain its ratio of working-age population to retirees, Poland would need to attract almost two million immigrant workers over the following decade. However, it admitted that that target was “unrealistic”. World.title: Poznej Vltavu Festival Returns to Prague on September 28
World.content:
The second edition of the Poznej Vltavu (Get to Know the Vltava) festival will take place across Prague on September 28, 2026.

For one day, the banks of the Vltava will host a programme exploring the river from a variety of perspectives.

The festival will feature workshops, exhibitions, sports activities, boat trips, and tours of places that are not normally open to the public.



Prague’s riverfront embankments and other locations along the Vltava will offer activities for children, adults, and seniors.

The festival aims to highlight the Vltava as a natural part of Prague’s urban environment and an important ecological feature, while giving visitors the opportunity to spend a day exploring the river and its surroundings.

Experts from a range of fields will discuss the Vltava in its broader context and offer insights into lesser-known aspects of the river.

This year’s programme will involve organisations including the Prague Institute of Planning and Development, Prague City Tourism, the Prague City Gallery, the Vltava River Authority, Prague Waterworks and Sewerage Company, the Prague Water Management Company, ROPID, Prague City Forests, the Nature Conservation Agency of the Czech Republic, and many others.

The festival area will extend farther along the Vltava this year, reaching Žluté lázně and the new Dvorecký Bridge, which has quickly become a popular destination for Prague residents since opening.

Most events will be free to attend, although some activities will require advance registration due to limited capacity.

More information is available on the festival’s Facebook event.

World.title: Red Arrows to Fly Over Charles Bridge This Friday
World.content:
Prague will hear the roar of Royal Air Force jets on Friday, September 18, when the Red Arrows aerobatic team stages a flypast over the city.

Ten BAE Hawk T1 aircraft from the British RAF team are scheduled to pass over the Charles Bridge at around 2:00 PM. The jets will leave smoke trails in the colours of the Czech flag during the display.



The formation is expected to approach Prague from the north before reaching the area around Václav Havel Airport. The aircraft will then form an arrow-shaped formation and fly around the western and southern parts of the capital before turning north along the Vltava.

The jets are expected to fly at an altitude of roughly 300 metres above the ground. The engines will be clearly audible across parts of the city, although the flypast itself will last only a short time.

After passing through central Prague, the formation will turn northeast and continue toward Ostrava. The city is hosting NATO Days, one of the Czech Republic’s largest military and security events, this weekend.

The timetable and route could still change because of weather or other air traffic in the Prague area. A similar Red Arrows flypast was held in Prague last September, but poor weather delayed the aircraft by more than an hour.

The flypast is being held in connection with Czech Air Force Day, which is observed on September 15.

The Red Arrows are the official aerobatic display team of the Royal Air Force and regularly perform at air shows and military events in Britain and abroad.

World.title: Groovy Market Fest Returns to Riegrovy Sady on October 3
World.content:
Prague’s Groovy Market Fest will return to Riegrovy Sady on Saturday, October 3, bringing together food, independent brands, design and live music for its third edition.

The one-day event will take place at Energy Pub from noon until 10 p.m.

Following two editions held during the summer, the organizers are extending the concept into the autumn, with visitors able to browse local products, eat street food and listen to live music and DJs throughout the day.



The market is organised around three main areas. The Food Garden will focus on gastronomy and street food from local businesses, while Palm Street will feature bakeries, artisanal products and other local goods. The Design Zone will bring together fashion, design and products from independent Czech brands.

Live performances and DJ sets will run from the afternoon into the evening, providing the musical programme alongside the market stalls.

Marek Novák, founder of Groovy Market Fest, said the first two editions helped the team establish the format and identify what visitors respond to.

“After two editions, we know exactly what works at Groovy Market Fest: high-quality local brands, good food, and an atmosphere that keeps people coming back,” Novák said. “This third edition is an opportunity for us to show that Groovy isn’t just a summer event, but a festival that holds a firm place in Prague all year round.”

Visitors can buy tickets for either of the two five-hour sessions. The first runs from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m., followed by a second session from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m.

A ticket for one session costs 100 CZK, while an all-day ticket covering both sessions is available for 190 CZK. Tickets are sold through GoOut.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Groovy Market Fest (@groovymarketfest)

From Barcelona street food to a Prague market

Groovy Market Fest was founded by Marek Novák and Veronika Kracíková, a couple with experience in Prague’s food scene and Barcelona’s street-food sector.

One of their main inspirations was Barcelona’s Palo Alto Market, an urban market known for combining food, design, music and independent creative businesses.

World.title: Prague Run Day to Bring Six Races to Riegrovy Sady on September 19
World.content:
On September 19, runners of all levels can take part in a new running event combining track and park races in one of Prague’s best-known green spaces.

There are six different races to choose from, so whether you’re looking for a serious challenge or just want to get out and run, there’s an option for you.



Six races to choose from

The programme includes six races, ranging from a short family run to a one-hour challenge.

The day will begin with the 800m Family Run, designed for young runners and their accompanying adults. There will also be an 800m race on the athletic track, offering participants the opportunity to compete over a short distance in a traditional track setting.

For those looking for a longer challenge, the 1 Mile race will take place on the athletic oval. The organisers describe it as a special opportunity to race over the classic distance, with participation limited to a maximum of 30 runners.

The 5km Solo Run will offer a more familiar challenge for runners of different experience levels. It is followed by the 4x3km Relay, a team race in which four runners each complete two 1.5km laps.

The final event of the day will be the Golden Hour Race, a one-hour running challenge taking place during the golden hour.

The event will be based at the Sokol Vinohrady athletic oval, which will serve as the main hub for the day.
